John ii. 6.And there were there six vessels of stone, placed for the Jews’ purification, such as [28] [Arabic, p. 20] would contain two or three jars.
John ii. 7.And Jesus said unto them, Fill the vessels [29] with water. And they filled them to the top.
John ii. 8.He said unto them, Draw [30] out now, and present to the ruler of the feast. And they did so.
John ii. 9.And when the ruler of the company tasted that water which had become wine, and knew not whence it was (but the servants knew, because they filled up the water), the ruler of the company called [31] the bridegroom,
John ii. 10.and said unto him, Every man presenteth first the good wine, and on intoxication he bringeth what is poor; but thou hast kept the good wine until [32] now.
John ii. 11.And this is the first sign
Perhaps a comma should be inserted after sign. which Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and manifested [33] his glory; and his disciples believed on him.
Luke iv. 14b.And his fame spread in all the country [34] which was around them.
Luke iv. 15.And he taught in their synagogues, and was glorified [35] by
If the text does not contain a misprint the word for by is wanting in both mss. It should doubtless be restored as in § 7, 3. every man.
Luke iv. 16.And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and entered, according to his custom, into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood [36] up to read.
Luke iv. 17.And he was given the book of Isaiah the prophet. And Jesus opened the book and found the place where it was written,

[37]
Luke iv. 18.The Spirit of the Lord is upon me,
And for this anointed he me, to preach good tidings to the poor;
And he hath sent me to heal the broken-hearted,

And to proclaim forgiveness to the evil-doers,
Evil-doers could easily be an Arabic copyist’s corruption of captives; but the word used here for forgiveness could hardly spring from an Arabic release (in Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary, where the thing seems to have happened, a different word is used). In Syriac, however, they are the same; while the first pair contain the same consonants. and sight to the blind,

And to bring the broken into forgiveness,
See preceding note.

[38]
Luke iv. 19.And to proclaim an acceptable year of the Lord.

[39]
Luke iv. 20.And he rolled up the book and gave it to the servant, and went and sat down: [40] and the eyes of all that were in the synagogue were observing him.
Luke iv. 21.And he began to say unto them, To-day hath this scripture been fulfilled which ye have heard with [41] your ears.
Luke iv. 22a.And they all bare him witness, and wondered at the words of grace which were proceeding from his mouth.

[42] [Arabic, p. 21]
Matt. iv. 17a.And from that time began Jesus to proclaim the gospel of the kingdom [43] of God, and to say, Repent ye, and believe in the gospel.
Mark i. 15.The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of heaven hath come near.

[44]
Matt. iv. 18.And while he was walking on the shore of the sea of Galilee, he saw two brethren, Simon who was called Cephas, and Andrew his brother, casting their nets into [45] the sea; for they were fishers.
Matt. iv. 19.And Jesus said unto them, Follow me, and I will [46] make you fishers of men.
Matt. iv. 20.And they immediately left their nets there and followed [47] him.
Matt. iv. 21.And when he went on from thence, he saw other two brothers, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the ship with Zebedee their father, mending [48] their nets; and Jesus called them.
Matt. iv. 22.And they immediately forsook the ship and their father Zebedee, and followed him.

[49]
Luke v. 1.And when the multitude gathered unto him to hear the word of God, while he [50] was standing on the shore of the sea of Gennesaret,
Luke v. 2.he saw two boats standing beside the sea, while
Or, but. the two fishers which were gone out of them were washing their [51] nets.
Luke v. 3.And one of them belonged to Simon Cephas. And Jesus went up and sat down in it, and commanded that they should move away a little from the land into [52] the water. And he sat down and taught the multitudes from the boat.
Luke v. 4.And when he had left off his speaking, he said unto Simon, Put out into the deep, and cast your [53] net for a draught.
Luke v. 5.And Simon answered and said unto him, My Master, we toiled [54] all night and caught nothing; now
Borg. ms. has but. The Arabic expressions are very similar. at thy word I will cast the net.
Luke v. 6.And when they did this, there were enclosed
Borg. ms. has he did this, he enclosed, on which see § 38, 43, note (end). Either reading could spring from the other, within the Arabic. a great many fishes; and their net was on the [55] point of breaking.
Luke v. 7.And they beckoned to their comrades that were in the other boat, to come and help them. And when they came, they filled both boats, so that they were on the point of sinking.

div3.title: Section VI.
div3.p:
[1] [Arabic, p. 22]
Luke v. 8.But when Simon Cephas saw this he fell before the feet of Jesus, and said unto him, My Lord, I beseech of thee to depart from me, for I am [2] a sinful man.
Luke v. 9.And amazement took possession of him, and of all who were with him, [3] because of the draught of the fishes which they had taken.
Luke v. 10.And thus also were James and John the sons of Zebedee overtaken,
The verb may be active as well as passive, but does not agree in gender with amazement. Mistakes in gender are, however, very common transcriptional errors. who were Simon’s partners. And Jesus said [4] unto Simon, Fear not; henceforth thou shalt be a fisher of men unto life.
Luke v. 11.And they brought the boats to the land; and they left everything, and followed him.

[5]
John iii. 22.And after that came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judæa; and he went [6] about there with them, and baptized.
John iii. 23.And John also was baptizing in Ænon, which is beside Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized. [7, 8]
John iii. 24.And John was not yet come into prison.
John iii. 25.And there was an inquiry between [9] one of John’s disciples and one of the Jews about purifying.
John iii. 26.And they
Dual. came unto John, and said unto him, Our master, he that was with thee beyond Jordan, to whom [10] thou hast borne witness, behold, he also baptizeth, and many come to him.
John iii. 27.John answered and said unto them,
Plural. In the Peshitta it is two individuals in verse 25. In Sin. the first is an individual and the second is ambiguous. In Cur. both are plural. A man can receive nothing of himself, except it be [11] given him
Or, he be given it. from heaven.
John iii. 28.Ye are they that bear witness unto me that I said, I am [12] not the Messiah, but I am one sent
The ordinary word for apostle. before him.
John iii. 29.And he that hath a bride is a bridegroom: and the friend of the bridegroom is he that standeth and listeneth to him, and rejoiceth greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. Lo now,
See § 9, 21, note. behold, [13, 14] [Arabic, p. 23] my joy becometh complete.
So Ciasca’s printed text. The Vat. ms., however, probably represents a past tense.
John iii. 30.And he must increase and I decrease.
John iii. 31.For
cf. Peshitta. he that is come from above is higher than everything; and he that is of the earth, of the earth he is, and of the earth he speaketh; and he that came down from heaven is [15] higher than all.
John iii. 32.And he beareth witness of what he hath seen and heard: and no man [16] receiveth his witness.
John iii. 33.And he that hath received his witness hath asserted
cf. consonants of Syriac text. that he is [17] truly God.
Borg. ms., that God is truly, or, assuming a very common grammatical inaccuracy, that God is true or truth, the reading in Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary.
John iii. 34.And he whom God hath sent speaketh the words
Lit. saying. of God: God gave [18] not the Spirit by measure.
John iii. 35.The Father loveth the Son, and hath put everything in [19] his hands.
John iii. 36.Whosoever believeth in the Son hath eternal
Lit. the life of eternity; here and everywhere except § 21, 40. life; but whosoever obeyeth not the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God cometh
i.e., alighteth-and-stayeth. upon him.

[20]
John iv. 1.And Jesus learned
Or, knew. that the Pharisees had heard that he had received many disciples, [21] and that he was baptizing more than John
John iv. 2.(not that Jesus was himself baptizing, [22] but his disciples);
John iv. 3a.and so he left Judæa.

[23]
Luke iii. 19.And Herod the governor, because he used to be rebuked by John because of
Herodias the wife of Philip his brother, and for all the sins which he was committing, [24] added to all that also this,
Luke iii. 20.that he shut up John in prison.

[25]
Matt. iv. 12.And when Jesus heard that John was delivered up, he went away to Galilee. [26]
John iv. 46.And he entered again into Cana, where he had made the water wine. And there [27] was at Capernaum a king’s servant, whose son was sick.
John iv. 47.And this man heard that Jesus was come from Judæa to Galilee; and he went to him, and besought of him that he would come down and heal his son; for he had come near unto death. [28, 29]
John iv. 48.Jesus said unto him, Except ye see signs and wonders, ye do
Or, will. not believe.
John iv. 49.The [Arabic, p. 24] king’s servant said unto him, My Lord, come down, that the child die not. [30]
John iv. 50.Jesus said unto him, Go; for thy son is alive. And that man believed the [31] word which Jesus spake, and went.
John iv. 51.And when he went down, his servants met him [32] and told him, and
Or, good news, and. said unto him, Thy son is alive.
John iv. 52.And he asked them at what time he recovered. They said unto him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left [33] him.
John iv. 53.And his father knew that that was at that hour in which Jesus said unto him, [34] Thy son is alive.
John iv. 54.And he believed, he and the whole people of his house. And this [35] is the second sign
See § 5, 32, note. which Jesus did when he returned from Judæa to Galilee.
Luke iv. 44.And he was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.

[36]
Matt. iv. 13.And he left Nazareth, and came and dwelt in Capernaum by the sea shore, in the [37] borders of Zebulun and Naphtali:
Matt. iv. 14.that it might be fulfilled which was said in Isaiah the prophet, who said,

[38]
Matt. iv. 15.The land of Zebulun, the land of Naphtali,
The way of the sea, the passage of the Jordan,
Galilee of the nations:

[39]
Matt. iv. 16.The people sitting in darkness
Saw a great light,
And those sitting in the region and in the shadow of death,
There appeared to them a light.

[40]
Luke iv. 31b.And he taught them on the sabbaths.
Luke iv. 32.And they wondered because of his doctrine:
Perhaps we might here render learning; but see § 28, 17, note. [41] for his word was as if it were authoritative.
Luke iv. 33.And there was in the synagogue [42] a man with an unclean devil, and he cried out with a loud voice, and said,
Luke iv. 34.Let me alone; what have I to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come for our [43] destruction? I know thee who thou art, thou Holy One of God.
Luke iv. 35.And Jesus rebuked him, and said, Stop up thy mouth, and come out of him. And the demon threw him [44] in the midst and came out of him, having done him no harm.
Luke iv. 36.And great amazement [Arabic, p. 25] took hold upon every man. And they talked one with another, and said, What is this word that orders the unclean spirits with power and [45] authority, and they come out?
Luke iv. 37.And the news of him spread abroad in all the region which was around them.

[46]
Luke iv. 38.And when Jesus went out of the synagogue,
Matt. ix. 9b.he saw a man sitting among the publicans,
So in the Arabic. It is, however, simply a misinterpretation of the expression in the Syriac versions for at the place of toll (cf. Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary). named Matthew: and he said unto him, Come after me. And he rose, and followed him.

[47, 48]
Mark i. 29b.And Jesus came to the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John.
Luke iv. 38c.And Simon’s wife’s mother was oppressed with a great fever, and they besought him for [49] her.
Luke iv. 39.And he stood over her and rebuked her fever, and it left her, and immediately [50] she rose and ministered to them.
Matt. viii. 16a.And at even they brought to him many that had [51] demons: and he cast out their devils with the
cf. § 1, 40, note 2. word.
Luke iv. 40b.And all that had sick, their diseases being divers and malignant, brought them unto him. And he laid his hand [52] on them one by one
Or, each. and healed them:
Matt. viii. 17.that that might be fulfilled which was said [53] in the prophet Isaiah, who said, He taketh our pains and beareth our diseases.
Mark i. 33.And [54] all the city was gathered together unto the door of Jesus.
Luke iv. 41.And he cast out devils also from many, as they were crying out and saying, Thou art the Messiah, the Son of God; and he rebuked them. And he suffered not the demons to speak, because they knew him that he was the Lord the Messiah.

div3.title: Section VII.
div3.p:
[1] [Arabic, p. 26]
Mark i. 35.And in the morning of that day he went out very early, and went to a [2] desert place, and was there praying.
Mark i. 36.And Simon and those that were with [3] him sought him.
Mark i. 37.And when they found him, they said unto him, All the people seek for [4] thee.
Mark i. 38.He said unto them, Let us go into the adjacent villages and towns, that I may [5] preach there also; for to this end did I come.
Luke iv. 42.And the multitudes were seeking him, and came till they reached him; and they took hold of him, that he should not [6] go away from them.
Luke iv. 43.But Jesus said unto them, I must preach of the kingdom of [7] God in other cities also: for because of this gospel was I sent.
Matt. ix. 35.And Jesus was going about all the cities and the villages, and teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all the diseases and all the sicknesses, [8]
Mark i. 39.and casting out the devils.
Luke iv. 14b.And his fame became known
Luke iv. 15.that
This may represent a Syriac as. he was teaching in [9] every place and being glorified by every man.
Mark ii. 14.And when he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphæus sitting among the tax-gatherers;
See above, note to § 6, 46, which applies, although the Arabic words are different. and he said unto him, Follow [10] me: and he rose and followed him.
Matt. iv. 24.And the news of him was heard of in all the land of Syria: and they brought unto him all those whom grievous ills had befallen through divers diseases, and those that were enduring torment, and those that were possessed, and lunatics,
Lit. son-of-the-roofs, a Syriac expression (cf. § 24, 31, note). and paralytics; and he healed them.

[11, 12]
Mark ii. 1.And after some days Jesus entered into Capernaum again.
Mark ii. 2.And when they heard that he was in the house,
This is the end of verse 1 in the Greek. many gathered, so that it could not hold them, even about [13] [Arabic, p. 27] the door; and he made known to them the word of God.
Luke v. 17b.And there were there some of the Pharisees and the teachers of the law, sitting, come from all the villages of Galilee, and Judæa, and Jerusalem; and the power of the Lord was [14] present to heal them.
Luke v. 18.And some men brought a bed with a man on it who was paralytic. [15] And they sought to bring him in and lay him before him.
Luke v. 19.And when they found no way to bring him in because of the multitude of people, they went up to the roof, and let him down with his bed from the roofing,
This word may be either a singular or a plural. into the midst before Jesus. [16]
Luke v. 20.And when Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the paralytic, My son, thy sins are forgiven [17] thee.
Luke v. 21.And the scribes and Pharisees began to think within their hearts, Why doth this man blaspheme?
This word ordinarily means to forge lies against; but our translator uses it regularly as here. Who is it that is able to forgive sins, but God alone? [18]
Mark ii. 8.And Jesus knew by the spirit that they were thinking this within themselves, and he [19] said unto them, Why do ye think this within your heart?
Mark ii. 9.Which is better,
Peshitta has easier. that it should be said to the paralytic, Thy sins are forgiven thee, or that it should be said [20] to him, Arise, and take thy bed, and walk?
Mark ii. 10.That ye may know that the Son of man [21] is empowered on earth to forgive sins (and he said to the paralytic),
Mark ii. 11.I say unto thee, [22] Arise, take thy bed, and go to thine house.
Mark ii. 12a.And he rose forthwith, and took his bed, and went out in the presence of all.
Luke v. 25b.And he went to his house praising God. [23]
Matt. ix. 8a.And when those multitudes saw, they feared;
Luke v. 26a.and amazement took possession of [24] them,
Matt. ix. 8b.and they praised God, who had given such power to men.
Luke v. 26c.And they said, We have seen marvellous things to-day,
Mark ii. 12c.of which we have never before seen the like.

[25] [Arabic, p. 28]
Luke v. 27.And after that, Jesus went out, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting [26] among the publicans:
See above, note to § 6, 46. and he said unto him, Follow me.
Luke v. 28.And he left [27] everything, and rose, and followed him.
Luke v. 29.And Levi made him a great feast in his house. And there was a great multitude of the publicans and others sitting with him. [28]
Luke v. 30.And the scribes and Pharisees murmured, and said unto his disciples, Why do ye eat [29] and drink with the publicans and sinners?
Luke v. 31.Jesus answered and said unto them, The physician seeketh not those who are well, but those that are afflicted with grievous [30, 31] sickness.
A Syriacism.
Luke v. 32.I came not to call the righteous, but the sinners, to repentance.
Luke v. 33.And they said unto him, Why do the disciples of John fast always, and pray, and the [32] Pharisees also, but thy disciples eat and drink?
Luke v. 34.He said unto them, Ye cannot make [33] the sons of the marriage feast
The Arabic word, which occurs here in many of the Arabic versions, could also be read bridegroom. The Syriac word for marriage chamber is also used in the sense of marriage feast. fast, while the bridegroom is with them.
Luke v. 35.Days will
come, when the bridegroom is taken away from them; then will they fast in those [34] days.
Luke v. 36a.And he spake unto them a parable:
Mark ii. 21.No man inserteth a new patch and seweth it in a worn garment, lest the newness of the new take from the worn, and [35] there occur a great rent.
Mark ii. 22.And no man putteth fresh wine into old skins, lest the wine burst the skins, and the skins be destroyed, and the wine spilled; but they put [36] the fresh wine in the new skins, and both are preserved.
Luke v. 38, 39.And no man drinketh old wine and straightway desireth fresh; for he saith, The old is better.

[37]
Matt. xii. 1.And while Jesus was walking on the sabbath day among the sown fields, his disciples [Arabic, p. 29] hungered. And they were rubbing the ears with their hands, and [38] eating.
Matt. xii. 2a.But some of the Pharisees, when they saw them,
Mark ii. 24.said unto him, See, [39] why
Syr. In Arab. it means what? do thy disciples on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?
Mark ii. 25.But Jesus said unto them, Have ye not read in olden time what David did, when he had need and [40] hungered, he and those that were with him?
Mark ii. 26.how he entered the house of God, when Abiathar was high priest, and ate the bread of the table of the Lord, which it was not lawful that any should eat, save the priests, and gave to them that were with him also? [41]
Mark ii. 27.And he said unto them, The sabbath was created because of man, and man was not [42] created because of the sabbath.
Matt. xii. 5.Or have ye not read in the law, that the priests in [43] the temple profane the sabbath, and yet they are blameless?
Matt. xii. 6.I say unto you now, [44] that here is what
This may be simply a misinterpretation of the ordinary Syriac reading, which in all probability agrees with the masculine reading found in the Text. Rec. of the Greek. is greater than the temple.
Matt. xii. 7.If ye had known this:
Is it possible that the Arabic word after known is not meant simply to introduce the quotation, but is to be taken in the adverbial sense, how representing the Syriac what that is? I love mercy, [45] not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned
See § 10, 13, note. those on whom is no blame.
Matt. xii. 8.The [46] Lord of the sabbath is the Son of man.
Mark iii. 21.And his relatives heard, and went out to take him, and said, He hath gone out of his mind.

[47]
Luke vi. 6.And on the next
Lit. other. The definite article is a mistake of the translator. sabbath day he entered
Here, at the end of leaf 17 of Vat. ms., is a note by a later hand: “Here a leaf is missing.” This first lacuna extends from § 7, 47 to § 8, 17. into the synagogue and was teaching. [48]
Luke vi. 7.And there was there a man whose right hand was withered. And the scribes and the Pharisees were watching him, whether he would heal on the sabbath day, [49] that they might find the means of accusing him.
Luke vi. 8.But he knew their thoughts, and said unto the man whose hand was withered, Rise and come near into the midst of [50] the synagogue.
Luke vi. 9.And when he came and stood, Jesus said unto them, I ask you, which is lawful to be done on the sabbath day, good or evil? shall lives be saved or [51] [Arabic, p. 30] destroyed?
Mark iii. 4b.But they were silent.
Mark iii. 5.Regarding
An easy clerical error for And so he regarded (cf. Peshitta). them with anger, being grieved because of the hardness of their hearts. And he said unto the man, Stretch out thy hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand became straight. [52]
Matt. xii. 11.Then he said unto them, What man of you shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a [53] well on the sabbath day, will not take it and lift it out?
Matt. xii. 12.And how much is man better than a sheep! Wherefore it is lawful on the sabbath to do good.

div3.title: Section VIII.
div3.p:
[1]
Matt. xii. 14.And the Pharisees went out, and consulted together concerning him, that they [2] might destroy him.
Matt. xii. 15.And Jesus perceived, and removed thence: and great multitudes [3] followed him; and he healed all of them:
Matt. xii. 16.and he forbade them that they should [4] not make him known:
Lit. lead to him.
Matt. xii. 17.that the saying in Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which said,

[5] 
 Matt. xii. 18.Behold, my
servant
 The Arabic word
strictly means young man. with whom I am pleased;

My beloved in whom my soul hath delighted:
Or, rested.
My spirit have I put upon him,
And he shall proclaim to the nations judgement.

[6]
Matt. xii. 19.He shall not dispute, nor cry out;
And no man shall hear his voice in the marketplace.

[7]
Matt. xii. 20.And a bruised reed shall he not break,

And a smoking lamp
Or, wick. shall he not extinguish,
Until he shall bring forth judgement unto victory.

[8]
Matt. xii. 21.And the nations shall rejoice in his name.
The Arab. might also mean, And he shall preach (the good tidings) to the peoples in his name (cf. § 22, 47, note).

[9]
Luke vi. 12.And in those days Jesus went out to the mountain that he might pray, and he [10] spent the night
This phrase, in this case adopted from the Syriac, really means, in Arab., morning found him. there in prayer to God.
Luke vi. 13a.And when the morning was come, he called the disciples.
Mark iii. 7.And he went towards the sea: and there followed him much people [11] from Galilee that he might pray,
It must be remembered that we have here only one ms. The Arabic words for Galilee and for mountain are very similar. The words that he might pray have therefore probably made their way here by some error from § 8, 9, above.
Mark iii. 8.and from Judæa, and from Jerusalem, and from Idumæa, and from beyond Jordan, and from Tyre, and from Sidon, and from Decapolis; [12] and great multitudes came unto him, which had heard what he did.
Mark iii. 9.And he spake to his disciples to bring him the boat because of the multitudes, that they [13] might not throng him.
Mark iii. 10.And he healed many, so that they were almost falling on [Arabic, p. 31] him
So (with the Peshitta) by transposing two letters. The Arabic text as it stands can hardly be translated. Almost may be simply a corruption of the Arabic word were. on account of their seeking to get near him. And
The syntax of the Arabic is ambiguous. The alternative followed above, which seems the most natural, is that which agrees most nearly with the Peshitta. those that had [14] plagues and unclean spirits,
Mark iii. 11.as soon as they beheld him, would fall, and [15] cry out, and say, Thou art the Son of God.
Mark iii. 12.And he rebuked them much, that they [16] should not make him known.
Luke vi. 18.And those that were under the constraint of
Or, troubled with. unclean [17] spirits were healed.
Luke vi. 19.And all of the crowd were seeking to come near
This is the meaning of the Arabic word, as it is the primary meaning of the Syriac; but in this work a number of words meaning approach are used (and generally translated) in the sense of touch. The commonest word so used is that in § 12, 13 (cf. also § 12, 35). him; because power went out from him, and he healed them all.

[18, 19]
Matt. v. 1a.And when Jesus saw the multitudes, he went up to the mountain.
Luke vi. 13b.And he called his disciples, and chose from them twelve; and they are those whom he named [20] apostles:
Luke vi. 14.Simon, whom he named Cephas, and Andrew his brother, and James and [21] John, and Philip and Bartholomew,
Luke vi. 15.and Matthew and Thomas, and James the son [22] of Alphæus, and Simon which was called the Zealot,
Luke vi. 16.and Judas the son of James, [23] and Judas the Iscariot, being he that had betrayed him.
So Vat. ms., followed by Ciasca (cf. Sin.). Borg. ms. has he that was betraying or was a traitor (cf. Peshitta).
Luke vi. 17a.And Jesus went down with them and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and the great [24] multitude of people.
Mark iii. 14.And these twelve he chose to be with him, and that he might [25] send them to preach, and to have power to heal the sick and to cast out devils.

[26]
Luke vi. 20.Then he lifted up his eyes unto them, and opened his mouth,
Matt. v. 2.and taught them, and said,

[27]
Matt. v. 3.Blessed are the poor in spirit: for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.

[28]
Matt. v. 4.Blessed are the sorrowful: for they shall be comforted.

[29]
Matt. v. 5.Blessed are the humble: for they shall inherit the earth.

[30]
Matt. v. 6.Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be satisfied.

[31]
Matt. v. 7.Blessed are the merciful: for on them shall be mercy.

[32] [Arabic, p. 32]
Matt. v. 8.Blessed are the pure in their hearts: for they shall see God.

[33]
Matt. v. 9.Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the sons of God.

[34]
Matt. v. 10.Blessed are they that were persecuted
This word, the ordinary meaning of which is expel, is freely used by our translator in the sense of persecute. for righteousness’ sake: for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.

[35]
Luke vi. 22a.Blessed are ye when men shall hate you, and separate you from them, and persecute you, and reproach you,
Matt. v. 11b.and shall speak against you with all evil talk, for my [36] sake, falsely.
Matt. v. 12.Then rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets before you.

[37]
Luke vi. 24.But woe unto you rich! for ye have received your consolation.

[38]
Luke vi. 25.Woe unto you that are satisfied! ye shall hunger.
Woe unto you that laugh now! ye shall weep and be sad.

[39]
Luke v. 26.Woe unto you when men praise you! for so did their fathers use to do to the false prophets.

[40]
Luke vi. 27.Unto you do I say, ye which hear,
Matt. v. 13.Ye are the salt of the earth: if then the salt become tasteless, wherewith shall it be salted? For any purpose it is of no use, but [41] is thrown outside, and men tread upon it.
Matt. v. 14.Ye are the light of the world. It is [42] impossible that a city built on a mountain should be hid.
Matt. v. 15.Neither do they light a
lamp and place it under a bushel, but on the lamp-stand, and it giveth light to all [43] who are in the house.
Matt. v. 16.So shall
Or, let (cf. § 4, 20, note). your light shine before men, that they may see [44] your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
Mark iv. 22.There is nothing [45] secret that shall not be revealed, or hidden that shall not be known.
Mark iv. 23.Whoever hath ears that hear, let him hear.

[46]
Matt. v. 17.Think not that I came to destroy the law or the prophets; I came not to destroy, [47] but to complete.
Matt. v. 18.Verily I say unto you, Until heaven and earth shall pass, there [Arabic, p. 33] shall not pass one point or one letter of the law, until all of it shall be [48] accomplished.
Matt. v. 19.Every one who shall violate now one of these small commandments, and shall teach men so, shall be called lacking in the kingdom of heaven: every one that shall do and teach shall
Lit. this (man) shall. be called great in the kingdom [49] of heaven.
Matt. v. 20.I say unto you now, unless your righteousness abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall not enter the kingdom of heaven.

[50]
Matt. v. 21.Ye have heard that it was said to the ancients, Do not kill; and every one that [51] killeth is worthy of the judgement.
Matt. v. 22.But I say unto you that every one who is angry with his brother without a cause is worthy of the judgement; and every one that saith to his brother, Thou foul one, is condemned
See § 10, 13, note. by the synagogue; and whosoever [52] saith to him, Thou fool, is worthy of the fire of Gehenna.
Matt. v. 23.If thou art now offering thy gift at the altar, and rememberest there that thy brother hath conceived [53] against thee any grudge,
Matt. v. 24.leave thy gift at the altar, and go first and satisfy thy [54] brother, and then return and offer thy gift.
Matt. v. 25a.Join
The text is rather uncertain. thine adversary quickly,
Luke xii. 58a.and while thou art still with him in the way, give a ransom and free thyself from him; [55] lest thine adversary deliver thee to the judge,
Matt. v. 25c.and the judge deliver thee to the tax-collector, [56] and thou fall into prison.
Matt. v. 26.And verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt not go out thence until thou payest the last farthing.

[57, 58]
Matt. v. 27.Ye have heard that it was said, Do not commit adultery:
Matt. v. 28.but I now say unto you, that every one that looketh at a woman lusting after her hath forthwith already [59] [Arabic, p. 34] committed adultery with her in his heart.
Matt. v. 29.If thy right eye injure thee, put it out and cast it from thee; for it is preferable for thee that one of thy [60] members should perish, and not thy whole body go into the fire of hell.
Matt. v. 30.And if thy right hand injure thee, cut it off and cast it from thee; and it is better for thee that [61] one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body fall into Gehenna.
Matt. v. 31.It was said that he that putteth away his wife should give her a writing of divorcement: [62]
Matt. v. 32.but I say unto you, that every one that putteth away his wife, except for the cause of adultery, hath made it lawful for
The text is probably corrupt. Vat. ms. has on margin, i.e., caused her. her to commit adultery: and whosoever taketh one that is put away committeth adultery.

div3.title: Section IX.
div3.p:
[1]
Matt. v. 33.Ye have heard also that it was said unto the ancients, Lie not, but perform unto [2] God in thy oaths:
Matt. v. 34.but I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven, for it [3] is God’s throne;
Matt. v. 35.nor by the earth, for it is a footstool under his feet; nor yet by [4] Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great
The adj. is in the superlative. King.
Matt. v. 36.Neither shalt thou swear by thy [5] head, for thou canst not make in it one lock of hair black or white.
Matt. v. 37.But your word shall be either Yea or Nay, and what is in excess of this is of the evil one.

[6, 7]
Matt. v. 38.Ye have heard that it was said, Eye for eye, and tooth for tooth:
Matt. v. 39.but I say unto you, Stand not in opposition to the evil;
A literal reproduction of the Greek, like that in Syr. versions. but whosoever smiteth thee on thy right [8] cheek,
Lit. jaw. turn to him also the other.
Matt. v. 40.And he that would sue thee, and take thy tunic, [9] leave to him also thy wrapper.
Matt. v. 41.And whosoever compelleth thee one mile, go with [10] [Arabic, p. 35] him twain.
Matt. v. 42.And he that asketh thee, give unto him:
Luke vi. 30b.and he that would borrow of thee, prevent him not. And prosecute
Or, punish. not him that taketh thy [11] substance.
Luke vi. 31.And as ye desire that men should do to you, so do ye also to them.

[12, 13]
Matt. v. 43.Ye have heard that it was said, Love thy neighbour and hate thine enemy:
Matt. v. 44.but I say unto you, Love your enemies, and pray for those that curse you, and deal well
with those that hate you, and pray for those who take you with violence and persecute you; [14]
Matt. v. 45.that ye may be sons of your heavenly Father, who maketh his sun to rise on the good and the evil, and sendeth down his rain on the righteous and the [15] unrighteous.
Matt. v. 46.If ye love them that love you, what reward shall ye have?
Luke vi. 32b.for the publicans [16] and sinners also love those that love them.
Luke vi. 33.And if ye do a kindness to those [17] who treat you well, where is your superiority? for sinners also do likewise.
Luke vi. 34.And if ye lend to him of whom ye hope for a reward,
Or, return. where is your superiority? for the [18] sinners also lend to sinners, seeking recompense from
Or, to be given back as much by. them.
Luke vi. 35.But love your enemies, and do good to them, and lend, and cut not off the hope of any man; that your reward may be great, and ye may be the children of the Highest: for he is lenient [19] towards the wicked and the ungrateful.
Luke vi. 36.Be ye merciful, even as your Father also is [20] merciful.
Matt. v. 47.And if ye inquire for the good of your brethren only, what more have [21] ye done than others? is not this the conduct of the publicans also?
Matt. v. 48.Be ye now
Our translator is continually using this word (cf. § 9, 23) where the context and the originals require then or therefore. We shall only occasionally reproduce the peculiarity. perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.

[22]
Matt. vi. 1.Consider your alms; do them not before men to let them see you: and if it be not [23] so,
A clumsy phrase. ye have no reward before your Father which is in the heavens.
Matt. vi. 2.When then thou givest an alms now, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as do the people of hypocrisy, [Arabic, p. 36] in the synagogues and the marketplaces, that men may praise them. And [24] verily say I unto you, They have received their reward.
Matt. vi. 3.But thou, when [25] thou doest alms, let thy left hand not know what thy right hand doeth;
Matt. vi. 4.that thine alms may be concealed: and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.

[26]
Matt. vi. 5.And whenever thou prayest, be not as the hypocrites, who love to stand in the synagogues and in the corners of the marketplaces for prayers, that men may behold [27] them.
Matt. vi. 6.And verily say I unto you, They have received their reward. But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and fasten thy door, and pray to thy Father in secret, and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly. [28]
Matt. vi. 7.And whenever ye pray, be not babblers, as the heathen; for they think that by the [29] abundance of their words they shall be heard.
Matt. vi. 8.Then be not ye now like unto them: [30] for your Father knoweth your request before ye ask him.
Luke xi. 1b.One of his disciples said [31] unto him, Our Lord, teach us to pray, as John taught his disciples.
Luke xi. 2a.Jesus said unto [32] them, Thus now pray ye now:
The Arabic text makes Matthew begin here.
Matt. vi. 9.Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy [33, 34] name.
Matt. vi. 10.Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done,
The text as printed reads, That thy will may be (done); but it is to be explained as a (very common grammatical) transcriptional error. The Cur., however, has and. as in heaven, so on earth.
Matt. vi. 11.Give us the [35] food of to-day.
Matt. vi. 12.And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgave those that trespassed [36] against us.
Matt. vi. 13.And bring us not into temptations, but deliver us from the evil one. For [37] thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever and ever.
Lit. unto the age of the ages.
Matt. vi. 14.If ye forgive [Arabic, p. 37] men their wrong-doing,
Or, folly; and so in following verse. your Father which is in heaven will forgive you. [38]
Matt. vi. 15.But if ye forgive not men, neither will your Father pardon your wrong-doing.

[39]
Matt. vi. 16.When ye fast, do not frown, as the hypocrites; for they make their faces austere, that they may be seen of
Or, shew to. men that they are fasting. Verily I say unto you, They [40] have received their reward.
Matt. vi. 17.But when thou fastest, wash thy face and anoint thy [41] head;
Matt. vi. 18.that thou make not an appearance to men of fasting, but to thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee.

[42]
Luke xii. 32.Be not agitated, little flock; for your Father hath delighted to give you the kingdom. [43]
Luke xii. 33a.Sell your possessions, and give in alms; take to yourselves purses that wax [44] not old.
Matt. vi. 19.Lay not up treasure on earth, where moth and worm corrupt, and where [45] thieves break through and steal:
Matt. vi. 20.but lay up for yourselves treasure in heaven, where [46] moth and worm do not corrupt, nor thieves break through nor steal:
Matt. vi. 21.for where your [47] treasure is, there also will your heart be.
Matt. vi. 22.The lamp of the body is the eye: if then
Or, for if. [48] thine eye now be sound, thy whole body also shall be light.
Matt. vi. 23.But if thine eye be evil, all thy body shall be dark. And if the light which is in thee is darkness, how [49] great is
Or, will be. thy darkness!
Luke xi. 35.Be watchful that the light which is in thee be not darkness. [50]
Luke xi. 36.Because that, if thy whole body is light, and have no part dark, it shall all be light, as the lamp giveth light to thee with its flame.

div3.title: Section X.
div3.p:
[1] [Arabic, p. 38]
Matt. vi. 24.No man can serve two masters; and that because it is necessary that he hate one of them and love the other, and honour one of them and despise the [2] other.
Matt. vi. 25.Ye cannot serve God and possessions. And because of this I say unto you, Be not anxious for yourselves,
Or, your souls; or, your lives. what ye shall eat and what ye shall drink; neither for your bodies, what ye shall put on. Is not the life better than the food, and the body [3] than the raiment?
Matt. vi. 26.Consider the birds of the heaven, which sow not, nor reap, nor store in barns; and yet your Father which is in heaven feedeth them. Are not ye [4] better than they?
Matt. vi. 27.Who of you when he trieth is able to add to his stature one [5] cubit?
Luke xii. 26.If then ye are not able for a small thing, why are ye anxious about the [6, 7] rest?
Matt. vi. 28.Consider the wild lily, how it grows, although it toils not, nor spins;
Matt. vi. 29.and I say unto you that Solomon in the greatness of his glory was not clothed like one of [8] them.
Matt. vi. 30.And if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to-day is, and to-morrow [9] is cast
Lit. falleth (cf. Syriac). into the oven, how much more shall be unto you, O ye of little faith!
Matt. vi. 31.Be not anxious, so as to say, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, With [10] what shall we be clothed?
Luke xii. 29b.Neither let your minds be perplexed in this:
Matt. vi. 32.all these things the nations of the world seek; and your Father which is in heaven knoweth [11] your need of all these things.
Matt. vi. 33.Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; [12] [Arabic, p. 39] and all these shall come to you as something additional for you.
Matt. vi. 34.Be not anxious for the morrow; for the morrow shall be anxious for what belongs to it. Sufficient unto the day is its evil.

[13]
Matt. vii. 1.Judge not, that ye be not judged:
Luke vi. 37b.condemn
The word means to contend successfully, but is used throughout by our translator in the sense of condemn. not, that ye be not condemned: [14]
Luke vi. 38.forgive, and it shall be forgiven you: release, and ye shall be released: give, that ye may be given unto; with good measure, abundant, full, they shall thrust
This is the reading adopted by Ciasca in his Latin version. The diacritical points in the Arabic text, as he has printed it (perhaps a misprint), give second person plural passive instead of third plural active. into your [15] bosoms.
Mark iv. 24b.With what measure ye measure it shall be measured to you. See to it what ye hear: with what measure ye measure it shall be measured to you; and ye [16] shall be given more.
Mark iv. 25.I say unto those that hear, He that hath shall be given unto; and he that hath not, that which he regards
cf. Luke viii. 18b. Our translator uses the same word in § 50, 5=Luke xxiii. 8b; and in both cases it represents the same word in the Syriac versions. as his shall be taken from him.

[17]
Luke vi. 39.And he spake unto them a parable, Can a blind man haply guide a blind man? [18] shall
Or, Do. they not both fall into a hollow?
Luke vi. 40.A disciple is not better than his master; [19] every perfect man shall be as his master.
Luke vi. 41.Why lookest thou at the mote which is in the eye of thy brother, but considerest not the column that is in thine own eye? [20]
Luke vi. 42.Or how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, I will take out the mote from thine eye; and the column which is in thine eye thou seest not? Thou hypocrite, take out first the column from thine eye; and then shalt thou see to take out the mote from the eye of thy brother.

[21]
Matt. vii. 6.Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast your pearls before the swine, lest they trample them with their feet, and return and wound you.

[22]
Luke xi. 5.And he said unto them, Who of you, that hath a friend, goeth to him at midnight, [23] and saith unto him, My friend, lend me three loaves;
Luke xi. 6.for a friend hath come [24] to me from a journey, and I have nothing to offer to him:
Luke xi. 7.and that friend shall [Arabic, p. 40] answer him from within, and say unto him, Trouble me not; for the door is shut, and my children are with me in bed, and I cannot rise and give thee? [25]
Luke xi. 8.And verily I say unto you, If he will not give him because of friendship, yet because [26] of his importunity he will rise and give him what he seeketh.
Luke xi. 9.And I also say unto you, Ask, and ye shall be given unto; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be [27] opened unto you.
Luke xi. 10.Every one that asketh receiveth, and he that seeketh findeth, and [28] he that knocketh, it shall be opened to him.
Luke xi. 11.What father of you, shall his son ask for bread—will he, think you, give him a stone?
The Arabic might also be rendered, What father of you whom his son asketh for bread, will (think you) give him a stone? But as the Peshitta preserves the confused construction of the Greek, it is probably better to render as above.and if he ask of him a fish, will he, [29] think you,
Luke xi. 12.instead of the fish give him a serpent? and if he ask him for an egg, will
[30] he, think you, extend to him a scorpion?
Luke xi. 13.If ye then, although being evil, know the gifts which are good, and give them to your children, how much more shall your [31] Father which is in heaven give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?
Matt. vii. 12.Whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: this is the law and the prophets.

[32]
Matt. vii. 13.Enter
There is nothing about striving. The verb is walaga, which means enter (cf. § 11, 48). ye by the narrow gate; for the wide gate and the broad way lead to destruction, [33] and many they be which go therein.
Matt. vii. 14.How narrow is the gate and straitened the way leading to life! and few be they that find it.

[34]
Matt. vii. 15.Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s
Or, lambs’. clothing, while within [35] they are ravening wolves.
Matt. vii. 16a.But by their fruits ye shall know them.
Luke vi. 44.For every tree is known by its fruit. For figs are not gathered
The verbs might be singular active, but not plural as in Syriac versions (cf., however, § 38, 43, note, end). In the Borg. ms. the nouns are in the accusative. of thorns, neither are grapes plucked of [36] briers.
Matt. vii. 17.Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit, but the evil tree bringeth [37] [Arabic, p. 41] forth evil fruit.
Matt. vii. 18.The good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can the [38] evil tree bring forth good fruit.
Luke vi. 45.The good man from the good treasures that are in his heart bringeth forth good things; and the evil man from the evil treasures that are in his heart bringeth forth evil things: and from the overflowings of the [39] heart the lips speak.
Matt. vii. 19.Every tree that beareth not good fruit is cut down and cast [40, 41] into the fire.
Matt. vii. 20.Therefore by their fruits ye shall know them.
Matt. vii. 21.Not all that say unto me, My Lord, my Lord, shall enter the kingdom of the heavens; but he that doeth [42] the will of my Father which is in heaven.
Matt. vii. 22.Many shall say unto me in that day, My Lord, my Lord, did we not prophesy in thy name, and in thy name cast out [43] devils, and in thy name do many powers?
Matt. vii. 23.Then shall I say unto them, I never [44] knew you: depart from me, ye servants of iniquity.
Luke vi. 47.Every man that cometh unto [45] me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to what he is like:
Luke vi. 48.he is like the wise man which built a house, and digged and went deep, and laid the [46] foundations on a rock:
Matt. vii. 25.and the rain came down, and the rivers overflowed, and the winds blew, and shook that house, and it fell not: for its foundation was laid on [47] rocks.
Matt. vii. 26.And every one that heareth these my words, and doeth them not, is like [48] the foolish man which built his house on sand, without foundation:
Matt. vii. 27.and the rain descended, and the rivers overflowed, and the winds blew, and smote upon that house, and it fell: and the fall of it was great.

div3.title: Section XI.
div3.p:
[3]
Matt. viii. 1.And when he descended from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

[4]
Matt. viii. 5a; Luke vii. 2.And when Jesus entered Capernaum, the servant of one of the chiefs was in an [5] evil case, and he was precious to him, and he was at the point of death.
Luke vii. 3.And he [6] heard of Jesus, and came to him with the elders of the Jews;
Matt. viii. 5b; Matt. viii. 6.and he besought him, and said, My Lord, my boy is laid in the house paralysed,
i.e., so as to be unable to walk. and he is suffering grievous [7] torment.
Luke vii. 4b.And the elders urgently requested of him, and said, He is worthy that [8] this should be done unto him:
Luke vii. 5.for he loveth our people, and he also built the synagogue [9, 10] for us.
Matt. viii. 7.Jesus said unto him, I will come and heal him.
Matt. viii. 8.That chief answered and said, My Lord, I am not worthy that my roof should shade thee; but it sufficeth [11] that thou speak a word, and my lad shall be healed.
Luke vii. 8.And I also am a man in obedience to authority, having under my hand soldiers:
Or, bodies of soldiers. and I say to this one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant that he do this, [12] and he doeth it.
Luke vii. 9a.And when Jesus heard that, he marvelled at him,
Or, it. and turned and said unto the multitude that were coming with him,
Matt. viii. 10b.Verily I say unto you, I have [13] not found in Israel the like of this faith.
Matt. viii. 11.I say unto you, that many shall come from the east and the west, and shall recline with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob [14] [Arabic, p. 43] in the kingdom of heaven:
Matt. viii. 12.but the children of the kingdom shall be cast
[15] forth into the outer darkness: and there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Matt. viii. 13.And Jesus said to that chief, Go thy way; as thou hast believed, so shall it be unto thee. [16]
Luke vii. 10.And his lad was healed in that hour. And that chief returned to the house and found that sick servant healed.

[17]
Luke vii. 11.And the day after, he was going to a city called Nain, and his disciples with him, [18] and a great multitude.
Luke vii. 12.And when he was come near the gate of the city, he saw a crowd
Lit. company. accompanying one that was dead, the only son of his mother; and his mother was a widow: and there was with her a great multitude of the people of the [19] city.
Luke vii. 13.And when Jesus saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep [20] not.
Luke vii. 14.And he went and advanced to the bier, and the bearers of it stood still; and [21] he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.
Luke vii. 15.And that dead man sat up and began [22] to speak; and he gave him to his mother.
Luke vii. 16.And fear came on all the people: and they praised God, and said, There hath risen among us a great prophet: and, God [23] hath had regard to his people.
Luke vii. 17.And this news concerning him spread in all Judæa, and in all the region which was about them.

[24]
Matt. viii. 18.And when Jesus saw great multitudes surrounding him, he commanded them to [25] depart to the other side.
Luke ix. 57a; Matt. viii. 19.And while they were going in the way, there came one of the scribes and said unto him, My Master, I will follow thee whithersoever thou [26] goest.
Matt. viii. 20.Jesus said unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the heaven have [27] nests; but the Son of man hath not a place in which to lay his head.
Luke ix. 59.And he said unto another, Follow me. And he said unto him, My Lord, suffer me first to go and [28] bury my father.
Luke ix. 60.Jesus said unto him, Leave the dead to bury their dead; but thou, [29] follow me and preach the kingdom of God.
Luke ix. 61.And another said unto him, I will follow [Arabic, p. 44] thee, my Lord; but first suffer me to go and salute my household and [30] come.
Luke ix. 62.Jesus said unto him, There is no one who putteth his hand to the plough
Lit. plough of the yoke. and looketh behind him, and yet is fit for the kingdom of God.

[31]
Mark iv. 35; Luke viii. 22d.And he said to them on that day in the evening, Let us go over to the other side [32] of the lake; and he left
cf., e.g., at § 17, 19, § 23, 16, where the same Arabic and Syriac word is used; cf. also the ambiguity of the Greek (R.V. has left). the multitudes.
Mark iv. 36a; Luke viii. 22b.And Jesus went up and sat in the ship, [33] he and his disciples, and there were with them other ships.
Mark iv. 36c; Matt. viii. 24a.And there occurred on the sea a great tempest
Lit. commotion. of whirlwind and wind,
Luke viii. 23c. and the ship was on the point of [34] sinking from the greatness
Or, abundance. of the waves.
Mark iv. 38a.But Jesus was sleeping on a cushion in the stern of the ship;
Matt. viii. 25.and his disciples came and awoke him, and said unto him, Our [35] Lord, save us; lo, we perish.
Luke viii. 24b.And he rose, and rebuked the winds and the turbulence of the water, and said to the sea, Be still, for thou art rebuked;
Mark iv. 39b.and the wind [36] was still, and there was a great calm.
Mark iv. 40.And he said unto them, Why are ye thus [37] afraid? and why have ye no faith?
Luke viii. 25b.And they feared greatly.
The last clause belongs in the Greek to verse 41. And they marvelled, and said one to another, Who, think you, is this, who commandeth also the wind and the waves and the sea, and they obey him?

[38]
Luke viii. 26.And they departed and came to the country of the Gadarenes, which is on the [39] other side, opposite the land of Galilee.
Luke viii. 27a.And when he went out of the ship to the land,
Mark v. 2b; Luke viii. 27c.there met him from among the tombs a man who had a devil for a long time, [40] and wore no clothes, neither dwelt in a house, but among the tombs.
Mark v. 3b.And no man was [Arabic, p. 45] able to bind him with chains,
Mark v. 4a.because any time that he was bound with chains [41] and fetters he cut the chains and loosened the fetters;
Luke viii. 29c.and he was snatched
Imperfect tense. [42] away of the devil into the desert,
Mark v. 4b, 5a.and no man was able to quiet him; and at all times, in the night and in the day, he would be among the tombs and in the mountains;
Matt. viii. 28b.and no man was able to pass by that way;
Mark v. 5b.and he would cry out and wound himself [43] with stones.
Mark v. 6.And when he saw Jesus at a distance, he hastened and worshipped [44] him, and cried with a loud voice and said,
Mark v. 7a; Luke viii. 28b.What have we to do with thee, Jesus, [45] Son of the most high God?
Mark v. 7c; Luke viii. 29a.I adjure thee by God, torment me not. And Jesus commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man: and he had suffered
Lit. and it was for him. a long [46] time since the time when he came into captivity to it.
Luke viii. 30.And Jesus asked him, What is thy name? He said unto him, Legion; for there had entered into him many [47] devils.
Luke viii. 31.And they besought him that he would not command them to depart into [48] the depths.
Luke viii. 32.And there was there a herd of many swine, feeding in the mountain,
and those devils besought him to give them leave to enter the swine; and he gave [49] them leave.
Luke viii. 33.And the devils went out of the man and entered into the swine.
Mark v. 13b.And that herd hastened to the summit and fell down into the midst of the sea, about two [50] thousand, and they were choked in the water.
Luke viii. 34.And when the keepers saw what [51] happened, they fled, and told those in the cities and villages.
Luke viii. 35.And the people went out to see what had happened; and they came to Jesus, and found the man whose [Arabic, p. 46] devils had gone out, clothed, modest,
cf. Syriac versions. seated at the feet of Jesus; and they [52] feared.
Luke viii. 36.And they reported what they saw, and how the man was healed who had a devil,
Mark v. 16b.and concerning those swine also.

div3.title: Section XII.
div3.p:
[1]
Luke viii. 37a.And all the multitude of the Gadarenes entreated him to depart from them, because that great fear took hold upon them.

[2, 3]
Matt. ix. 1.But Jesus went up into the ship, and crossed, and came to his city.
Luke viii. 38.And that man from whom the devils went out entreated that he might stay with him; but [4] Jesus sent him away, and said unto him,
Luke viii. 39a.Return to thy house, and make known what [5] God hath done for thee.
Mark v. 20.And he went, and began to publish in Decapolis
Lit. the ten cities. what Jesus had done for him; and they all marvelled.

[6]
Mark v. 21a; Luke viii. 40b.And when Jesus had crossed in the ship to that side, a great multitude received [7] him; and they were all looking for him.
Luke viii. 41a.And a man named Jairus, the chief of the [8] synagogue, fell before the feet of Jesus,
Mark v. 23a.and besought him much, and said unto him, I have an only daughter, and she is come nigh unto death;
Matt. ix. 18b.but come and lay thy [9] hand upon her, and she shall live.
Matt. ix. 19.And Jesus rose, and his disciples, and they followed [10] him.
Mark v. 24b.And there joined him a great multitude, and they pressed him.

[11, 12]
Mark v. 25.And a woman, which had a flow of blood for twelve years,
Mark v. 26.had suffered much of many physicians, and spent all that she had, and was not benefited at all, but her [13] trouble increased further.
Mark v. 27.And when she heard of Jesus, she came in the thronging of [14] [Arabic, p. 47] the crowd behind him, and touched
See § 8, 17, note. his garments;
Mark v. 28.and she thought within [15] herself, If I could reach to touch his garments, I should live.
Mark v. 29.And immediately the fountain of her blood was dried; and she felt in her body that she was healed [16] of her plague.
Mark v. 30.And Jesus straightway knew within himself that power had gone out of him; and he turned to the crowd, and said, Who approached unto my garments? [17]
Luke viii. 45b.And on their denying, all of them, Simon Cephas and those with him said unto him, Our Master, the multitudes throng thee and press thee, and sayest thou, Who approached [18] unto me?
Luke viii. 46.And he said, Some one approached unto me; and I knew that [19] power went forth from me.
Luke viii. 47a.And that woman, when she saw that she was not hid [20] from him, came fearing and agitated (for she knew what had happened to her),
Mark v. 33b; Luke viii. 47c.and fell down and worshipped him, and told, in the presence of all the people, for what [21] reason she touched him, and how she was healed immediately.
Luke viii. 48; Mark v. 34b.And Jesus said unto her, Be of good courage, daughter; thy faith hath made thee alive; depart in peace, and be whole from thy plague.

[22]
Luke viii. 49.And while he was yet speaking, there came a man from the house of the chief of the synagogue, and said unto him, Thy daughter hath died; so trouble not the [23] teacher.
Luke viii. 50.But Jesus heard, and said unto the father of the maid, Fear not: but believe [24] only, and she shall live.
Mark v. 37.And he suffered no man to go with him, except [25] Simon Cephas, and James, and John the brother of James.
Mark v. 38.And they reached the house of the chief of the synagogue; and he saw them agitated, weeping and wailing. [26]
Mark v. 39.And he entered, and said unto them, Why are ye agitated and weeping? the [27] [Arabic, p. 48] maid hath not died, but she is sleeping.
Luke viii. 53.And they laughed at him, for [28] they knew that she had died.
Mark v. 40b.And he put every man forth without, and took the father of the maid, and her mother, and Simon, and James, and John, and [29] entered into the place where the maid was laid.
Mark v. 41.And he took hold of the hand of the maid, and said unto her, Maid, arise.
Luke viii. 55a.And her spirit returned, and straightway [30] she arose and walked:
Mark v. 42b.and she was about twelve years of age.
Luke viii. 55b.And he commanded [31] that there should be given to her something to eat.
Luke viii. 56.And her father wondered greatly:
[32] and he warned them that they should tell no man what had happened.
Matt. ix. 26.And this report spread in all that land.

[33]
Matt. ix. 27.And when Jesus crossed over from there, there joined him two blind men, crying [34] out, and saying, Have mercy on us, thou son of David.
Matt. ix. 28.And when he came to the house, those two blind men came to him: and Jesus said unto them, Believe ye [35] that I am able to do this? They said unto him, Yea, our Lord.
Matt. ix. 29.Then he touched
Lit. went forward to (cf. § 8, 17, note). [36] their eyes, and said, As ye have believed, it shall be unto you.
Matt. ix. 30.And immediately their eyes were opened. And Jesus forbade them, and said, See that no man know. [37]
Matt. ix. 31.But they went out and published the news in all that land.

[38]
Matt. ix. 32.And when Jesus went out, they brought to him a dumb man having a devil. [39]
Matt. ix. 33.And on the going out of the devil that dumb man spake. And the multitudes marvelled, and said, It was never so seen in Israel

[40]
Matt. ix. 35.And Jesus was going about in all the cities and in the villages, and teaching in their synagogues, and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease [41] [Arabic, p. 49] and sickness; and many followed him.
Matt. ix. 36.And when Jesus saw the multitudes, he had compassion on them, for they were wearied and scattered,
Lit. cast away (cf. meanings of Syriac word). as sheep [42] that have no shepherd.
Matt. x. 1a; Luke ix. 1b.And he called his twelve disciples, and gave them power and [43] much authority over all devils and diseases;
Luke ix. 2.and sent them two and two, that they [44] might proclaim the kingdom of God, and to heal the sick.
Matt. x. 5.And he charged them, and said, Walk not in the way of the heathen, nor enter into the cities of the Samaritans.
§ 34, 40, shows that this Arabic form may be so translated. [45, 46]
Matt. x. 6.Go especially unto the sheep that are lost of the sons of Israel.
Matt. x. 7.And [47] when ye go, proclaim and say, The kingdom of heaven is come near.
Matt. x. 8.And heal the sick, and cleanse the lepers, and cast out the devils: freely ye have received, freely [48, 49] give.
Matt. x. 9f.Get you not gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses;
Mark vi. 8b; Luke ix. 3.and take nothing for the way, except a staff only; nor bag, nor bread; neither shall ye have two tunics, [50] nor shoes, nor staff, but be shod with sandals;
Matt. x. 10c; Mark vi. 9a.for the labourer is worthy of his food. [51]
Matt. x. 10d.And whatever city or village ye enter, inquire who is worthy in it, and there be until [52, 53] ye go out.
Matt. x. 11.And when ye enter into the house, ask for the peace of the house: and if the house is worthy, your peace shall come upon it;
Matt. x. 12; Matt. x. 13.but if it is not worthy, your [54] peace shall return unto you.
Matt. x. 14a; Mark vi. 11b.And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your sayings, when ye go out from that house, or from that village, shake off the dust [55] [Arabic, p. 50] that is under your feet against them for a testimony.
Matt. x. 15.And verily I say unto you, To the land of Sodom and Gomorrah there shall be rest in the day of judgement, rather than to that city.

div3.title: Section XIII.
div3.p:
[1]
Matt. x. 16.I am sending you as lambs among wolves: be ye now wise as serpents, and [2] harmless
The word is occasionally used in this sense, but ordinarily means sound, unhurt. as doves.
Matt. x. 17.Beware of men: they shall deliver you to the councils of the [3] magistrates, and scourge you in their synagogues;
Matt. x. 18.and shall bring you before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and against the nations. [4]
Matt. x. 19.And when they deliver you up, be not
From this point down to Matt. x. 27a, is assigned by Vat. ms. to Mark. anxious, nor consider beforehand, what ye [5] shall say; but ye shall be given
Borg. ms. reads, but what ye are granted ye shall speak, and ye shall be given in, etc., and there seems to be a trace of this reading in Ciasca’s text. in that hour what ye ought to speak.
Matt. x. 20.Ye do not [6] speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaketh in you.
Matt. x. 21.The brother shall deliver up his brother to death, and the father his son; and the sons shall rise against their [7] parents, and put them to death.
Matt. x. 22.And ye shall be hated of every man because of [8] my name; but he that endureth unto the end of the matter shall be saved.
See note to § 1, 78.
Matt. x. 23.When they expel you from this city, flee to another. Verily I say unto you, Ye shall not finish all the cities of the people of Israel, until the Son of man come.

[9, 10]
Matt. x. 24.A disciple is not superior to his lord, nor a servant to his master.
Matt. x. 25.For it is enough then for the disciple that he be as his lord, and the servant as his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more the people
[11] of his house!
Matt. x. 26.Fear them not therefore:
See note to § 9, 21. for there is nothing covered, that shall [12] [Arabic, p. 51] not be revealed; nor hid, that shall not be disclosed and published.
Matt. x. 27a; Luke xii. 3b.What I say unto you in the darkness, speak ye in the light; and what ye have told [13] secretly in the ears in closets, let it be proclaimed on the housetops.
Luke xii. 4a; Luke x. 28b.I say unto you now, my beloved, Be not agitated at
Perhaps this Arabic word is a copyist’s error for that used a few lines further down in Luke xii. 5, the Arabic words being very similar; but see note on § 1, 14. those who kill the body, but have no power to [14] kill the soul. I will inform you whom ye shall fear: him
Syriac. which is able to destroy [15] soul and body in hell.
Luke xii. 5; Matt. x. 29.Yea, I say unto you, Be afraid of him especially. Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing in a bond?
The Vat. ms., like the Brit. Mus. text of Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary, omits for a farthing, retaining in a bond. The two phrases are simply different explanations of the same Syriac consonants. These are really the naturalised Greek word rendered farthing in Eng. version; but they also form a Syriac word meaning bond. and one of them shall not fall on the [16] ground without your Father.
Matt. x. 30.But what concerns you: even the hair of your heads [17, 18] also is numbered.
Matt. x. 31.Fear not therefore; ye are better than many sparrows.
Matt. x. 32.Every man who confesseth me now before men, I also will confess him before my Father [19] which is in heaven;
Matt. x. 33.but whosoever denieth me before men, I also will deny him before my Father which is in heaven.

[20]
Luke xii. 51.Think ye that I am come to cast peace into the earth? I came not to cast peace, [21] but to cast dissension.
Luke xii. 52.Henceforth there shall be five in one house, three of them [22] disagreeing with two, and the two with the three.
Luke xii. 53.The father shall become hostile to his son, and the son to his father; and the mother to her daughter, and the daughter to her mother; and the mother in law to her daughter in law, and the daughter [23] in law to her mother in law:
Matt. x. 36.and a man’s enemies shall be the people of his house. [24]
Matt. x. 37.Whosoever loveth father or mother better than me is not worthy of me; and whosoever [Arabic, p. 52] loveth son or daughter more than his love of me is not worthy of me. [25]
Matt. x. 38.And every one that doth not take his cross and follow me is not worthy of [26] me.
Matt. x. 39.Whosoever findeth his life
Or, soul. shall lose it; and whosoever loseth his life
Or, soul. for my sake shall find it.

[27]
Matt. x. 40.And whosoever receiveth you receiveth me; and whosoever receiveth me receiveth [28] him that sent me.
Matt. x. 41.And whosoever receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall take
Or, receive. a prophet’s reward; and whosoever shall receive a righteous man [29] in the name of a righteous man shall take
Or, receive. a righteous man’s reward.
Matt. x. 42a; Mark ix. 41b.And every one that shall give to drink to one of these least ones a drink of water only, in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward.

[30]
Matt. xi. 1.And when Jesus finished charging his twelve disciples, he removed thence to [31] teach and preach in their cities.
Luke x. 38.And while they were going in the way they entered into a certain village; and a woman named Martha entertained him in her house. [32]
Luke x. 39.And she had a sister named Mary, and she came and sat at the feet of our Lord, [33] and heard his sayings.
Luke x. 40.But Martha was disquieted by much serving; and she came and said unto him, My Lord, givest thou no heed that my sister left me alone to [34] serve? speak to her that she help me.
Luke x. 41.Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, [35] Martha, thou art solicitous and impatient
Or, agitated. on account of many things:
Luke x. 42.but what is sought is one thing. But Mary hath chosen for herself a good portion, and that which shall not be taken from her.

[36]
Mark vi. 12.And the apostles went forth, and preached to the people that they might repent. [37]
Mark vi. 13.And they cast out many devils, and anointed many sick with oil, and healed them. [38, 39]
Luke vii. 18.And the disciples of John told him
Lit. And his disciples told John, as in the Greek, etc. of all these things.
Matt. xi. 2a; Luke vii. 19.And when John heard in [Arabic, p. 53] the prison of the doings of the Messiah, he called two of his disciples, and sent them to Jesus, and said, Art thou he that cometh, or look we for [40] another?
Luke vii. 20.And they came to Jesus, and said unto him, John the Baptist hath sent [41] us unto thee, and said, Art thou he that cometh, or look we for another?
Luke vii. 21.And in that hour he cured many of diseases, and of plagues of an evil spirit; and he gave sight [42] to many blind.
Luke vii. 22.Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and tell John everything ye have seen and heard: the blind see, and the lame walk, and the lepers are cleansed, and the blind
A different word from that used in the preceding verse. It is either an Arabic copyist’s error for the word for deaf used in Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary, or a careless blunder. hear, and the dead rise, and the poor have the gospel preached to [43] them.
Luke vii. 23.And blessed is he who doubteth not in me.

[44]
Luke vii. 24.And when John’s disciples departed, Jesus began to say to the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? a reed shaken with the [45] winds?
Luke vii. 25.And if not, then what went ye out to see? a man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they that are in magnificent garments and in voluptuousness are in the abode [46] of kings.
Luke vii. 26.And if not, then what went ye out to see? a prophet? Yea, I say unto [47] you, and more than a prophet.
Luke vii. 27.This is he of whom it is written,
I am sending my messenger before thy face
To prepare the way before thee.

div3.title: Section XIV.
div3.p:
[1]
Matt. xi. 11.Verily I say unto you, There hath not arisen among those whom women have borne a greater than John the Baptist; but he that is little now in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

[2] [Arabic, p. 54]
Luke vii. 29.And all the people which heard, and the publicans, justified
Syriac. In Arabic the word ordinarily means believed. God, for [3] they had been baptized with the baptism of John.
Luke vii. 30.But the Pharisees and the scribes wronged
See below, § 20, 28, note. the purpose of God in themselves, in that they were not baptized of [4] him.
Matt. xi. 12a.And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven is [5] snatched away by violence.
Luke xvi. 16.The law and the prophets were until John; and after that, the kingdom of God is preached, and all press to enter it:
Matt. xi. 12b.and they that exert themselves [6, 7] snatch it away.
Matt. xi. 13.All the prophets and the law until John prophesied.
Matt. xi. 14.And if ye [8] will, then receive it, that he is Elijah, which is to come.
Matt. xi. 15.Whosoever hath ears that hear [9] let him hear.
Luke xvi. 17.Easier is the perishing of heaven and earth, than the passing away of [10] one point of the law.
Luke vii. 31b.To whom then shall I liken the people of this generation,
See § 1, 49, note. and [11] to whom are they like?
Luke vii. 32.They are like the children sitting in the market, which call to their companions, and say, We sang to you, and ye danced not; we wailed to you, [12] and ye wept not.
Luke vii. 33.John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; [13] and ye said, He hath demons:
Luke vii. 34.and the Son of man came eating and drinking; and ye said, Behold, a gluttonous man, and a drinker of wine, and an associate of publicans [14, 15] and sinners!
Luke vii. 35.And wisdom was justified of all her children.
Mark iii. 20, and verse 19b.And when he said that, they came to the house. And there gathered unto him again multitudes, [16] so that they found not bread to eat.
Luke xi. 14.And while he was casting out a devil which was dumb, when he cast out that devil, that dumb man spake. And the multitudes [17] [Arabic, p. 55] marvelled.
Matt. xii. 24.And the Pharisees, when they heard, said, This man doth not cast out the devils, except by Beelzebul the chief of the demons, which is in him. [18, 19]
Luke xi. 16.And others requested of him a sign from heaven, to tempt him.
Matt. xii. 25.And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them in parables, Every kingdom that withstandeth itself shall become desolate; and every house or city that disagreeth with itself shall not [20] stand:
Matt. xii. 26a.and if a devil cast out a devil, he withstandeth himself; neither shall he be [21] able to stand, but his end shall be.
Mark iii. 26b; Matt. xii. 26b.Then how now shall his kingdom stand? for ye [22] said that I cast out devils by Beelzebul.
Luke xi. 18b; Matt. xii. 27.And if I by Beelzebul cast out the devils, then your children, by what do they cast them out? And for this cause they shall [23] be judges against you.
Matt. xii. 28.But if I by the Spirit of God cast out devils, then the kingdom [24] of God is come near unto you.
Matt. xii. 29.Or how can a man enter into the house of a valiant man, and seize his garments,
The word used in the Syriac versions (Pesh. and Cur.) means garments as well as utensils, and the Arabic translator has chosen the wrong meaning (cf. § 42, 44). if he do not beforehand secure himself
Certain derivatives from the same root signify bind, but hardly this word. from [25] that valiant man? and then will he cut off
The two Arab. mss. differ in this word, but the meaning is about the same. Perhaps both are corrupt. his house.
Luke xi. 21.But when the valiant man is [26] armed, guarding his house, his possessions are in peace.
Luke xi. 22.But if one come who is more valiant than he, he overcometh him, and taketh his whole armour, on which [27] he relieth, and divideth his spoil.
Luke xi. 23.Whosoever is not with me is against me; and [28] whosoever gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.
Mark iii. 28.For this reason I say unto you, [Arabic, p. 56] that all sins and blasphemies with which men blaspheme shall be forgiven [29] them:
Mark iii. 29.but whosoever shall blaspheme against the Holy Spirit, there is no [30] forgiveness for him for ever, but he is deserving of eternal punishment:
Mark iii. 30.because they
[31] said that he had an unclean spirit.
Matt. xii. 32.And he said also, Every one that speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him; but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, nor in the world to [32] come.
Matt. xii. 33.Either ye must make a good tree
Or, a tree good. and its fruit good; or ye must make an evil [33] tree
Or, a tree evil. and its fruit evil: for the tree is known by its fruit.
Matt. xii. 34.Ye children of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? from the overflowings of the heart the mouth [34] speaketh.
Luke vi. 45a.The good man from the good treasures which are in his heart bringeth forth good things; and the wicked man from the evil treasures which are in his [35] heart bringeth forth evils.
Matt. xii. 36.I say unto you, that every idle word which men shall [36] speak, they shall give an answer for in the day of judgement:
Matt. xii. 37.for by thy sayings thou shalt be justified, and by thy sayings thou shalt be judged.

[37]
Luke xii. 54.And he said to the multitudes, When ye see the clouds appear from the west, [38] straightway ye say that there cometh rain; and so it cometh to pass.
Luke xii. 55.And when [39] the south wind bloweth, ye say that there will be heat; and it cometh to pass.
Matt. xvi. 2b.And when the evening is come, ye say, It will be fair weather, for the heaven has become [40] red.
Matt. xvi. 3.And in the morning ye say, To-day there will be severe weather, for the redness [Arabic, p. 57] of the heaven is paling.
Matt. xvi. 4; this is reckoned to verse 3 in the Greek.Ye hypocrites, ye know to examine the face of the heaven and the earth; but the signs of this time ye know not to discern.

[41]
Matt. xii. 22.Then they brought to him one possessed of a demon, dumb and blind; and he [42] healed him, so that the dumb and blind began to speak and see.
Matt. xii. 23.And all the multitudes wondered, and said, Is this, think you, the son of David?

[43]
Mark vi. 30.And the apostles returned unto Jesus, and told him everything that they had [44] done and wrought.
Wrought may have arisen from taught by a transcriptional error (transposition of l and m) within the Arabic text. As it appears to occur in both mss., they would seem to have a common origin, which, however, can hardly have been the autograph of the translator.
Mark vi. 31.And he said unto them, Come, let us go into the desert alone, and rest ye a little. And many were going and returning, and they had not leisure, not even to eat bread.

[45]
Luke vii. 36.And after that, there came to him one of the Pharisees, and besought him that he would eat bread with him. And he entered into the house of that Pharisee, and [46] reclined.
Luke vii. 37.And there was in that city a woman that was a sinner; and when she knew that he was sitting in the house of that Pharisee, she took a box of sweet ointment, [47] and stood behind him,
Luke vii. 38.towards his feet, weeping, and began to wet his feet with her tears, and to wipe them with the hair of her head, and to kiss his feet, and [48] anoint them with the sweet ointment.
Luke vii. 39.And when that
A comparison with the Syriac text recommends this rendering. Pharisee saw it, who invited him, he thought within himself, and said, This man, if he were a prophet, would know who she is and what is her history: for the woman which touched him was a sinner.

div3.title: Section XV.
div3.p:
[1]
Luke vii. 40.Jesus answered and said unto him, Simon, I have something to say unto thee. And [2] he said unto him, Say on, my Master.
Luke vii. 41.Jesus said unto him, There were two debtors [Arabic, p. 58] to one creditor; and one of them owed five hundred pence, and the other [3] owed fifty pence.
Luke vii. 42.And because they had not wherewith to pay, he forgave [4] them both. Which of them ought to love him more?
Luke vii. 43.Simon answered and said, I suppose, he to whom he forgave most. Jesus said unto him, Thou hast judged rightly. [5]
Luke vii. 44.And he turned to that woman, and said to Simon, Dost thou see this woman? I entered into thy dwelling, and thou gavest me not water to wash my feet: but this [6] woman hath bathed
Lit. sunk, a word the choice of which is explained by the Syriac. my feet with her tears, and dried them with her hair.
Luke vii. 45.And thou kissedst me not: but this woman, since she
Or, I. entered, hath not ceased to kiss my [7] feet.
Luke vii. 46.And thou anointedst not my head with oil:
Same word in Arabic. but this woman hath anointed [8] my feet with sweet ointment.
Same word in Arabic.
Luke vii. 47.And for this, I say unto thee, Her many sins are forgiven her, because she loved much; for he to whom little is forgiven loveth little. [9, 10]
Luke vii. 48.And he said unto that woman, Thy sins are forgiven thee.
Luke vii. 49.And those that were invited [11] began to say within themselves, Who is this that forgiveth sins also?
Luke vii. 50.And Jesus said to that woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.

[12]
John ii. 23b.And many believed in him when they saw the signs which he was doing. [13, 14]
John ii. 24.But Jesus did not trust
The meaning is not apparent. himself to them,
John ii. 25.for he knew every man, and he needed not any man to testify to him concerning every man; for he knew what was in man.

[15]
