John viii. 38.And what I saw with my Father, I say: and what ye saw with your father, [50] ye do.
John viii. 39.They answered and said unto him, Our father is Abraham. Jesus said unto them, If ye were the children of Abraham, ye would do the deeds of Abraham. [51]
John viii. 40.Now, behold, ye seek to kill me, a man that speak
Lit. speaketh, according to Arabic idiom. with you
Borg. ms. omits with you. the truth, that I [52] heard from God: this did Abraham not do.
John viii. 41.And ye do the deeds of your father. They said unto him, We were not born of fornication;
Borg. ms. has an adulteress, mistaking the less common Arabic word for a clerical error. we have one Father, who is [53] God.
John viii. 42.Jesus said unto them, If God were your Father, ye would love me: I proceeded and came
Different words are used in the Arabic; so in the Greek, but not in the Peshitta. Sin. and Cur. are wanting. from God; and it was not of my own self that I came,
Different words are used in the Arabic; so in the Greek, but not in the Peshitta. Sin. and Cur. are wanting. but he sent [54] [Arabic, p. 136] me.
John viii. 43.Why then do ye not know my word? Because ye cannot hear my word. [55]
John viii. 44.Ye are from the father, the devil,
Lit. backbiter. and the lust of your father do ye desire to do, who from the beginning is a slayer of men, and in the truth standeth not, because the truth is not in him. And when he speaketh untruth, he speaketh from [56] himself: for he is a liar, and the father of untruth.
John viii. 45.And I who speak the truth, ye [57] believe me not.
John viii. 46.Who of you rebuketh me for a sin? And if I speak the truth, ye [58] do not believe me.
This is probably simply a clerical error for the ordinary reading, why have ye not believed me? The Arabic words why and not having the same consonants, one of them was purposely or accidentally omitted by a copyist.
John viii. 47.Whosoever is of God heareth the words of God: therefore do [59] ye not hear, because ye are not of God.
John viii. 48.The Jews answered and said unto him, [60] Did we not say well that thou art a Samaritan, and hast demons?
John viii. 49.Jesus said unto them, As for me, I have not a devil; but my Father do I honour, and ye dishonour [61] me.
John viii. 50.I seek not my glory: here is one who seeketh and judgeth.

div3.title: Section XXXVI.
div3.p:
[1]
John viii. 51.Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever keepeth my word shall not see death [2] for ever.
John viii. 52.The Jews said unto him, Now we know that thou hast demons. Abraham is dead, and the prophets; and thou sayest, Whosoever keepeth my word shall not [3] taste death for ever.
John viii. 53.Art thou haply greater than our father Abraham, who is [4] dead, and than the prophets, which are dead? whom makest thou thyself?
John viii. 54.Jesus said unto them, If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing: my Father is he that [5] glorifieth me; of whom ye say, that he is our
cf. Peshitta. The Sinaitic omits our. God;
John viii. 55.and yet ye have not known him: but I know him; and if I should say that I know him not, I should become [6] [Arabic, p. 137] a liar like you: but I know him, and keep his word.
John viii. 56.Abraham your father [7] longed to see my day; and he saw, and rejoiced.
John viii. 57.The Jews said unto him, [8] Thou art now not fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham?
John viii. 58.Jesus said unto [9] them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.
John viii. 59.And they take
The Vat. ms. has took him, probably omitting stones, though Ciasca does not say so. Take is probably a copyist’s error (change in diacritical paints) for took. stones to stone him:
John viii. 60 [reckoned to verse 59 in the Greek.].but Jesus concealed himself, and went out of the temple. And he passed through them, and went his way.

[10]
John ix. 1.And as he passed, he saw a man blind from his mother’s womb.
John ix. 2.And his [11] disciples asked him, and said, Our Master, who sinned, this man, or his parents, so [12] that he was born blind?
A different word in Arabic from that used in verses 1 and 6.
John ix. 3.Jesus said unto them, Neither did he sin, nor his parents: [13] but that the works of God may be seen in him.
The Vat. ms. has that we may see the works of God in him. By the addition of a diacritical point this would give the same sense as in the text above, and more grammatically.
John ix. 4.It is incumbent on me to do the deeds of him that sent me, while it is day: a night will come, and no man will be [14] able to busy himself.
John ix. 5.As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world. [15]
John ix. 6.And when he said that, he spat upon the ground, and made clay of his spittle, and [16] smeared it on the eyes of the blind man, and said unto him,
John ix. 7.Go and wash thyself in [17] the pool
The Arabic word properly means baptism. The Syriac has both meanings. of Siloam.
Lit. Shiloha, as in Syriac.
John ix. 8.And he went and washed, and came seeing. And his neighbours, which saw him of old begging, said, Is not this he that was sitting begging? [18]
John ix. 9.And some said, It is he; and others said, Nay, but he resembles him much. He [19, 20] said, I am he.
John ix. 10.They said unto him, How then were thine eyes opened?
John ix. 11.He answered and said unto them, A man named Jesus made clay, and smeared it on my eyes, and said unto me, Go and wash in the water of Siloam: and I went and [21] washed, and received sight.
Lit. saw.
John ix. 12.They said unto him, Where is he? He said, I know not. [22, 23] [Arabic, p. 138]
John ix. 13.And they brought him that was previously blind to the Pharisees.
John ix. 14.And the day in which Jesus made clay and opened with it his eyes was a sabbath [24] day.
John ix. 15.And again the Pharisees asked him, How didst thou receive sight? And he said [25] unto them, He put clay on mine eyes, and I washed, and received sight.
John ix. 16.The people
An easy clerical error for Some. of the Pharisees said, This man is not from God, for he keepeth not the sabbath. And others said, How can a man that is a sinner do these signs? And there came [26] to be a division amongst them.
John ix. 17.And again they said to that blind man, Thou, then, what sayest thou of him that opened for thee thine eyes? He said unto them, [27] I say that he is a prophet.
John ix. 18.And the Jews did not believe concerning him, that he was blind, and received sight, until they summoned the parents of him who received [28] sight, and asked them,
John ix. 19.Is this
Lit. them, whether this be. your son, of whom ye said that he was born blind? [29] how then, behold, doth he now see?
John ix. 20.His parents answered and said, We know [30] that this is our son, and that he was born blind:
John ix. 21.but how he has come to see now, or who it is that opened his eyes, we know not: and he also has reached his prime; [31] ask him, and he will speak for himself.
John ix. 22.This said his parents, because they were fearing the Jews: and the Jews decided, that if any man should confess of him that [32] he was the Messiah, they would put him out of the synagogue.
John ix. 23.For this reason [33] said his parents, He hath reached his prime; ask him.
John ix. 24.And they called the man a second time, him that was blind, and said unto him, Praise God: we know that this [34] man is a sinner.
John ix. 25.He answered and said unto them, Whether he be a sinner, I know [35] not: I know one thing, that I was blind, and I now see.
John ix. 26.They said unto him again, [36] [Arabic, p. 139] What did he unto thee? how opened he for thee thine eyes?
John ix. 27.He said unto them, I said unto you, and ye did not hear: what
Or, why (cf. note, § 7, 38). wish ye further to hear? [37] ye also, do ye wish to become disciples to him?
John ix. 28.And they reviled him, and said unto him, Thou art the disciple
Disciples is probably simply a misprint in Ciasca’s text. of that man; but as for us, we are the disciples of [38] Moses.
John ix. 29.And we know that God spake unto Moses: but this man, we know not [39] whence he is.
John ix. 30.The man answered and said unto them, From this is the wonder, [40] because ye know not whence he is, and mine eyes hath he opened.
John ix. 31.And we know that God heareth not the voice of sinners: but whosoever feareth him, and doeth [41] his will, him he heareth.
John ix. 32.From eternity hath it not been heard of, that a man [42] opened the eyes of a blind man, who had been born in blindness.
John ix. 33.If then this man [43] were not from God, he could not do that.
John ix. 34.They answered and said unto him, Thou wast all of thee born in sins, and dost thou teach us? And they put him forth without.

[44]
John ix. 35.And Jesus heard of his being put forth without, and found him, and said unto [45] him, Dost thou believe in the Son of God?
John ix. 36.He that was made whole answered [46] and said, Who is he, my Lord, that I may believe in him?
John ix. 37.Jesus said unto him, [47] Thou hast seen him, and he that speaketh to thee is he.
John ix. 38.And he said, I believe, my Lord. And he fell down worshipping him.

div3.title: Section XXXVII.
div3.p:
[1]
John ix. 39.And Jesus said, To judge the world am I come, so that they that see not may [2] see, and they that see may become blind.
John ix. 40.And some of the Pharisees which were [3] with him heard that, and they said unto him, Can it be that we are blind?
John ix. 41.Jesus said unto them, If ye were blind, ye should not have sin: but now ye say, We see: and because of this your sin remaineth.
Or, is permanent.

[4] [Arabic, p. 140]
John x. 1.Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever entereth not into the fold of the sheep by the door, but goeth up from another place, that man is a thief and a [5, 6] stealer.
John x. 2.But he that entereth by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
John x. 3.And therefore
Or, to him. the keeper of the door openeth for him the door; and the sheep hear his voice: and [7] he calleth his sheep
A different word (lit. rams) from that used in the other verses; so in Peshitta (cf. Sin., which, however, differs somewhat); cf. also § 54, 40 f., note. by their names, and they go forth unto him.
John x. 4.And when he putteth forth his sheep, he goeth before them, and his sheep
A different word (lit. rams) from that used in the other verses; so in Peshitta (cf. Sin., which, however, differs somewhat); cf. also § 54, 40 f., note. follow him: because [8] they know his voice.
John x. 5.And after a stranger will the sheep not go, but they flee from [9] him: because they hear not the voice of a stranger.
John x. 6.This parable spake Jesus unto them: but they knew not what he was saying unto them.

[10]
John x. 7.Jesus said unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the [11] sheep.
John x. 8.And all that came are thieves and stealers: but the sheep heard them not. [12]
John x. 9.I am the door: and if a man enter by me, he shall live, and shall go in and go out, [13] and shall find pasture.
John x. 10.And the stealer cometh not, save that he may steal, and kill, and destroy: but I came that they might have life, and that they might have [14] the thing that is better.
Or, best thing. Vat. ms. omits from but I came.
John x. 11.I am the good shepherd; and the good shepherd giveth [15] himself
Or, his life. for his sheep.
John x. 12.But the hireling, who is not a shepherd, and whose the sheep
cf. note to § 37, 6. are not, when he seeth the wolf as it cometh, leaveth the sheep, and fleeth, [16] and the wolf cometh, and snatcheth away the sheep, and scattereth
Or, to snatch…and scatter. them:
John x. 13.and the [17] hireling fleeth because he is an hireling, and hath no care for the sheep.
John x. 14.I am the [18] good shepherd;
John x. 15.and I know what is mine, and what is mine knoweth me, as my Father knoweth me, and I know my Father; and I give myself
Or, my life. for the sheep. [19]
John x. 16.And I have other sheep also, that are not of this flock: them also I must invite, and they shall hear my voice; and all the sheep shall be one, and the shepherd one. [20] [Arabic, p. 141]
John x. 17.And therefore doth my Father love me, because I give my life, that I may [21] take it again.
John x. 18.No man taketh it from me, but I leave it of my own choice. And I have the right to leave it, and have the right also to take it. And this commandment did I receive of my Father.

[22]
John x. 19.And there occurred a disagreement among the Jews because of these sayings. [23]
John x. 20.And many of them said, He hath a devil, and is afflicted with madness;
Lit. epilepsy. why listen [24] ye to him?
John x. 21.And others said, These sayings are not those of men possessed with demons. Can a demon haply open the eyes of a blind man?

[25, 26]
John x. 22.And the feast of the dedication came on at Jerusalem: and it was winter.
John x. 23.And [27] Jesus was walking in the temple in the porch of Solomon.
John x. 24.The Jews therefore surrounded him, and said unto him, Until when dost thou make our hearts anxious? [28]
John x. 25.If thou art the Messiah, tell us plainly. He answered and said unto them, I told you, and ye believe not: and the deeds that I do in my Father’s name bear witness [29, 30] to me.
John x. 26.But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep,
cf. § 37, 6. as I said unto you. [31]
John x. 27.And my sheep
cf. § 37, 6. hear my voice, and I know them, and they come after me:
John x. 28.and I give them eternal life; and they shall not perish for ever, nor shall any man snatch [32] them out of my hands.
Or, hand; but probably dual (cf. Syr.).
John x. 29.For the Father, who hath given them unto me, is greater [33] than all; and no man is able to take them from the hand of my
So Peshitta; but Sin. the. Borg. ms. omits the hand of. Father.
John x. 30.I and [34, 35] my Father are one.
John x. 31.And the Jews took stones to stone him.
John x. 32.Jesus said unto them, Many good deeds from my Father have I shewed you; because of which
Lit. which deed. of them, [36] then, do ye stone me?
John x. 33.The Jews said unto him, Not for the good deeds do we stone thee, but because thou blasphemest; and, whilst thou art a man, makest thyself
[37] God.
John x. 34.Jesus said unto them, Is it not thus written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? [38] [Arabic, p. 142]
John x. 35.And if he called those gods—for
cf. Peshitta. to them came the word of God (and it is [39] not possible in
This in could more easily arise as a clerical error (repetition) in the Syriac text. the scripture that anything should be undone)—
John x. 36.he then, whom the Father hath sanctified and sent into the world, do ye say that he blasphemeth; [40] because I said unto you, I am the Son of God?
John x. 37.If then I do not the deeds of my [41] Father, ye believe me not.
So Ciasca’s text, following Vat. ms. But this is probably a clerical error for the reading of Borg. ms., which omits ye.
John x. 38.But if I do, even if ye believe not me, believe the deeds: that ye may know and believe that my Father is in me, and I in my Father. [42]
John x. 39.And they sought again to take him: and he went forth out of their hands.

[43]
John x. 40.And he went beyond Jordan to the place where John was baptizing formerly; [44] and abode there.
John x. 41.And many people came unto him; and they said, John did not [45] work even one sign: but all that John said of this man is truth.
John x. 42.And many believed in him.

[46]
John xi. 1.And there was a sick man, named Lazarus, of the village of Bethany, the brother [47] of Mary and Martha.
John xi. 2.And Mary was she that anointed with sweet ointment the feet of Jesus, and wiped them with her hair; and Lazarus, who was sick, was the [48] brother of this woman.
cf. Peshitta.
John xi. 3.And his sisters sent unto Jesus, and said unto him, Our [49] Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.
John xi. 4.But Jesus said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glorifying of God, that the Son of God may be glorified [50, 51] because of it.
John xi. 5.And Jesus loved Martha, and Mary, and Lazarus.
John xi. 6.And when he [52] heard that he was sick, he abode in the place where he was two days.
John xi. 7.And after that, [53] he said unto his disciples, Come, let us go into Judæa.
John xi. 8.His disciples said unto him, Our [Arabic, p. 143] Master, now the Jews desire to stone thee; and goest thou again thither? [54, 55]
John xi. 9.Jesus said unto them, Is not the day of twelve hours? If then a man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of the world.
John xi. 10.But if [56] a man walk in the night, he stumbleth, because there is no lamp in him.
John xi. 11.This said Jesus: and after that, he said unto them, Lazarus our friend hath fallen asleep; but [57] I am going to awaken him.
John xi. 12.His disciples said unto him, Our Lord, if he hath [58] fallen asleep, he will recover.
John xi. 13.But Jesus said that concerning his death: while they [59] supposed that he spake of lying down to sleep.
John xi. 14.Then Jesus said unto them plainly, [60] Lazarus is dead.
John xi. 15.And I am glad that I was not there for your sakes, that ye may [61] believe; but let us go thither.
John xi. 16.Thomas, who is called Thama,
The Syriac word for Twin. said to the disciples, his companions, Let us also go, and die with him.

div3.title: Section XXXVIII.
div3.p:
[1, 2]
John xi. 17.And Jesus came to Bethany, and found him already four days in the grave.
John xi. 18.And Bethany was beside Jerusalem, and its distance from it was a sum of fifteen furlongs;
Arabic mil, a somewhat indefinite distance. [3]
John xi. 19.and many of the Jews came unto Mary and Martha, to comfort their heart [4] because of their brother.
John xi. 20.And Martha, when she heard that Jesus had come, went [5] out to meet him: but Mary was sitting in the house.
John xi. 21.Martha then said unto Jesus, [6] My Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
John xi. 22.But I know now that, [7] whatever thou shalt ask of God, he will give thee.
John xi. 23.Jesus said unto her, Thy brother shall [8] rise.
John xi. 24.Martha said unto him, I know that he shall rise in the resurrection at the last day. [9]
John xi. 25.Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: whosoever believeth in [10] [Arabic, p. 144] me, even though he die, he shall live:
John xi. 26.and every living one that believeth [11] in me shall never die. Believest thou this?
John xi. 27.She said unto him, Yea, my Lord: I believe that thou art the Messiah, the Son of God, that cometh into the [12] world.
John xi. 28.And when she had said that, she went and called Mary her sister secretly, [13] and said unto her, Our Master hath come, and summoneth thee.
John xi. 29.And Mary, when [14] she heard, rose in haste, and came unto him.
John xi. 30.(And Jesus then had not come into [15] the village, but was in the place where Martha met him.)
John xi. 31.And the Jews also that were with her in the house, to comfort her, when they saw that Mary rose up and went out in haste, went after her, because they supposed that she was going to the [16] tomb to weep.
John xi. 32.And Mary, when she came to where Jesus was, and saw him, fell at his feet, and said unto him, If thou hadst been here, my Lord, my brother had
[17] not died.
John xi. 33.And Jesus came; and when he saw her weeping, and the Jews that were [18] with her weeping, he was troubled
This is the Syriac word (cf. the versions, and below, § 44, 44; see also Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary, ad loc). in himself, and sighed; and he said,
John xi. 34.In what [19] place have ye laid him? And they said unto him, Our Lord, come and see.
John xi. 35.And [20] the tears of Jesus came.
So in Syriac versions.
John xi. 36.The Jews therefore said, See the greatness of his love for [21] him!
John xi. 37.But some of them said, Could not this man, who opened the eyes of that [22] blind man, have caused that this man also should not die?
John xi. 38.And Jesus came to the place of burial, being troubled within himself. And the place of burial was a cave, [23] and a stone was placed at its door.
John xi. 39.Jesus therefore said, Take these stones away. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, said unto him, My Lord, he hath come to [24] stink for some time: he hath been
Borg. ms. omits some time: he hath been. four days dead.
John xi. 40.Jesus said unto her, Did not I say [25] [Arabic, p. 145] unto thee, If thou believest, thou shalt see the glory of God?
John xi. 41.And they removed those stones. And Jesus lifted his eyes on high, and said, My Father, [26] I thank thee since thou didst hear me.
John xi. 42.And I know that thou at all times hearest me: but I say this unto thee because of this multitude that is standing, that they [27] may believe that thou didst send me.
John xi. 43.And when he had said that, he cried with a [28] loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.
John xi. 44.And that dead man came out, having his hands and feet bound with bandages, and his face wrapped in a scarf. Jesus said unto them, Loose him, and let him go.

[29]
John xi. 45.And many of the Jews which came unto Mary, when they saw the deed of Jesus, [30] believed in him.
John xi. 46.But some of them went to the Pharisees, and informed them of all that Jesus did.

[31]
John xi. 47.And the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered, and said, What shall we do? [32] for lo, this man doeth many signs.
John xi. 48.And if we leave him thus, all men will believe [33] in him: and the Romans will come and take our country and people.
John xi. 49.And one of them, who was called Caiaphas, the chief priest he was in that year, said unto them, [34]
John xi. 50.Ye know not anything, nor consider that it is more advantageous for us that one [35] man should die instead of the people, and not that the whole people perish.
John xi. 51.And this he said not of himself: but because he was the chief priest of
So both mss.; but the Vat. ms. had originally a reading equivalent to the text above with of omitted. that year, he [36] prophesied that Jesus was to die instead of the people;
John xi. 52.and not instead of the people alone, but that he might gather the scattered children of God together. [37]
John xi. 53.And from that day they considered how to kill him.

[38] [Arabic, p. 146]
John xi. 54.And Jesus did not walk openly amongst the Jews, but departed thence to a place near the wilderness, to a town
The Arabic word as printed (following Vat. ms.) means a place for monks to live in, but we should certainly restore a diacritical point over the last letter, and thus obtain another Syriac loan-word (that used here in the Peshitta), meaning town. See also Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary, ad loc. called Ephraim; and he was there, going [39] about with his disciples.
John xi. 55.And the passover of the Jews was near: and many went [40] up from the villages unto Jerusalem before the feast, to purify themselves.
John xi. 56.And they sought for Jesus, and said one to another in the temple, What think ye of his [41] holding back from the feast?
John xi. 57.And the chief priests and the Pharisees had given commandment, that, if any man knew in what place he was, he should reveal it to them, that they might take him.

[42]
Luke ix. 51.And when the days of his going up were accomplished, he prepared himself that [43] he might go
The present Arabic reading in going could pretty easily arise from that assumed in the translation above. to Jerusalem.
Luke ix. 52.And he sent messengers before him, and departed,
This and the following verb are singular in the printed Arabic (against the versions), although Ciasca renders them plural. A copyist using a carelessly written Arabic exemplar might conceivably overlook the plural terminations. Besides, they are often omitted in Syriac mss. and [44] entered into a village
cf. note, § 1, 40. of Samaria, that they might make ready for him.
Luke ix. 53.And they [45] received him not, because he
Lit. his body. was prepared for going to Jerusalem.
Luke ix. 54.And when James and John his disciples saw it, they said unto him, Our Lord, wilt thou that we speak, and fire come down from heaven, to extirpate them, as did Elijah also? [46]
Luke ix. 55.And Jesus turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not of what spirit ye are. [47]
Luke ix. 56.Verily the Son of man did not come to destroy lives, but to give life. And they went to another village.

div3.title: Section XXXIX.
div3.p:
[1]
John xii. 1.And Jesus six days before the passover
cf. the Greek phrase. came to Bethany, where was Lazarus, [2] whom Jesus raised from among the dead.
John xii. 2.And they made
Lit. he made (cf. first note to § 38, 43, last sentence). a feast for him there: [3] and Martha was serving; while Lazarus was one of them that sat with him.
Mark xiv. 3a.And [4] at the time of Jesus’ being at Bethany in the house of Simon the leper,
John xii. 9.great multitudes of the Jews heard that Jesus was there: and they came, not because of Jesus alone, but [Arabic, p. 147] that they might look also on Lazarus, whom he raised from among the dead. [5, 6]
John xii. 10.And the chief priests considered how they might kill Lazarus also;
John xii. 11.because [7] many of the Jews were going on his account, and believing in Jesus.
John xii. 3a.And Mary took a case of the ointment of fine nard, of great price,
Mark xiv. 3b.and opened it, and poured [8] it out on the head of Jesus as he was reclining;
John xii. 3b.and she anointed his feet, and wiped them with her hair: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment. [9, 10]
John xii. 4.But Judas Iscariot, one of the disciples, he that was to betray him, said,
John xii. 5.Why was [11] not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given unto the poor?
John xii. 6.This he said, not because of his care for the poor, but because he was a thief, and the chest [12] was with him, and what was put
Lit. fell (cf. § 25, 18). into it he used to bear.
Mark xiv. 4.And that displeased the rest of the disciples also within themselves, and they said, Why went this ointment [13] to waste?
Matt. xxvi. 9.It was possible that it should be sold for much, and the poor be given [14] it.
Mark xiv. 5b.And they were angry with
Or, spake angrily to. Mary.
Matt. xxvi. 10a.And Jesus perceived it, and said unto them,
Mark xiv. 6b.Leave her; why molest ye her? a good work hath she accomplished on me:
John xii. 7b.for the [15] day of my burial kept she it.
John xii. 8a.At all times the poor are with you, and when ye [16] wish ye can do them a kindness:
Mark xiv. 7b.but I am not at all times with you.
Matt. xxvi. 12.And for this cause, when she poured
Lit. cast, as in Greek. this ointment on my body, it is as if she did it for my burial, [17] and anointed my body beforehand.
Mark xiv. 8b; Mark xiv. 9.And verily I say unto you, In every place where this my gospel shall be proclaimed in all the world, what she did shall be told for a memorial of her.

[18, 19] [Arabic, p. 148]
Luke xix. 28.And when Jesus said that, he went out leisurely to go to Jerusalem.
Luke xix. 29a; Matt. xxi. 1b.And when he arrived at Bethphage and at Bethany, beside the mount which is [20] called the mount of Olives,
Matt. xxi. 2a; Mark xi. 2b.Jesus sent two of his disciples, and he said unto them, Go [21] into this village that is opposite you:
Matt. xxi. 2b; Luke xix. 30b.and when ye enter it, ye shall find an ass tied, and [22] a colt with him,
Sic. which no man ever yet mounted: loose him, and bring them
Dual in Arabic. unto me.
Matt. xxi. 2c; Luke xix. 31a.And if any man say unto you, Why loose ye them? say unto him thus, We [23] seek them for our Lord; and straightway send them hither.
Matt. xxi. 3b; Matt. xxi. 4.All this was, that what was said in the prophet might be fulfilled, which said,

[24]
Matt. xxi. 5.Say ye unto the daughter of Zion,
Behold, thy King cometh unto thee,
Meek, and riding upon an ass,
And upon a colt the foal of an ass.

[25]
John xii. 16.And the disciples did not know this at that time: but after that Jesus was glorified, his disciples remembered that these things were written of him, and that this [26] they had done unto him.
Matt. xxi. 6a; Luke xix. 32b.And when the two disciples went, they found as he had [27] said unto them, and they did as Jesus charged them.
Matt. xxi. 6b; Luke xix. 33.And when they loosed them, [28] their owners said unto them, Why loose ye them?
Luke xix. 34.They said unto them, We seek [29] them for our Lord.
Mark xi. 6b; Matt. xxi. 7.And they let them go. And they brought the ass and the colt, [30] and they placed on the colt their garments; and Jesus mounted it.
Matt. xxi. 8.And most of the multitudes spread their garments on the ground before him: and others cut branches [31] from the trees, and threw them in the way.
Luke xix. 37.And when he neared his
The Syriac versions have the. descent from [Arabic, p. 149] the mount of Olives, all the disciples began to rejoice and to praise God with [32] a loud voice for all the powers which they had seen;
Matt. xxi. 9b [or better Luke xix. 38a.].and they said, Praise in the highest; Praise to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name [33] of the Lord;
Mark xi. 10a.and blessed
Or, and, Blessed. is the kingdom that cometh, that of
The Arabic has to, but it probably represents the Syriac text with the meaning given above. our father David:
Luke xix. 38c.Peace in heaven, and praise in the highest.

[34]
John xii. 12b.And a great multitude, that which came to the feast, when they heard that Jesus [35] was coming to Jerusalem, took young palm branches,
Lit. the heart (or, pith) of the palm. The word pith, which occurs also in the Æhiopic version (Ezek. xxvii. 25; Jubilees, ch. 16) and in Ibn-at-Tayyib’s exposition, though not in the Brit. Mus. gospel text, is perhaps used here of the inner branches from its resemblance to the post-biblical Hebrew word employed in accounts of the Feast of Tabernacles.
John xii. 13.and went forth to meet him, and cried and said, Praise: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, the [36] King of Israel.
Luke xix. 39.Certain therefore of the Pharisees from among the multitudes [37] said unto him, Our Master, rebuke thy disciples.
Luke xix. 40.He said unto them, Verily I say unto you, If these were silent, the stones would cry out.

[38, 39]
Luke xix. 41.And when he drew near, and saw the city, he wept over it, and said,
Luke xix. 42.Would that thou hadst known the things that are
Lit. are found, a rendering due to the Syriac. for thy peace, in this thy day! now that is [40] hidden from thine eyes.
Luke xix. 43.There shall come unto thee days when thine enemies [41] shall encompass thee, and straiten thee from every quarter,
Luke xix. 44.and shall get possession of
So Ciasca’s text, following Vat. ms. The other ms. has drag, which by restoring a diacritical point to the third radical would give destroy, the reading of the Syriac versions. Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary has hide. thee, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee a stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.

[42]
Matt. xxi. 10.And when he entered into Jerusalem, the whole city was agitated, and they said, [43] Who is this?
Matt. xxi. 11.And the multitudes said, This is Jesus, the prophet that is from Nazareth [44] of Galilee.
John xii. 17.And the multitude which was with him bare witness that he called [45] Lazarus from the grave, and raised him from among the dead.
John xii. 18.And for this cause great multitudes went out to meet him, because they heard the sign which he did.

div3.title: Section XL.
div3.p:
[1] [Arabic, p. 150]
Matt. xxi. 14.And when Jesus entered the temple, they brought unto him blind and [2] lame: and he healed them.
Matt. xxi. 15.But when the chief priests and the Pharisees saw the wonders that he did, and the children that were crying in the temple and [3] saying, Praise be to the Son of David: it distressed them,
Matt. xxi. 16.and they said, Hearest thou not what these say? Jesus said unto them, Yea: did ye not read long ago, From [4] the mouths of children and infants thou hast chosen my praise?
John xii. 19.And the Pharisees said one to another, Behold, do ye not see that nothing availeth us? for lo, the whole world hath followed him.

[5]
John xii. 20.And there were among them certain Gentiles also, which had come up to worship [6] at the feast:
John xii. 21.these therefore came to Philip, who was of Bethsaida of Galilee, [7] and asked him, and said unto him, My lord, we wish to see Jesus.
John xii. 22.And Philip [8] came and told Andrew: and Andrew and Philip told Jesus.
John xii. 23.And Jesus answered and said unto them, The hour is come nigh, in which the Son of man is to be glorified. [9]
John xii. 24.Verily, verily, I say unto you, A grain of wheat, if it fall not and die in the [10] earth, remaineth alone; but if it die, it beareth much fruit.
John xii. 25.He that loveth his life
Or, soul; or, self. destroyeth it; and he that hateth his life
Or, soul; or, self. in this world shall keep it unto the life eternal. [11]
John xii. 26.If a man serve me, he will follow me; and where I am, there shall my servant be [12] also: and whosoever serveth me, the Father will honour him.
John xii. 27.Now is my soul troubled: [Arabic, p. 151] and what shall I say? My Father, deliver me from this hour. But [13] for this cause came I unto this hour.
John xii. 28.My Father, glorify thy name. And a [14] voice was heard from heaven, I have glorified it, and shall glorify it.
John xii. 29.And the multitude that were standing heard, and said, This is thunder: and others said, An [15] angel speaketh to him.
John xii. 30.Jesus answered and said unto them, Not because of me [16] was this voice, but because of you.
John xii. 31.Now is the judgement of this world; and the [17] prince of this world shall now be cast forth.
John xii. 32.And I, when I am lifted up from the [18] earth, shall draw every man unto me.
John xii. 33.This he said, that he might shew by what [19] manner of death he should die.
John xii. 34.The multitudes said unto him, We have heard out of the law that the Messiah abideth for ever: how then sayest thou, that the Son of [20] man is to be lifted up? who is this, the Son of man?
John xii. 35.Jesus said unto them, Another little while is the light with you. Walk so long as ye have light, lest the darkness overtake you; for he that walketh in the darkness knoweth not whither he goeth. [21]
John xii. 36.So long as ye have light, believe the light, that ye may be the children of the light.

[22]
Luke xvii. 20.And when certain of the Pharisees asked of Jesus, when the kingdom of God should come, he answered and said unto them, The kingdom of God cometh not
[23] with expectation:
Luke xvii. 21.neither shall they say, Lo, it is here! nor, Lo, it is there! for the kingdom of God is within you.

[24]
Luke xxi. 37.And in the daytime he was teaching in the temple; and at night he used to go [25] out, and pass the night in the mount called the mount of Olives.
Luke xxi. 38.And all the people came
i.e., used to come. to him in the morning in the temple, to hear his word.

[26, 27]
Matt. xxiii. 1.Then spake Jesus unto the multitudes and his disciples, and said unto them,
Matt. xxiii. 2.On [28] [Arabic, p. 152] the seat of Moses are seated the scribes and Pharisees:
Matt. xxiii. 3.everything that they say unto you now to keep, keep and do: but according to their deeds [29] do ye not; for they say, and do not.
Matt. xxiii. 4.And they bind heavy burdens, and lay them on the shoulders of the people; while they with one of their fingers will not come [30, 31] near
Or, touch. them.
Matt. xxiii. 5a.But all their deeds they do to make a shew before men.
Mark xii. 37b.And all the multitude were hearing that with pleasure.

[32]
Mark xii. 38.And in the course of his teaching he said unto them, Guard yourselves from the [33] scribes, who desire to walk in robes,
Mark xii. 39.and love salutation in the marketplaces, and sitting in the highest places of the synagogues, and at feasts in the highest parts of [34] the rooms:
Matt. xxiii. 5b.and they broaden their amulets, and lengthen the cords of their cloaks, [35]
Matt. xxiii. 7b.and love that they should be called by men, My master,
Mark xii. 40.and devour widows’ houses, because
The Syriac word means on the pretext of as well as because of (cf. § 50, 11, note). of their prolonging their prayers; these then shall receive greater judgement. [36]
Matt. xxiii. 8.But ye, be ye not called masters:
This word is not spelled in the ordinary way. Doubtless we should supply two diacritical points and read, with the Syriac versions, My master. for your master is one; all ye are brethren. [37]
Matt. xxiii. 9.Call not then to yourselves any one
cf. Peshitta. father on earth: for your Father is one, who is [38] in heaven.
Matt. xxiii. 10.And be not called directors: for your director is one, even the Messiah. [39, 40]
Matt. xxiii. 11.He that is great among you shall be unto you a minister.
Matt. xxiii. 12.Whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and whosoever shall abase himself shall be exalted.

[41]
Luke xi. 43.Woe unto you, Pharisees! because ye love the highest places in the synagogues, and salutation in the marketplaces.

[42]
Matt. xxiii. 14.Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye devour widows’ houses, because
Syriac, same as in § 40, 35; Arabic different. of your prolonging your prayers: for this reason then ye shall receive greater judgement.

[43]
Matt. xxiii. 13a.Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye have shut the kingdom of God before men.

[44] [Arabic, p. 153]
Luke xi. 52a.Woe unto you that know the law! for ye concealed the keys of knowledge:
Matt. xxiii. 13b.ye enter not, and those that are entering ye suffer not to enter.

[45]
Matt. xxiii. 15.Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because
Adopting the reading of Borg. ms. (cf. next verse). ye compass land and sea to draw
Perhaps this reading is due to the easy confusion of d and r in Syriac; but it might also conceivably be a corruption of the Arabic word in the next clause. It occurs also in the text of Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary. one proselyte; and when he is become so, ye make him a son of hell twice as much
Doubtless the Arabic word should be read as a monosyllable, as in Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary. as yourselves.

[46]
Matt. xxiii. 16.Woe unto you, ye blind guides! because ye say, Whosoever sweareth by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever sweareth by the gold that is in the temple, [47] shall be condemned.
See § 10, 13.
Matt. xxiii. 17.Ye blind foolish ones: which is greater, the gold, or the [48] temple which sanctifieth the gold?
Matt. xxiii. 18.And, Whosoever sweareth by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever sweareth by the offering that is upon it, shall be condemned.
See § 10, 13. [49]
Matt. xxiii. 19.Ye blind foolish ones: which is greater, the offering, or the altar which sanctifieth [50] the offering?
Matt. xxiii. 20.Whosoever then sweareth by the altar, hath sworn by it, and by all [51] that is upon it.
Matt. xxiii. 21.And whosoever sweareth by the temple, hath sworn by it, and by [52] him that is dwelling in it.
Matt. xxiii. 22.And whosoever sweareth by heaven, hath sworn by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth upon it.

[53]
Matt. xxiii. 23.Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye tithe mint and rue and dill and cummin and all herbs, and ye leave the important matters of the law, judgement, and mercy, and faith, and the love of God: this ought ye to do, and [54] not to leave that undone.
Matt. xxiii. 24.Ye blind guides, which strain out a gnat, and swallow
The Arabic word as printed gives no suitable sense. Either the last radical has been omitted, or the last two radicals have exchanged places. camels.

[55]
Matt. xxiii. 25.Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye cleanse the outside
of the cup and of the platter, while the inside of them is full of injustice and wrong. [56]
Matt. xxiii. 26.Ye blind Pharisees, cleanse first the inside of the cup and of the platter, then shall the outside of them be cleansed.

[57] [Arabic, p. 154]
Matt. xxiii. 27.Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye resemble whited sepulchres, which appear
Lit. are seen. from the outside beautiful, but within [58] full of the bones of the dead, and all uncleanness.
Matt. xxiii. 28.So ye also from without appear unto men like the righteous, but within ye are full of wrong and hypocrisy.

[59]
Luke xi. 45.One of the scribes answered and said unto him, Teacher, in this saying of thine [60] thou art casting a slur on us.
Luke xi. 46.He said, And to you also, ye scribes, woe! for ye lade men with heavy burdens, and ye with one of your fingers come not near
Or, touch. those burdens.

[61]
Matt. xxiii. 29a; Luke xi. 47b; Matt. xxiii. 29b.Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye build the tombs of the prophets, which your fathers killed, and adorn the burying-places of the righteous, [62] and say,
Matt. xxiii. 30.If we had been in the days of our fathers, we should not have been partakers [63] with them in the blood of the prophets.
Matt. xxiii. 31.Wherefore, behold, ye witness against [64] yourselves, that ye are the children of those that slew the prophets.
Matt. xxiii. 32.And ye also, [65] ye fill up the measure
Lit. boundary or limit. of your fathers.
Matt. xxiii. 33.Ye serpents, ye children of vipers, where shall ye flee from the judgement of Gehenna?

div3.title: Section XLI.
div3.p:
[1]
Matt. xxiii. 34.Therefore, behold, I, the wisdom of God, am sending unto you prophets, and apostles, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall slay and crucify; and some of them ye shall beat in your synagogues, and persecute
cf. 8, 34. from city to [2] city:
Matt. xxiii. 35.that there may come on you all the blood of the righteous that hath been poured upon the ground
Or, earth. from the blood of Abel the pure to the blood of Zachariah the son of Barachiah, whom ye slew between the temple
Or, sanctuary. and the altar. [3]
Matt. xxiii. 36.Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.
See § 1, 49, note.

[4] [Arabic, p. 155]
Matt. xxiii. 37.O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, slayer of the prophets, and stoner of them that are sent unto her! how many times did I wish to gather thy children, as [5] a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
Matt. xxiii. 38.Your house shall [6] be left over you desolate.
Matt. xxiii. 39.Verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

[7]
John xii. 42.And many of the rulers also believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they [8] were not confessing him, lest they be put
Lit. become. out of the synagogue:
John xii. 43.and they loved [9] the praise of men more than the praising of God.
John xii. 44.And Jesus cried and said, [10] Whosoever believeth in me, believeth not in me, but in him that sent me.
John xii. 45.And [11] whosoever seeth me hath seen him that sent me.
John xii. 46.I am come a light
The text as it stands ought to mean I am a light. I am come; but it is a word-for-word reproduction of the Peshitta, and should therefore doubtless be rendered as above. into the [12] world, and so every one that believeth in me abideth not in the darkness.
John xii. 47.And whosoever heareth my sayings, and keepeth them not, I judge him not: for I came [13] not to judge the world, but to give the world life.
Or, to save the world (cf. § 1, 78, note).
John xii. 48.Whosoever wrongeth
See § 20, 28, note. me, and receiveth not my sayings, there is one that judgeth him: the word that I spake, it [14] shall judge him at the last day.
John xii. 49.I from myself did not speak: but the Father which sent me, he hath given me commandment,
Not the same word. what I should say, and what I [15] should speak; and I know that his commandment
Not the same word. is eternal life.
John xii. 50.The things that I say now, as my Father hath said unto me, even so I say.

[16]
Luke xi. 53.And when he said that unto them, the scribes and Pharisees began their evil-doing, being angry with him, and finding fault with his sayings, and harassing
So Ciasca, following Vat. ms. The true reading, however, is probably that underlying the Borg. ms. If we restore diacritical points to the radical letters we get deceiving (cf. § 41, 31), an alternative meaning (or the word laying wait for, used in the Peshitta. The Arabic follows the Peshitta very closely in this and the following verse. him [17] in many things;
Luke xi. 54.seeking to catch something from his mouth, that they might be able to calumniate him.

[18]
Luke xii. 1.And when there gathered together myriads of great multitudes, which almost trode
[Arabic, p. 156] one upon another, Jesus began to say unto his disciples, Preserve yourselves [19] from the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
Luke xii. 2.For there is nothing [20] concealed, that shall not be revealed: nor hid, that shall not be known.
Luke xii. 3.Everything that ye have said in the darkness shall be heard in the light; and what ye have spoken secretly in the ears in the inner chambers shall be proclaimed on the roofs.

[21, 22]
John xii. 36b.This said Jesus, and he went and hid himself from them.
John xii. 37.But notwithstanding [23] his having done all these signs before them, they believed not in him:
John xii. 38.that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, who said,
My Lord, who is he that hath believed to hear us?
And the arm of the Lord, to whom hath it appeared?

[24]
John xii. 39.And for this reason it is not possible for them to believe, because Isaiah also said,

[25]
John xii. 40.They have blinded their eyes, and made dark their heart;
That they may not see with their eyes, and understand with their heart,
And turn,
So that I should heal them.

[26]
John xii. 41.This said Isaiah when he saw his glory, and spake of him.

[27]
Matt. xxiv. 1.And when Jesus went out of the temple, certain of his disciples came forward [28] to shew
Or, and shewed. him the buildings of the temple,
Mark xiii. 1b; Luke xxi. 5b.and its beauty and greatness, and the strength of the stones that were laid in it, and the elegance of its building, and that [29] it was adorned with noble stones and beautiful colours.
Matt. xxiv. 2a.Jesus answered and said [30] unto them, See ye these great buildings?
Luke xix. 43a; Luke xix. 44b [or rather Matt. xxiv. 2b, or Mark xiii. 2b].verily I say unto you, Days will come, when there shall not be left here a stone upon another, that shall not be cast down.

[31]
Mark xiv. 1.And two days before
Lit. before two days would be (cf. Sin. and above, § 39, 1, note). the passover of unleavened bread, the chief priests and [32] the scribes sought how they might take him by deceit,
cf. § 41, 16, note. and kill him:
Mark xiv. 2.and they said, It shall not be at the feast, lest the people be agitated.

[33]
Mark xiii. 3.And when Jesus sat on the mount of Olives opposite the temple, his disciples, Simon Cephas and James and John and Andrew, came forward unto him, and said unto him [34] between themselves and him,
Luke xxi. 7b; Matt. xxiv. 3b.Teacher, tell us when that shall be, and what is the sign [35] [Arabic, p. 157] of thy coming and the end of the world.
Matt. xxiv. 4a; Luke xvii. 22b; Matt. xxiv. 4b.Jesus answered and said unto them, Days will come, when ye shall long to see one of the days of the Son of [36, 37]
Matt. xxiv. 5a.man, and shall not behold.
Luke xxi. 8b.Take heed lest any man lead you astray. Many shall [38] come in my name, and say, I am the Messiah;
Mark xiii. 6b; Luke xxi. 8c.and they shall say, The time is come [39] near, and shall lead many astray: go not therefore after them.
Mark xiii. 7a; Matt. xxiv. 7b; Luke xxi. 9b.And when ye hear of wars and tidings of insurrections, see to it, be
Or, that ye be, if we suppose the present text to have resulted from the loss of the second of two alifs. not agitated: for these things must [40] first be; only the end is not yet come.
Matt. xxiv. 7a.Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom [41] against kingdom:
Luke xxi. 11.and great earthquakes shall be in one place and another, and there shall be famines and deaths and agitations: and there shall be fear and terror and great signs that
Or, omit that. shall appear from heaven, and there shall be great [42, 43] storms
Matt. xxiv. 8.All these things are the beginning of travail.
Luke xxi. 12.But before all of that, they shall lay hands upon you, and persecute you, and deliver you unto the synagogues [44] and into prisons, and bring you before kings and judges for my name’s sake.
Luke xxi. 13.And [45] that shall be unto you for a witness.
Mark xiii. 10.But first must my gospel be preached unto all [46] nations.
Luke xii. 11.And when they bring you into the synagogues before the rulers and the authorities, be not anxious beforehand how ye shall answer for yourselves, or what ye [47, 48] shall say:
Mark xiii. 11b.because it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Spirit.
Luke xxi. 14.Lay it to your heart, not [49] [Arabic, p. 158] to be anxious before the time what ye shall say:
Luke xxi. 15.and I shall
The Arabic text lacks a letter. give you understanding and wisdom,
Borg. ms. reads you the fruits of wisdom. which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay. [50]
Matt. xxiv. 9.And then shall they deliver you unto constraint, and shall kill you: and ye shall be [51] hated of all nations because of my name.
Matt. xxiv. 30.And then shall many go astray,
See § 25, 17, note. and they [52] shall hate one another, and deliver one another unto death.
Luke xxi. 16.And your parents, and your brethren, and your kinsfolk, and your friends shall deliver you up, and shall [53, 54] slay some of you.
Luke xxi. 18.But a lock of hair from your heads shall not perish.
Luke xxi. 19.And by [55] your patience ye shall gain
Or, possess. your souls.
Matt. xxiv. 11.And many men,
So the Arabic text; but it doubtless simply represents the Syriac, which here agrees with the Greek. false prophets, shall arise, [56] and lead many astray.
Matt. xxiv. 12.And because of the abounding of iniquity, the love of many
[57] shall wax cold.
Matt. xxiv. 13.But he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.
Matt. xxiv. 14.And [58] this, the
So the Arabic text; but it doubtless simply represents the Syriac, which here agrees with the Greek. gospel of the kingdom, shall be preached in all the world for a testimony to all nations; and then shall come the end of all.

div3.title: Section XLII.
div3.p:
[1]
Luke xxi. 20.But when ye see Jerusalem with the army compassing it about, then know that [2] its desolation is come near.
Luke xxi. 21.Those then that are in Judæa at that time shall flee to the mountain; and those that are within her shall flee; and those that are in the [3] villages shall not enter her.
Luke xxi. 22.For these days are the days of vengeance, that all that [4] is written may be fulfilled.
Matt. xxiv. 15.And when ye see the unclean sign of desolation,
So Vat. ms., following the Peshitta. Ciasca follows Borg. ms., which by a change of diacritical points has the hardly grammatical reading, see that it is the desolation, the unclean thing spoken of. Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary supports Vat. ms. spoken of in Daniel the prophet, standing in the pure place, he that readeth shall understand, [5, 6]
Matt. xxiv. 16.and then he that is in Judæa shall flee in to the mountain:
Mark xiii. 15.and let him that is on the [7] roof not go down, nor enter in to take anything from his house:
Mark xiii. 16.and let him that is in [8] [Arabic, p. 159] the field not turn behind him to take his garment.
Luke xxi. 23.Woe to them that are with child and to them that give suck in those days! there shall be great [9] distress in the land, and wrath against this nation.
Luke xxi. 24.And they shall fall on the edge of the sword,
This word has a Syriac meaning given to it. In Arabic it means war. and shall be taken captive to every land: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the nations, until the times of the nations be ended.

[10]
Mark xiii. 21.Then if any man say unto you, The Messiah is here; or, Lo, he is there; believe [11] him not:
Matt. xxiv. 24.there shall rise then false Messiahs and prophets of lying, and shall do signs and wonders, in order that they may lead astray even the elect also, if they [12] be able.
Mark xiii. 23.But as for you, beware: for I have acquainted you with everything [13] beforehand.
Matt. xxiv. 26.If then they say unto you, Lo, he is in the desert; go not out, lest ye [14] be taken: and if they say unto you, Lo, he is in the chamber; believe not.
Matt. xxiv. 27.And as the lightning appeareth from the east, and is seen unto the west; so shall be the [15] coming of the Son of man.
Luke xvii. 25.But first he must suffer much and be rejected by this [16] generation.
cf. § 16, 2.
Matt. xxiv. 20.Pray therefore that your flight be not in winter, nor on a sabbath: [17]
Matt. xxiv. 21.there shall be then great tribulation,
Same Arabic (and Syriac) word as in § 41, 50. the like of which there hath not been from the [18] beginning of the world till now, nor shall be.
Mark xiii. 20.And except the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh would have lived: but because of the elect, whom he elected, [19] he shortened those days.
Luke xxi. 25.And there shall be signs in the sun and the moon and the stars; and upon the earth affliction
Same Arabic (and Syriac) word as in § 41, 50. of the nations, and rubbing of hands for the confusion
So the Borg. ms. The Vat. ms., followed by Ciasca, has grief. [20] [Arabic, p. 160] of the noise of the sea, and an earthquake:
Luke xxi. 26a.the souls of men shall [21] go forth from fear of that which is to come upon the earth.
Mark xiii. 24a; Matt. xxiv. 29.And in those days, straightway after the distress of those days, the sun shall become dark, and the moon shall not shew its light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers [22] of heaven shall be convulsed:
Matt. xxiv. 30.and then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and at that time all the tribes of the earth shall wail, and look unto the Son [23] of man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and much glory.
Matt. xxiv. 31.And he shall send his angels with the great trumpet, and they shall gather his elect from the four [24] winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
Lit. the end of heaven unto its end.
Luke xxi. 28.But when these things begin to be, be of good cheer, and lift up your heads; for your salvation
Or, deliverance. is come near.

[25]
Matt. xxiv. 32.Learn the example of the fig tree: when it letteth down its branches,
cf. Peshitta, which text the translator seems to have misread. and putteth [26] forth its leaves, ye know that the summer is come;
Matt. xxiv. 33.so ye also, when ye see these things begun to be, know ye that the kingdom of God hath arrived at the [27] door.
Matt. xxiv. 34.Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, until all these [28] things shall be.
Matt. xxiv. 35.Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my sayings shall not pass away.

[29]
Luke xxi. 34.Take heed to yourselves, that your hearts become not heavy with inordinate desire,
cf. Peshitta. and drunkenness, and the care of the world at any time, and that day come
[30] upon you suddenly:
Luke xxi. 35.for it is as a shock that shocks all the inhabitants that are on the [31] face of the whole earth.
Luke xxi. 36.Watch at all times, and pray, that ye may be worthy to escape [Arabic, p. 161] from all the things that are to be, and that ye may stand before the Son of [32] man.
Mark xiii. 32.Of that day and of that hour hath no man learned, not even the angels [33] of heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.
Mark xiii. 33.See ye, and watch and pray: for ye know [34] not when that time will be.
Mark xiii. 34.It is as a man, who journeyed, and left his house, and gave his authority to his servants, and appointed every man to his work, and [35] charged the porter to be wakeful.
Mark xiii. 35.Be wakeful then:
cf. § 9, 21. since ye know not when the lord of the house cometh, in the evening, or in the middle of the night, or when the [36] cock croweth, or in the morning;
Mark xiii. 36.lest he come unexpectedly, and find you sleeping. [37]
Mark xiii. 37.The thing that I say unto you, unto all of you do I say it, Be ye watchful.

[38]
Matt. xxiv. 37.For as it was in the days of Noah, so shall the coming of the Son of man be. [39]
Matt. xxiv. 38.As they were before the flood eating and drinking, and taking wives, and giving [40] wives to men,
Matt. xxiv. 39.until the day in which Noah entered into the ark, and they perceived not till the flood came, and took them all; so shall the coming of the Son of man [41] be.
Luke xvii. 28.And as it was in the days of Lot; they were eating and drinking, and selling [42] and buying, and planting and building,
Luke xvii. 29.on the day in which Lot went out from Sodom, and the Lord rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them [43, 44] all:
Luke xvii. 30.so shall it be in the day in which the Son of man is revealed.
Or, appeareth.
Luke xvii. 31.And in that day, whosoever is on the roof, and his garments
cf. § 14, 24 note. in the house, let him not go down to [45] take them: and he that is in the field shall not turn behind him.
Luke xvii. 32.Remember Lot’s [46] wife.
Luke xvii. 33.Whosoever shall desire to save his life shall destroy it: but whosoever shall [47] destroy his life shall save it.
Luke xvii. 34.Verily I say unto you, In that night there shall be two on [48] [Arabic, p. 162] one bed; one shall be taken, and another left.
Luke xvii. 35.And two women shall be grinding [49] at one mill; one shall be taken, and another left.
Luke xvii. 36.And two shall be in the [50] field; one shall be taken, and another left.
Luke xvii. 37.They answered and said unto him, To what place, our Lord? He said unto them, Where the body is, there will the eagles [51, 52] gather.
Matt. xxiv. 42.Be attentive now: for ye know not at what hour your Lord cometh.
Matt. xxiv. 43.Know this: if the master of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have been attentive, and would not make it possible that his house should be [53] broken through.
Matt. xxiv. 44.Therefore be ye also ready: for in the hour that ye think not the Son of man cometh.

div3.title: Section XLIII.
div3.p:
[1]
Luke xii. 41.Simon Cephas said unto him, Our Lord, is it to us that thou hast spoken this [2] parable, or also to every man?
Luke xii. 42a [Borg. ms. omits Luke xii. 42a]; Matt. xxiv. 45.Jesus said unto him, Who, thinkest thou, is the servant, the master of the house,
i.e., the steward. trusted with control,
Borg. ms. has trusted and faithful. Doubtless we should supply diacritical points to the reading of Vat. ms., and translate trusted and wise. Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary, however, has both and wise and the word translated with control, used in a different sense. whom his lord set over his [3] household, to give them their food in its season?
Matt. xxiv. 46.Blessed is that servant, whom his [4] lord shall come and find having done so.
Luke xii. 44a; Matt. xxiv. 47b.Verily I say unto you, He will set him [5] over all that he hath.
Matt. xxiv. 48; Luke xii. 45b.But if that evil servant say in his heart, My lord delayeth his [6] coming;
Matt. xxiv. 49b.and shall begin to beat his servants and the maidservants of his lord, and [7] shall begin to eat and to drink with the drunken;
Matt. xxiv. 50.the lord of that servant shall come [8] in the day that he thinketh not, and in the hour that he knoweth not,
Matt. xxiv. 51a.and shall [Arabic, p. 163] judge him, and appoint his portion with the hypocrites,
Luke xii. 46b.and with those that are not faithful:
Matt. xxiv. 51b.there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

[9]
Matt. xxv. 1.Then shall the kingdom of heaven be like unto ten virgins, those that took their [10] lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom and the bride.
Matt. xxv. 2.Five of them were [11] wise, and five foolish.
Matt. xxv. 3.And those foolish ones took their lamps, and took not with [12, 13] them oil:
Matt. xxv. 4.but those wise ones took oil in vessels along with their lamps.
Matt. xxv. 5.When then [14] the bridegroom delayed, they all slumbered and slept.
Matt. xxv. 6.But in the middle of the night there occurred a cry, Behold, the bridegroom cometh! Go forth therefore to [15, 16] meet him.
Matt. xxv. 7.Then all those virgins arose, and made ready their lamps.
Matt. xxv. 8.The foolish [17] said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out.
Matt. xxv. 9.But those wise answered and said, Perhaps
See § 10, 17, and § 4, 24, note. there will not be enough for us and you: but go ye to
[18] the sellers, and buy for yourselves.
Matt. xxv. 10.And when they went away to buy, the bridegroom came; and those that were ready went in with him to the marriage feast: and [19] the door was shut.
Matt. xxv. 11.And at last those other virgins also came and said, Our Lord, [20] our Lord, open unto us.
Matt. xxv. 12.He answered and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, [21] I know you not.
Matt. xxv. 13.Watch then, for ye know not that day nor that hour.

[22]
Matt. xxv. 14.It is as a man, who went on a journey, and called his servants, and delivered unto [23] them his possessions.
Matt. xxv. 15.And unto one he gave five talents,
cf. § 27, 2, note. and another two, and another [24] one; every one according to his strength; and went on his journey forthwith.
Matt. xxv. 16.He [Arabic, p. 164] then that received the five talents went and traded with them, and gained [26] other five.
Matt. xxv. 17.And so also he of the two gained other two.
Matt. xxv. 18.But he that received [27] the one went and digged in the earth, and hid the money of his lord.
Matt. xxv. 19.And after a long time the lord of those servants came, and took from them the account. [28]
Matt. xxv. 20.And he that received five talents came near and brought other five, and said, My lord, thou gavest me five talents: lo, I have gained other five in addition to them. [29]
Matt. xxv. 21.His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: over a little hast [30] thou been faithful, over much will I set thee: enter into the joy of thy lord.
Matt. xxv. 22.And he that had the two came near and said, My lord, thou gavest me two talents: lo, [31] other two have I gained in addition to them.
Matt. xxv. 23.His lord said unto him, Good,
A Persian word. The Vat. ms. omits it. thou faithful servant: over a little hast thou been faithful, over much will I set thee: enter [32] into the joy of thy lord.
Matt. xxv. 24.And he also that received the one talent came forward and said, My lord, I knew thee that thou art a severe man, who reapest where thou [33] sowest not, and gatherest where thou didst not scatter:
Matt. xxv. 25.and so I was afraid, and [34] went away and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, thou hast what is thine.
Matt. xxv. 26.His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest me [35] that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I did not scatter;
Matt. xxv. 27.it was incumbent on thee to put my money to the bank,
Lit. table (cf. Peshitta). and then I should come and seek it with its [36] gains.
Matt. xxv. 28.Take now from him the talent, and give it to him that hath ten talents. [37]
Matt. xxv. 29.Whosoever hath shall be given, and he shall have more: but he that hath not, even [38] [Arabic, p. 165] what he hath shall be taken from him.
Matt. xxv. 30.And the unprofitable servant, put him forth into the outer darkness: there shall be the weeping and gnashing of teeth.

[39, 40]
Luke xii. 35.Your loins shall be girded, and your lamps lit;
Luke xii. 36.and ye shall be like the people that are looking for their lord, when he shall return from the feast; so that, when [41] he cometh and knocketh, they may at once open unto him.
Luke xii. 37.Blessed are those servants, whom their lord shall come and find attentive: verily I say unto you, that he will gird his waist, and make them sit down, and pass through
cf. Peshitta (and Greek). them and serve [42] them.
Luke xii. 38.And if he come in the second watch, or the third, and find thus, blessed are those servants.

[43]
Matt. xxv. 31.But when the Son of man cometh in his glory, and all his pure angels with him, [44] then shall he sit on the throne of his glory:
Matt. xxv. 32.and he will gather before him all the nations, and separate them the one from the other, like the shepherd who separateth [45] the sheep from the goats;
Matt. xxv. 33.and will set
Or, and setteth; but the Peshitta confirms the rendering given above. the sheep on his right, and the goats on his [46] left.
Matt. xxv. 34.Then shall the King say to those that are at his right, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundations
cf. § 17, 17, note. of the world: [47]
Matt. xxv. 35.I hungered, and ye gave me to eat; and I thirsted, and ye gave me to drink; and I [48] was a stranger, and ye took me in;
Matt. xxv. 36.and I was naked, and ye clothed me; and I [49] was sick, and ye visited me; and I was in prison, and ye cared for me.
Matt. xxv. 37.Then shall those righteous say unto him, Our Lord, when saw we thee hungry, and fed thee? [50] or thirsty, and gave thee to drink?
Matt. xxv. 38.And when saw we thee a stranger, and took [51] thee in? or naked, and clothed thee?
Matt. xxv. 39.And when saw we thee sick, or imprisoned, and [52] cared for thee?
Matt. xxv. 40.The King shall answer and say
Perfect tenses, as in Peshitta. unto them, Verily I say unto you, What [53] [Arabic, p. 166] ye did to one of these my brethren, the little ones, ye did unto me.
Matt. xxv. 41.Then shall he say unto those that are on his left also, Depart from me, ye cursed, [54] into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his hosts:
Matt. xxv. 42.I hungered, and ye fed me [55] not; and I thirsted, and ye did not give me to drink;
Matt. xxv. 43.and I was a stranger, and ye
took me not in; and I was naked, and ye clothed me not; and I was sick, and imprisoned, [56] and ye visited me not.
Matt. xxv. 44.Then shall those also answer and say, Our Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, or athirst, or naked, or a stranger, or sick, or imprisoned, [57] and did not minister unto thee?
Matt. xxv. 45.Then shall he answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, When ye did it not unto one of these little ones, ye did it not [58] unto me also.
Matt. xxv. 46.And these shall go away into eternal punishment: but the righteous into eternal life.

div3.title: Section XLIV.
div3.p:
[1, 2]
Matt. xxvi. 1.And when Jesus
Borg. ms., the Lord Jesus. finished all these sayings, he said unto his disciples,
Matt. xxvi. 2.Ye know that after two days will be the passover, and the Son of man is delivered up to be [3] crucified.
Matt. xxvi. 3.Then gathered together the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders [4] of the people, unto the court of the chief priest, who was called Caiaphas;
Matt. xxvi. 4.and they took counsel together concerning Jesus, that they might seize him by subtilty, and [5] kill him.
Matt. xxvi. 5.But they said, Not during the feast, lest there take place a disturbance among the people;
Luke xxii. 2b.for they feared the people.

[6]
Luke xxii. 3.And Satan entered into Judas who was called Iscariot, who was of the number [7] of the twelve.
Luke xxii. 4a; Matt. xxvi. 15a.And he went away, and communed with the chief priests, and the scribes, and those that held command in the temple, and said unto them, What [8] [Arabic, p. 167] would ye pay me, and I will deliver him unto you?
Mark xiv. 11a; Matt. xxvi. 15b.And they, when they heard it, were pleased, and made ready
Probably the letter that stands for and should be repeated, and the phrase rendered and appointed. for him thirty pieces of money.
So Vat. ms. (following Peshitta) and Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary. Borg. ms., followed by Ciasca, has dirhams of money. [9]
Luke xxii. 6.And he promised
Lit. became responsible unto. Syriac versions as in text above (cf. § 44, 33). them, and from that time he sought an opportunity
The Arabic (lit. a stumbling or a cause of stumbling) doubtless represents the Syriac. that he might deliver unto them Jesus without the multitude.

[10]
Mark xiv. 12.And on the first day of unleavened bread the disciples came to Jesus, and said unto him, Where wilt thou that we go and make ready for thee that thou mayest eat the passover?

[11]
John xiii. 1.And before the feast of the passover, Jesus knew that the hour was arrived for his departure from this world unto his Father; and he loved his own in this world, [12] and to the last he loved them.
John xiii. 2.And at the time of the feast, Satan put into the [13] heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to deliver him up.
John xiii. 3.And Jesus, because he knew that the Father had delivered into his hands everything, and that he came [14] forth from the Father, and goeth unto God,
John xiii. 4.rose from supper, and laid aside his [15] garments;
John xiii. 5.and took a towel, and girded his waist, and poured water into a bason, and began to wash the feet of his disciples, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith [16] his waist was girded.
John xiii. 6.And when he came to Simon Cephas, Simon said unto [17] him, Dost thou, my Lord, wash for me my feet?
John xiii. 7.Jesus answered and said unto [18] him, What I do, now thou knowest not; but afterwards thou shalt learn.
John xiii. 8.Simon said unto him, Thou shalt never wash for me my feet. Jesus said unto him, If I [19] wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.
John xiii. 9.Simon Cephas said unto him, Then, my [20] Lord, wash not for me my feet alone, but my hands also and my head.
John xiii. 10.Jesus said unto him, He that batheth
The Arabic word means swimmeth. The Syriac versions have is bathed, which Borg. ms. misreads bathed, and Vat. ms. (followed by Ciasca) corrupts into batheth, rendering it swimmeth. needeth not to wash save his feet, whereas his whole [21] body is clean: and ye also are clean, but not all of you.
John xiii. 11.For Jesus knew him that should betray him; therefore said he, Ye are not all clean.

[22] [Arabic, p. 168]
John xiii. 12.So when he had washed their feet, he took his garments, and sat down, and [23] said unto them, Know ye what I have done unto you?
John xiii. 13.Ye call me, Master, [24] and, Lord: and ye say well; so I am.
John xiii. 14.If then I, now, who am your Lord and Master, have washed for you your feet, how needful is it that ye should wash one another’s feet! [25]
John xiii. 15.This have I given you as an example, that as I have done to you so ye should do [26] also.
John xiii. 16.Verily, verily, I say unto you, No servant is greater than his lord; nor an [27] apostle greater than he that sent him.
John xiii. 17.If ye know that, ye are happy if ye do it. [28]
John xiii. 18.My saying this
Or, This my saying. is not for all of you: for I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture might be fulfilled, He that eateth with me bread lifted against me his
[29] heel.
John xiii. 19.Henceforth I say unto you before it come to pass, that, when it cometh to [30] pass, ye may believe that I am he.
John xiii. 20.Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and whosoever receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.

[31]
Luke xxii. 27.Who is the great one, he that sitteth, or he that serveth? is it not he that sitteth? [32]
Luke xxii. 28.I am among you as he that serveth.
Luke xxii. 29.But ye are they that have continued with me [33] in my temptations;
Luke xxii. 30.I promise
cf. § 44, 9, note. you, as my Father promised
cf. § 44, 9, note. me, the kingdom, that ye may eat and drink at the table of my kingdom.

[34]
Luke xxii. 7.And the first day
Vat. ms. has the word day on the margin, added by a late hand. came, the feast of unleavened bread, on which the Jews were [35] wont
The misprint in the Arabic text has been overlooked in the list of Corrigenda. to sacrifice
Or, kill. the passover.
Luke xxii. 8.And Jesus sent two of his disciples, Cephas and John, and said unto them, Go and make ready for us the passover, that we may eat. [36, 37]
Luke xxii. 9.And they said unto him, Where wilt thou that we make ready for thee?
Luke xxii. 10a.He said unto them, Go, enter the city;
Mark xiv. 13b; Luke xxii. 10b.and at the time of your entering, there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water;
Luke xxii. 11a.follow him, and the place where he entereth, say [38] to such an one, the master of the house,
Matt. xxvi. 18b.Our Master saith, My time is come, and [Arabic, p. 169] at thy house I keep the passover.
Luke xxii. 11b.Where then is the lodging-place where [39] I shall eat with my disciples?
Luke xxii. 12.And he will shew you a large upper room [40] spread and made ready:
Mark xiv. 15.there then make ready for us.
Mark xiv. 16.And his two disciples went out, and came to the city, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover as he had said unto them.

[41]
Luke xxii. 14.And when the evening was come, and the time arrived, Jesus came and reclined, [42] and the twelve apostles with him.
Luke xxii. 15.And he said unto them, With desire I have [43] desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer:
Luke xxii. 16.I say unto you, that henceforth I shall not eat it, until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.

[44]
John xiii. 21a.Jesus said that, and was agitated
The Syriac word is retained. In Arabic it properly means become strong or proud (cf. § 38, 17). in his spirit, and testified, and said, Verily, [45] verily, I say unto you, One of you, he that eateth with me, shall betray me.
Mark xiv. 18b; Mark xiv. 19.And they were very sorrowful; and they began to say unto him, one after another of [46] them, Can it be I, Lord?
Mark xiv. 20.He answered and said unto them, One of the twelve, [47] he that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, will betray me.
Luke xxii. 21.And lo, the hand of [48] him that betrayeth me is on the table.
Mark xiv. 21.And the Son of man goeth, as it is written of him: woe then to that man by whose hand the Son of man is betrayed! for it [49] would have been better for that man had he not been born.
John xiii. 22.And the disciples [50] looked one on another, for they knew not to whom he referred;
Luke xxii. 23.and they began to search among themselves, who that might be who was to do this.

div3.title: Section XLV.
div3.p:
[1, 2] [Arabic, p. 170]
John xiii. 23.And one of his disciples was sitting
The Syriac versions have reclining. in his bosom, he whom Jesus loved.
John xiii. 24.To him Simon Cephas beckoned, that he should ask him who this was, concerning [3] whom he spake.
John xiii. 25.And that disciple leaned
Lit. fell. on Jesus’ breast, and said unto him, [4] My Lord, who is this?
John xiii. 26.Jesus answered and said, He to whom I shall dip bread, and give it. And Jesus dipped bread, and gave to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. [5]
John xiii. 27.And after the bread, Satan entered him. And Jesus said unto him, What thou [6] desirest to do, hasten the doing of it.
John xiii. 28.And no man of them that sat knew why he [7] said this unto him.
John xiii. 29.And some of them thought, because Judas had the box, that he was bidding him buy what would be needed for the feast; or, that he might pay [8] something to the poor.
Matt. xxvi. 25.Judas the betrayer answered and said, Can it be I, my [9] Master? Jesus said unto him, Thou hast said.
John xiii. 30.And Judas took the bread straightway, and went forth without: and it was still night.

[10]
John xiii. 31.And Jesus said, Now is the Son of man being glorified,
A simple change of diacritical points would give the reading of the Greek and of the Syriac versions. and God is being glorified
A simple change of diacritical points would give the reading of the Greek and of the Syriac versions. [11] in him;
John xiii. 32.and if God is glorified in him, God also will glorify him in him, and straightway will glorify him.

[12]
Mark xiv. 22a.And while they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed, and divided;
Matt. xxvi. 26b.and he
[13] gave to his disciples, and said unto them, Take and eat; this is my body.
Mark xiv. 23a.And he [Arabic, p. 171] took a cup, and gave thanks, and blessed, and gave them,
Matt. xxvi. 27b.and said, Take [14, 15] and drink of it, all of you.
Mark xiv. 23b.And they drank of it, all of them.
Mark xiv. 24a.And he said unto them,
Matt. xxvi. 28.This is my blood, the new covenant, that is shed for many for the [16] forgiveness of sins.
Matt. xxvi. 29.I say unto you, I shall not drink henceforth of this, the juice of the vine, until the day in which I drink
Peshitta adds it. The reading of the Sinaitic is doubtful. with you new wine in the kingdom of [17] God.
Luke xxii. 19b.And thus do ye in remembrance of me.
Luke xxii. 31.And Jesus said unto Simon, Simon, [18] behold, Satan asketh that he may sift you like wheat:
Luke xxii. 32.but I entreat
Past tense in Syriac versions. for thee, that thou lose not thy faith:
We may translate, with the Syriac versions, that thy faith fail not, only if we assign a somewhat Syriac meaning to the verb, and assume either an error in diacritical points (t for y) or an unusual (Syriac) gender for faith. and do thou, at some time, turn
cf. Syriac versions. and strengthen thy brethren.

[19]
John xiii. 33.My children, another little while am I with you. And ye shall seek me: and as [20] I said unto the Jews, Whither I go, ye cannot come; I say unto you now also.
John xiii. 34.A new commandment I give you, that ye may love one another; and as I have loved [21] you, so shall ye also love one another.
John xiii. 35.By this shall every man know that ye are [22] my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
John xiii. 36.Simon Cephas said unto him, Our Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered and said unto him, Whither I go, thou canst not now follow me; but later thou shalt come.

[23]
Matt. xxvi. 31.Then said Jesus unto them, Ye all shall desert
The Arabic word is not unlike the word for stumble, and Borg. ms. omits me. me this night:
Vat. ms. omits this night. it is written, I [24] will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered.
Matt. xxvi. 32.But after my [25] rising, I shall go before you into Galilee.
Matt. xxvi. 33.Simon Cephas answered and said unto [26] him, My Lord, if every man desert thee, I shall at no time desert thee.
Luke xxii. 33b.I am with thee ready for imprisonment and for death.
John xiii. 37b.And my life will I give up for thee. [27] [Arabic, p. 172]
John xiii. 38a.Jesus said unto him, Wilt thou give up thy life for me?
Mark xiv. 30b.Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Thou shalt to-day, during this night, before the cock crow [28] twice, three times deny me, that thou knowest me not.
Luke xxii. 34b; Mark xiv. 31.But Cephas said the more,
Or, went on saying. Even if it lead to
Lit. end in. Or, if I come to (the point of). death with thee, I shall not deny thee, my Lord. And in like manner said all the disciples also.

[29]
John xiv. 1.Then Jesus said unto them, Let not your hearts be troubled:
The diacritical points in both Vat. (followed by Ciasca) and Borg. mss. appear to demand a rendering inquire for be troubled. In Ibn-at-Tayyib’s comments (not the text), however (with other points), we have the meaning wail (root nhb). Every Syriac version uses a different word. believe in God, [30] and believe in me.
John xiv. 2.The stations
Or, ranks. in my Father’s house are many, else I should [31] have told
Or, should tell. you. I
