Probably the Arabic represents a Syriac For I. go to prepare for you a place.
John xiv. 3.And if I go to prepare for you a place, I shall return again, and take you unto me: and so where I am, there ye [32, 33] shall be also.
John xiv. 4.And the place that I go ye know,
Different words. and the way ye know.
Different words.
John xiv. 5.Thomas said unto him, Our Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how is the way for [34] us to the knowledge of that?
cf. Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary (f. 352a) and order of words in Peshitta (not Sin.).
John xiv. 6.Jesus said unto him, I am the way, and the truth, [35] and the life: and no man cometh unto my Father, but through me.
John xiv. 7.And if ye had known me, ye should have known my Father: and from henceforth ye know
Lit. have known. him, [36] and have seen him.
John xiv. 8.Philip
Different forms, as in Peshitta. said unto him, Our Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth [37] us.
John xiv. 9.Jesus said unto him, Have I been all this time with you, and dost thou not know
More exactly, hast thou not come to know. me, Philip?
Different forms, as in Peshitta. whosoever hath seen me hath seen the Father; how then sayest [38] thou, Shew us the Father?
John xiv. 10.Believest thou not that I am in my Father, and my Father in me? and the saying that I say, I say not of myself: but my Father who dwelleth in [39] me, he doeth these deeds.
John xiv. 11.Believe that I am in my Father, and my Father in me: [40] [Arabic, p. 173] or else believe for the sake of the deeds.
John xiv. 12.Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever believeth in me, the deeds that I do shall he do also; and [41] more than that shall he do: I go unto the Father.
John xiv. 13.And what ye shall ask in my [42] name, I shall do unto you, that the Father may be glorified in his Son.
John xiv. 14.And if ye [43, 44] ask me
The Borg. ms. has me clearly (cf. Peshitta). The Vat. ms. is ambiguous. in my name, I will do it.
John xiv. 15.If ye love me, keep my commandments.
John xiv. 16.And I will entreat of my Father, and he will send unto you another Paraclete, that he [45] may be with you for ever, even the Spirit of truth:
John xiv. 17.whom the world cannot receive; for it hath not seen him, nor known him: but ye know him; for he hath dwelt
Probably a misreading of the Peshitta (not Sin. or Cur.), since the next clause also agrees with it.
[46] with you, and is in you.
John xiv. 18.I will not leave you orphans: I will come unto you. [47]
John xiv. 19.Another little while, and the world seeth me not; but ye see me that I live, and ye [48] shall live also.
John xiv. 20.And in that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.

div3.title: Section XLVI.
div3.p:
[1]
John xiv. 21.Whosoever hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will [2] shew myself unto him.
John xiv. 22.Judas (not Iscariot) said unto him, My Lord, what is the [3] purpose of thy intention to shew thyself to us, and not to the world?
John xiv. 23.Jesus answered and said unto him, Whosoever loveth me will keep my word: and my Father will love him, and to him will we come, and make our
Lit. the (cf. Syriac versions). abode with him. [4]
John xiv. 24.But he that loveth me not keepeth not my word: and this word that ye hear is not my word, but the Father’s which sent me.

[5, 6]
John xiv. 25.This have I spoken unto you, while I was yet with you.
John xiv. 26.But the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom my Father will send in my name, he will teach you everything, and [7] [Arabic, p. 174] he will bring to your remembrance all that I say unto you.
John xiv. 27.Peace I leave you; my peace I give unto you: and not as this world giveth, give I unto you. [8]
John xiv. 28.Let your heart not be troubled,
This word is quite unlike that used in § 45, 29. nor fearful. Ye heard that I said unto you, that I go away, and come unto you. If
The Syriac form of the introductory particle is wrongly used, for in Arabic it has interrogative force. ye loved me, ye would rejoice, that I go away to my [9] Father: for my Father is greater than I.
John xiv. 29.And now I say unto you before it come [10] to pass, that, when it cometh to pass, ye may believe me.
John xiv. 30.Now I will not speak with you much: the Archon of the world will come, and he will have nothing in [11] me:
John xiv. 31a.but that the world may know that I love my Father, and as my Father charged me, so I do.

[12]
Luke xxii. 35.And he said unto them, When I sent you without purses, or wallets, and shoes,
The first letter of the Arabic word has lost its diacritical point. [13] lacked ye perchance anything? They said unto him, Nothing.
Luke xxii. 36.He said unto them, Henceforth, whosoever hath a purse, let him take it, and likewise the wallet also: and whosoever hath not a sword, shall sell his garment, and buy for himself a [14] sword.
Luke xxii. 37.I say unto you, that this scripture also must be fulfilled in me, that I should be reckoned
A possible rendering of the Syriac he was reckoned. with the transgressors: for all that is said of me is fulfilled in [15] me.
Luke xxii. 38.His disciples said unto him, Our Lord, lo, here are two swords. He said [16] unto them, They are sufficient.
John xiv. 31b; Luke xxii. 39.Arise, let us go hence. And they arose, and praised, and went forth, and went, according to their custom, to the mount of Olives, he and his disciples.

[17]
John xv. 1.And he said unto them, I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. [18]
John xv. 2.Every branch that produceth not fruit in me, he taketh it: and that which giveth fruit, [19] he cleanseth it, that it may give much fruit.
John xv. 3.Ye are already clean because of the word [20] that I have spoken unto you.
John xv. 4.Abide in me, and I in you. And as the branch of the [Arabic, p. 175] vine cannot produce fruit of itself, if it be not abiding in the vine; so too ye [21] also, if ye abide not in me.
John xv. 5.I am the vine, and ye are the branches: He then that abideth in me, and I in him, he giveth much fruit: for without me ye cannot [22] do anything.
John xv. 6.And if a man abide not in me, he is cast without, like a withered [23] branch; and it is gathered, and cast
The verbs may be active or passive, but are singular (cf. § 38, 43, note). into the fire, that it may be burned.
John xv. 7.If ye abide in me, and my word abide in you, everything that ye desire to ask shall be [24] done unto you.
John xv. 8.And herein is the Father glorified, that ye may give much fruit; [25] and ye shall be my disciples.
John xv. 9.And as my Father loved me, I loved you also: [26] abide in my love.
John xv. 10.If ye keep my commands, ye shall abide in my love; as I have [27] kept my Father’s commands, and abode in his love.
John xv. 11.I have spoken that unto you, [28] that my joy
Two words from the same root. may be in you, and your joy
Two words from the same root. be fulfilled.
John xv. 12.This is my commandment, [29] that ye love one another, as I loved you.
John xv. 13.And no love is greater than this, namely, [30] that a man should give his life for his friends.
John xv. 14.Ye are my friends, if ye do all that [31] I command you.
John xv. 15.I call you not now servants; for the servant knoweth not what
his lord doeth: my friends have I now called you; for everything that I heard from [32] my Father I have made known unto you.
John xv. 16.Ye did not choose
Different words. me, but I chose I you, and appointed you, that ye also should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should
Or, shall and will, respectively. [33] abide; and that all that ye shall ask my Father in my name, he may
Or, shall and will, respectively. give you.
John xv. 17.This [34] I command
Or, have commanded. you, that ye love one another.
John xv. 18.And if the world hate you, know that [35] before you it hated me.
John xv. 19.If then ye were of the world, the world would love its own: but ye are not of the world: I chose you out of the world: therefore the world [36] [Arabic, p. 176] hateth you.
John xv. 20.Remember the word that I said unto you, that no servant is greater than his lord. And if they persecuted
cf. § 8, 34, note. me, you also will they [37] persecute;
cf. § 8, 34, note. and if they kept my word, your word also will they keep.
John xv. 21.But all these things will they do unto you for my name’s sake, for they have not known
The Arabic text (Vat.) is grammatically inaccurate, and the Borg. ms. has know not. him [38] that sent me.
John xv. 22.And if I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: [39] but now they have no excuse for their sins.
John xv. 23.Whosoever hateth me, also hateth my [40] Father.
John xv. 24.And if I had not done the deeds before them that no other man did, they would not have had sin: but now they have seen and hated me and my Father [41] also: that the word may be fulfilled that is written in their law,
John xv. 25.They hated me for [42] nothing.
John xv. 26.But when the Paraclete is come, whom I will send unto you from my Father, even the Spirit of truth, which goeth forth from my Father, he shall bear witness of [43] me:
John xv. 27.and ye also bear witness, because from the beginning ye have been with me.

[44, 45]
John xvi. 1.I have said that unto you, that ye may not stumble.
Lit. sway (as one does in dozing).
John xvi. 2.And they shall put you out of their synagogues: and there cometh an
Or, the, as in Borg. ms. hour when every one that killeth [46] you shall think that he hath offered unto God an offering.
John xvi. 3.And they will do that, [47] because they do not know me, nor my Father.
John xvi. 4.I have said that unto you, so that [48] when its time is come, ye may remember it, that I told you.
John xvi. 5 [in the Greek and English verse 5 begins at But.].And this hitherto I said not unto you, because I was with you. But
In the Greek and English verse 5 begins at But. now I go unto him that sent me; and no [49] man of you asketh me whither I go.
John xvi. 6.I have said that unto you now, and grief hath [50] come and taken possession of your hearts
John xvi. 7.But I say the truth unto you; It is better
Or, best. for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Paraclete will not come unto you; [51] [Arabic, p. 177] but if I go away, I will send him unto you.
John xvi. 8.And when he cometh, he will reprove the world for sin, and for righteousness, and for judgement: [52, 53] for sin,
John xvi. 9.because they have not believed in me;
John xvi. 10.and for righteousness, because I go [54] to my Father;
John xvi. 11.and for judgement, because
Lit. that (cf. Peshitta). the Archon of this world hath been [55] judged.
John xvi. 12.And further have I many things to speak unto you, but ye cannot tarry
Or perhaps receive (them). Possibly a Syriac d has been read r. But Ibn-at-Tayyib in the text of his Commentary (f. 357a) has a word which perhaps might be rendered accommodate yourselves (to them) (same letters, but last two transposed), while his comment (f. 357b) gives ye cannot bear it. [56] now.
John xvi. 13.Howbeit
Or, And. when the Spirit of truth is come, he will remind
The Syriac words for remind and lead differ only in the length of a single stroke. Ibn-at-Tayyib (ibid. f. 357b) almost seems to have read illumine you with, although he calls attention to the “Greek” reading. you of all the truth: he will say nothing from himself; but everything that he heareth, that shall [57] he say: and he shall make known unto you the things that are to be.
John xvi. 14.And he shall [58] glorify me; for from me shall he take and shew you.
John xvi. 15.All that my Father hath is mine: therefore said I unto you, that he taketh
Same tense. of mine, and shall shew
Same tense. you.

div3.title: Section XLVII.
div3.p:
[1]
John xvi. 16.A little while, and ye shall not behold me; and a little while again, and ye shall [2] behold me; because I go to the Father.
John xvi. 17.His disciples therefore said one to another, What is this that he hath said unto us, A little while, and ye shall not behold me; and a little while again, and ye shall behold me: and, I go to my [3] Father?
John xvi. 18.And they said, What is this little while that he hath said? We know not [4] what he speaketh.
John xvi. 19.And Jesus perceived that they were seeking to ask him, and said unto them, Do ye inquire among yourselves concerning this, that I said unto you, A little while, and ye behold me not, and a little while again, and ye shall [5] behold me?
John xvi. 20.Verily, verily,
Not quite the usual formula, there being here no article. I say unto you, that ye shall weep and grieve, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your grief shall turn
The Arabic might also be rendered be turned, but the Syriac is intransitive. to joy.

[6]
John xvi. 21.For, a woman when the time is come for her that she should bring forth, the arrival of the day of her bringing forth distresseth her: but whenever she hath brought forth a son, she remembereth not her distress, for joy at the birth of a man into the [7] world.
John xvi. 22.And ye now also grieve: but I shall see you, and your hearts shall rejoice, [8] [Arabic, p. 178] and your joy no man taketh from you.
John xvi. 23.And in that day ye shall ask me nothing. And verily, verily,
Not quite the usual formula, there being here no article (cf. also § 47, 5). I say unto you, All that ye ask my Father in my name, he will give you.
John xvi. 24.Hitherto ye have asked nothing [9] in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be complete.

[10]
John xvi. 25.I have spoken unto you now in ænigmas:
Not the usual word for proverb or parable (cf. Syriac versions). but there will come an hour when
So Vat. ms. and Peshitta. The Borg. ms., followed by Ciasca, has and a time when. I shall not speak to you in ænigmas,
Not the usual word for proverb or parable (cf. Syriac versions). but shall reveal unto you the Father plainly, [11] in that day when
cf. Peshitta. ye shall ask in my name:
John xvi. 26.and I say not unto you, that I shall [12] entreat the Father for you;
John xvi. 27.for the Father loveth you, because ye have loved me, [13] and have believed that I came forth from my Father.
John xvi. 28.I came forth from my Father, and came into the world: and I leave the world, and go unto my Father. [14]
John xvi. 29.His disciples said unto him, Lo, thy speech is now plain, and thou hast not said one [15] thing in an ænigma.
John xvi. 30.Now, lo, we know that thou knowest everything, and needest not that any man should ask thee: and by this we believe that thou camest forth [16, 17] from God.
John xvi. 31.Jesus said unto them, Believe that an hour cometh,
John xvi. 32.and lo, it hath come, and ye shall be scattered, every one of you to his place, and shall leave me [18] alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
John xvi. 33.This have I said unto you, that in me ye may have peace. And in the world trouble shall overtake you: but be of good courage; for I have overcome the world.

[19]
John xvii. 1.This said Jesus, and lifted up his eyes unto heaven, and said, My Father, the hour [20] is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son may glorify thee:
John xvii. 2.as thou gavest him authority [21] over all flesh, that all that thou hast given him, he might give them
Lit. it or him. eternal life.
John xvii. 3.And this is eternal life, that they should
In the Borg. ms. the sentence begins with that they might, the preceding clause being omitted. know that thou alone art true God, and that he [22] [Arabic, p. 179] whom thou didst send is Jesus the Messiah.
The above is perhaps the most natural rendering of the Arabic; but the latter is really only an awkward word-for-word reproduction of the Peshitta, which means know thee, who alone art the God of truth, and him whom thou didst send, (even) Jesus the Messiah.
John xvii. 4.I glorified thee in the earth, [23] and the work which thou gavest me to do I have accomplished.
John xvii. 5.And now glorify thou me, O Father, beside thee, with that glory which I had with thee [24] before the world was.
John xvii. 6.I made known thy name to the men whom thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them to me; and they have kept [25, 26] thy word.
John xvii. 7.Now they
So Ciasca’s text. The Vat. ms. has I, with the Peshitta and probably Sinaitic. know that all that thou hast given me is from thee:
John xvii. 8.and the sayings which thou gavest me I have given unto them; and they received them, and knew of a truth that I came forth from thee, and believed that thou didst send me. [27]
John xvii. 9.And I ask for their sake: and my asking is not for the world, but for those whom [28] thou hast given me; for they are thine:
John xvii. 10.and all that is mine is thine, and all that is [29] thine is mine: and I am glorified in them.
John xvii. 11.And now I am not in the world, and they are in the world, and I come to thee. My
So in Sinaitic. The Peshitta omits My. holy Father, keep them in thy [30] name which thou hast given unto me, that they may be one, as we are.
John xvii. 12.When I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: and I kept those whom thou gavest unto me: and no man of them hath perished, but the son of perdition; that [31] the scripture might be fulfilled.
John xvii. 13.Now I come to thee: and this I say in the world, [32] that my joy may be complete in them.
John xvii. 14.I have given them thy word; and the world [33] hated them, because they were not of the world, as I was not of the world.
John xvii. 15.And I ask not this, that thou take them from the world, but that thou keep them from the [34, 35] evil one.
John xvii. 16.They were not of the world, as I was not of the world.
John xvii. 17.O Father, sanctify [36] them in thy truth: for thy word is truth.
John xvii. 18.And as thou didst send me into the world, I [37] [Arabic, p. 180] also send them into the world.
John xvii. 19.And for their sake I sanctify myself, that they [38] also may be sanctified in the truth.
John xvii. 20.Neither for these alone do I ask, but for [39] the sake of them that believe in me through their word;
John xvii. 21.that they may be all one;
as thou art in me, and I in thee, and so they also shall be one in us: that the world [40] may believe that thou didst send me.
John xvii. 22.And the glory which thou hast given unto [41] me I have given unto them;
John xvii. 23.that they may be one, as we are one; I in them, and thou in me, that they may be perfect into
Vat. ms. has as. one; and that the world may know that [42] thou didst send me, and that I
cf. Peshitta, as pointed in the editions. loved them, as thou lovedst me.
John xvii. 24.Father, and those whom thou hast given me, I wish that, where I am, they may be with me also; that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before [43] the foundation
cf. § 17, 17, note. of the world.
John xvii. 25.My righteous Father,
The Arabic as it stands should mean My Father is righteous; but it is simply the ordinary Syriac reading, and is so rendered above. and the world knew thee not, [44] but I know thee; and they knew that thou didst send me; and I made known unto them thy name, and will make it known to them;
John xvii. 26.that the love wherewith thou lovedst me may be in them, and I shall
Or perhaps may. be in them.

div3.title: Section XLVIII.
div3.p:
[1]
John xviii. 1.This said Jesus, and went forth with his disciples to a place which was called Gethsemane,
Matt. xxvi. 36. on
Vat. ms. has and on. the side that is in the plain
The word rendered plain (cf. Dozy, Supplement, sub voc.), which occurs also in the text of Ibn-at-Tayyib (loc. cit., f. 362b), properly means lake. The word in the Jerusalem Lectionary means valley as well as stream. For the whole clause cf. the text of John xviii. in Die vier Evangelien, arabisch, aus der Wiener Handschrift, edited by P. de Lagarde, 1864. of Kidron, the mountain,
cf. Sinaitic Syriac and Luke xxii. 39. the place [2] in which was a garden; and he entered thither, he and his disciples.
John xviii. 2.And Judas the [3] betrayer knew that place: for Jesus oft-times met with his disciples there.
Luke xxii. 40a; Matt. xxvi. 36b.And when Jesus came to the place, he said to his disciples, Sit ye here, so that I may go and pray; [4, 5] [Arabic, p. 181] and pray ye, that ye enter not into temptations.
Luke xxii. 40b; Matt. xxvi. 37.And he took with him Cephas and the sons of Zebedee together, James and John; and he began to [6] look sorrowful, and to be anxious.
Matt. xxvi. 38.And he said unto them, My soul is distressed unto [7] death: abide ye here, and watch with me.
Luke xxii. 41a.And he withdrew from them a little, [8] the space of a stone’s throw;
Mark xiv. 35b.and he kneeled,
Lit. fell on his knees. and fell on his face, and prayed, so [9] that, if it were possible, this hour might pass
Lit. let this hour pass. The Borg. ms. omits him. him.
Mark xiv. 36a.And he said, Father, thou art able for all things; if thou wilt, let this cup pass me:
Luke xxii. 42b.but let not my will be done, [10] but let thy will be done.
Matt. xxvi. 40a; Mark xiv. 37b.And he came to his disciples, and found them sleeping; [11] and he said unto Cephas, Simon, didst thou sleep?
Matt. xxvi. 40b.Could ye thus not for one hour [12] watch with me?
Matt. xxvi. 41a; Matt. xiv. 38b.Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptations: the spirit is [13] willing and ready, but the body is weak.
Lit. diseased. The Arabic word is rare in the sense required by the context (cf. Pesh.).
Matt. xxvi. 42.And he went again a second time, and prayed, and said, My Father, if it is not possible with regard to
This reading would perhaps more easily arise out of the Sinaitic than out of the Peshitta. this cup that it pass, [14] except I drink it, thy will be done.
Mark xiv. 40.And he returned again, and found his disciples sleeping, for their eyes were heavy from their grief and anxiety; and they knew not [15] what to say to him.
Matt. xxvi. 44.And he left them, and went away again, and prayed a third [16] time, and said the very same word.
Luke xxii. 43.And there appeared unto him an angel from [17] heaven, encouraging him.
Luke xxii. 44.And being afraid
cf. Peshitta. Or, And although he was afraid. he prayed continuously:
The Peshitta (hardly Cur.) is capable of this interpretation. and his sweat
cf. Syr., especially Peshitta. [18] [Arabic, p. 182] became like a stream of blood, and fell on the ground.
Luke xxii. 45a.Then he rose from [19] his prayer, and came to his disciples, and found them sleeping.
Luke xxii. 46; Matt. xxvi. 45b.And he [20] said unto them, Sleep now, and rest:
Mark xiv. 41b.the end hath arrived,
cf. Syr., especially Peshitta. and the hour hath come; [21] and behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Mark xiv. 42a; Matt. xxvi. 46b.Arise, let us go:
cf. § 4, 20, note. for he hath come that betrayeth me.

[22]
Matt. xxvi. 47.And while he was still speaking, came Judas the betrayer, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude carrying lanterns and torches
John xviii. 3. and swords and staves, from the chief priests and scribes and elders of the people, and with him the footsoldiers [23] of the Romans.
cf. John xviii. 3 (Jerusalem Lectionary). In Syriac Romans means soldiers. The Arabic footsoldiers might be man (singular).
Matt. xxvi. 48; Mark xiv. 44b.And Judas the betrayer gave them a sign, and said, He whom I shall kiss, he is he: take him with care,
cf. Syriac versions. Obviously we must supply a diacritical point over the last radical, or read the middle one as dhal. and lead him away.
Lit. him to —. Borg. ms. probably means bear him away.

[24]
John xviii. 4a.And Jesus, because he knew everything that should come upon him, went forth [25] unto them.
Matt. xxvi. 49; Matt. xxvi. 50a.And immediately Judas the betrayer came to Jesus, and said, Peace, [26] my Master; and kissed him.
Luke xxii. 48b.And Jesus said unto him, Judas, with a kiss betrayest [27] thou the Son of man?
Matt. xxvi. 50b; Luke xxii. 52a, c.Was it for that thou camest, my friend? And Jesus said [28] to those that came unto him, Whom seek ye?
John xviii. 4b; John xviii. 5.They said unto him, Jesus the Nazarene. Jesus said unto them, I am he. And Judas the betrayer also was standing [29] with them.
John xviii. 6.And when Jesus said unto them, I am he, they retreated backward, and [30] fell to the ground.
John xviii. 7.And Jesus asked them again, Whom seek ye? They answered, [31] Jesus the Nazarene.
John xviii. 8.Jesus said unto them, I told you that I am he: and if ye seek [32] me, let these go away: that the word might be fulfilled which he spake,
John xviii. 9.Of those [33] [Arabic, p. 183] whom thou hast given me I lost not even one.
Matt. xxvi. 50c.Then came those that were with Judas, and seized Jesus, and took him.

[34]
Luke xxii. 49.And when his disciples saw what happened, they said, Our Lord, shall we smite [35] them with swords?
John xviii. 10.And Simon Cephas had a sword, and he drew it, and struck the servant of the chief priest, and cut off his right ear. And the name of that servant [36] was Malchus.
John xviii. 11a.Jesus said unto Cephas, The cup which my Father hath given [37] me, shall I not drink it?
John xviii. 11c; Matt. xxvi. 52b.Put the sword into its sheath: for all that take with
Withis doubtless an accidental repetition of by (the same Arabic particle) in the next clause. the [38] sword shall die by the sword.
Matt. xxvi. 53.Thinkest
The introductory interrogative particle may represent an original Or. thou that I am not able to ask of my [39] Father, and he shall now raise up for me more than
Vat. ms. omits than, and has more only in the margin by another hand. twelve tribes of angels?
Matt. xxvi. 54.Then [40] how should the scriptures which were spoken be fulfilled, that thus it must be?
Luke xxii. 51b.Your [41] leave in this.
The phrase is awkward. The rendering is different in the text (f. 292a, cf. Lagarde, Die vier Evv.), and yet again in the comment (f. 293a) of Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary.
Matt. xxvi. 55.And he touched the ear of him that was struck, and healed it. And in that hour Jesus said to the multitudes, As they come out against a thief are ye come out against me with swords and staves to take me? Daily was I with you in [42] the temple sitting teaching, and ye took me not:
Luke xxii. 53b.but this is your hour, and the power [43] of darkness.
Matt. xxvi. 56.And that was, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.

[44]
John xviii. 12a.Then the disciples all left him, and fled. And the footsoldiers and the officers [45] and the soldiers
cf. § 11, 11. of the Jews seized Jesus, and came.
Mark xiv. 51.And a certain
Lit. one. young man [46] followed him, and he was wrapped in a towel, naked:
Mark xiv. 52.and they seized him; so he [47] [Arabic, p. 184] left the towel, and fled naked.
John xviii. 12b; John xviii. 13.Then they took Jesus, and bound him, and brought him to Annas first; because he was the father in law of Caiaphas, [48] who was chief priest that year.
John xviii. 14.And Caiaphas was he that counselled the Jews, that it was necessary that one man should die instead of the people.

[49]
John xviii. 15.And Simon Cephas and one of the other disciples followed Jesus. And the chief [50] priest knew that disciple, and he entered with Jesus into the court;
John xviii. 16.but Simon was standing without at the door. And that other disciple, whom the chief priest knew, [51] went out and spake unto her that kept the door, and she brought Simon in.
John xviii. 17a.And when the maid that kept the door saw Simon, she looked stedfastly at him, and said unto him, Art not thou also one of the disciples of this man, I mean Jesus the [52] Nazarene?
Luke xxii. 57; Mark xiv. 68b.But he denied, and said, Woman, I know him not, neither know I even [53] what thou sayest.
John xviii. 18a.And the servants and the soldiers rose, and made a fire in the [54] middle of the court, that they might warm themselves; for it was cold.
Luke xxii. 55a.And when [55] the fire burned up, they sat down around it.
John xviii. 18c; Matt. xxvi. 58b.And Simon also came, and sat down with them to warm himself, that he might see the end of what should happen.

div3.title: Section XLIX.
div3.p:
[1, 2]
John xviii. 19.And the chief priest asked Jesus about his disciples, and about his doctrine.
cf. § 6, 40, note.
John xviii. 20.And Jesus said unto him, I was speaking
Peshitta, spake; Sin. omits the verse; Cur. lacking. openly to the people; and I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, where all the Jews gather; and I have spoken nothing in [3] [Arabic, p. 185] secret.
John xviii. 21.Why askest thou me? ask those that have heard, what I spake unto [4] them: for they know all that I said.
John xviii. 22.And when he had said that, one of the soldiers which were standing there struck the cheek
See § 9, 7, note. of Jesus, and said unto him,
[5] Dost thou thus answer the chief priest?
John xviii. 23.Jesus answered and said unto him, If I [6] have spoken evil, bear witness of evil:
Borg. ms. has the evil. but if well, why didst thou smite me?
John xviii. 24.And Annas sent Jesus bound unto Caiaphas the chief priest.

[7]
John xviii. 25a.And when Jesus went out, Simon Cephas was standing in the outer court warming [8] himself.
Mark xiv. 69a.And that maid saw him again, and began to say to those that stood [9] by, This man also was there with Jesus the Nazarene.
Matt. xxvi. 71b; Matt. xxvi. 73b.And those that stood by [10] came forward and said to Cephas, Truly thou art one of his disciples.
Matt. xxvi. 72.And he [11] denied again with an oath, I know not the man.
Luke xxii. 58a; John xviii. 26a.And after a little one of the servants of the chief priest, the kinsman of him whose ear Simon cut off, saw him; and [12] he disputed
This is an alternative meaning of the Syriac word affirmed, used in the Peshitta. and said, Truly this man was with him:
Luke xxii. 59b.and he also is a Galilæan; [13] and his speech resembles.
cf. Sinaitic (Curetonian wanting). Vat. ms., which Ciasca follows, adds him or it.
Matt. xxvi. 73c; John xviii. 26b.And he said unto Simon, Did not I see thee with him [14] in the garden?
Mark xiv. 71.Then began Simon to curse,
Borg. ms., by adding diacritical points, gets asserted. and to swear, I know not this man [15] whom ye have mentioned.
Luke xxii. 60b.And immediately, while he was speaking, the cock crew [16] twice.
Luke xxii. 61a.And in that hour Jesus turned, he being without, and looked stedfastly at Cephas. And Simon remembered the word of our Lord, which he said unto him, [17, 18]
Mark xiv. 30b, c.Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice.
Luke xxii. 62.And Simon went forth without, and wept bitterly.

[19] [Arabic, p. 186]
Luke xxii. 66a.And when the morning approached, the servants of all the chief priests and the scribes and the elders of the people and all the multitude assembled, [20, 21] and made a plot;
Matt. xxvii. 1b.and they took counsel against Jesus to put him to death.
Matt. xxvi. 59b.And they sought false witnesses who should witness against him, that they might put him to [22, 23] death, and they found not;
Matt. xxvi. 60a.but many false witnesses came,
Mark xiv. 59.but their witness did not [24, 25] agree.
Matt. xxvi. 60b.But at last there came two lying witnesses,
Mark xiv. 57b; Mark xiv. 58.and said, We heard him say, I will destroy this
Syriac order, but not in agreement with the versions. temple of God that is made with hands, and will build another not [26, 27] made with hands after three days.
Mark xiv. 59; Matt. xxvi. 63a.And not even so did their witness agree. But Jesus was silent.
Mark xiv. 60a.And the chief priest rose in the midst, and asked Jesus, and said, [28]
Matt. xxvi. 62b.Answerest thou not a word concerning anything? what do these
Vat. ms. has anything, when these. witness against [29, 30] thee?
Mark xiv. 61a.But Jesus was silent, and answered him nothing.
Luke xxii. 66b.And they took him up [31] into their assembly,
The word usually means synagogue in this work. and said unto him, If thou art the Messiah, tell us.
Luke xxii. 67.He said [32] unto them, If I tell you, ye will not believe me:
Luke xxii. 68.and if I ask you, ye will not answer [33] me a word, nor let me go.
Matt. xxvi. 63b.And the chief priest answered and said unto him, I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us whether thou art the Messiah, the [34, 35] Son of the living God.
Matt. xxvi. 64a.Jesus said unto him, Thou hast said that I am he.
Luke xxii. 70.They all said unto him, Then thou art now the Son of God? Jesus said, Ye have said [36] that I am he.
Matt. xxvi. 64b.I say unto you, that henceforth ye shall see the Son of man sitting [37] [Arabic, p. 187] at the right hand of power, and coming on the clouds of heaven.
Mark xiv. 63a; Matt. xxvi. 65b.Then the [38] chief priest rent his tunic,
The foreign word used in the Peshitta is preserved. The Sinaitic uses a Syriac word meaning garment. and said, He hath blasphemed.
Luke xxii. 71.And they all said, Why should we seek now witnesses? we have heard now the blasphemy from his mouth. [39, 40] What then think ye?
Mark xiv. 64b; Matt. xxvi. 66.They all answered and said, He is worthy of death.
Mark xiv. 65a; Luke xxii. 63b.Then some of them drew near, and spat in his face, and struck him, and scoffed at him. [41]
Mark xiv. 65c; Matt. xxvi. 68.And the soldiers struck him on his cheeks,
See § 9, 7, note. and said, Prophesy unto us, thou Messiah: [42] who is he that struck thee?
Luke xxii. 65.And many other things spake they falsely,
See § 7, 17, note. and said against him.

[43]
John xviii. 28; Mark xv. 1b.And all of their assembly arose,
cf. Luke xxiii. 1a. and took Jesus, and brought him bound
cf. Matt. xxvii. 2; Mark xv. 1. to [44] the prætorium,
Arabic, diwdn. and delivered him up to Pilate the judge;
John xviii. 28c.but they entered not into the prætorium, that they might not be defiled when they should eat the passover.

[45]
Matt. xxvii. 11a; John xviii. 29.And Jesus stood before the judge. And Pilate went forth unto them without, and [46] said unto them, What accusation
Lit. plea. have ye against this man?
John xviii. 30.They answered and said unto him, If he had not been doing evils, neither should we have delivered [47] him up unto thee.
Luke xxiii. 2b.We found this man leading our people astray, and restraining from giving tribute to Cæsar, and saying of himself that he is the King, the Messiah. [48]
John xviii. 31.Pilate said unto them, Then take ye him, and judge him according to your law.
[Arabic, p. 188] The Jews said unto him, We have no authority to put a man to death: [49]
John xviii. 32.that the word might be fulfilled, which Jesus spake, when he made known by what manner of death he was to die.

[50]
John xviii. 33.And Pilate entered into the prætorium, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Art [51] thou the King of the Jews?
John xviii. 34.Jesus said unto him, Of thyself saidst thou this, or [52] did others tell it thee concerning me?
John xviii. 35.Pilate said unto him, Am I, forsooth,
See § 4, 24, note. a Jew? The sons of thy nation
The Syriac word. and the chief priests delivered thee unto me: what [53] hast thou done?
John xviii. 36.Jesus said unto him, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be [54] delivered to the Jews: now my kingdom is not from hence.
John xviii. 37.Pilate said unto him, Then thou art a king? Jesus said unto him, Thou hast said that I am a king. And for this was I born, and for this came I into the world, that I should bear witness [55] of the truth.
John xviii. 38a.And every one that is of the truth heareth my voice. Pilate said unto him, And what is the truth? And when he said that, he went out again unto the Jews.

div3.title: Section L.
div3.p:
[1]
Luke xxiii. 4.And Pilate said unto the chief priests and the multitude, I have not found [2] against this man anything.
Luke xxiii. 5.But they cried out and said, He hath disquieted
Or, led astray (cf. § 25, 17, note). our people with his teaching in all Judæa, and he began
cf. Syriac versions. from Galilee and unto this [3] place.
Luke xxiii. 6.And Pilate, when he heard the name of Galilee, asked, Is this man a Galilæan? [4]
Luke xxiii. 7.And when he learned that he was under the jurisdiction of Herod, he sent him to Herod: for he was in Jerusalem in those days.

[5]
Luke xxiii. 8.And Herod, when he saw Jesus, rejoiced exceedingly: for he had desired to see him for a long time, because he had heard regarding him many things; and he counted on
Same word as in § 10, 16 (see note there). [6] [Arabic, p. 189] seeing some sign from him.
Luke xxiii. 9.And he questioned him with many words; but [7] Jesus answered him not a word.
Luke xxiii. 10.And the scribes and chief priests were [8] standing by, and they accused him vehemently.
Luke xxiii. 11.And Herod scoffed at him, he and his servants; and when he had scoffed at him, he clothed him in robes of scarlet, [9] and sent him to Pilate.
Luke xxiii. 12.And on that day Pilate and Herod became friends, there having been
Lit. and there was. enmity between them before that.

[10, 11]
Luke xxiii. 13.And Pilate called the chief priests and the rulers of the people,
Luke xxiii. 14.and said unto them, Ye brought unto me this man, as the perverter of your people: and I have tried him before you, and have not found in this man any cause
The Arabic word may also, like the Syriac, mean thing, but hardly, as that does here, fault or crime. The Vat. ms., pointing differently, reads thing. The same confusion occurs at § 40, 35 (cf. a converse case in § 25, 40). of all that ye [12] seek
So Ciasca’s text, following the Borg. ms. The Vat. ms. has plotted, which is nearer the Syriac accuse. against him:
Luke xxiii. 15.nor yet Herod: for I sent him unto him; and he hath done [13] nothing for which he should deserve death.
Luke xxiii. 16.So now I will chastise him, and let [14, 15] him go.
Luke xxiii. 18a.The multitude all cried out and said, Take him from us, take him.
Mark xv. 3a.And [16] the chief priests and the elders accused him of many things.
Matt. xxvii. 12.And during their [17] accusation he answered not a word.
Matt. xxvii. 13.Then Pilate said unto him, Hearest thou not [18] how many things they witness against thee?
Matt. xxvii. 14.And he answered him not, not even one word: and Pilate marvelled at that.

[19]
Matt. xxvii. 19.And when the judge sat on his tribune, his wife sent unto him, and said unto him, See that thou have nothing to do with that righteous man: for I have suffered much in my dream
See § 3, 12, note. to-day because of him.

[20]
Matt. xxvii. 15.And at every feast the custom of the judge was to release to the people one [21] prisoner, him whom they would.
Matt. xxvii. 16.And there was in their prison a well-known prisoner, [22, 23] called Barabbas.
Matt. xxvii. 17a.And when they assembled, Pilate said unto them,
John xviii. 39.Ye have a custom, that I should release unto you a prisoner at the passover: will ye that I [24] release unto you the King of the Jews?
John xviii. 40.And they all cried out and said, Release not [Arabic, p. 190] unto us this man, but release unto us Barabbas. And this Barabbas was a [25] robber,
Luke xxiii. 19.who for sedition
Ciasca’s text, following the Vat. ms., has disorder. Borg. ms. has division (cf. heresies, Curetonian of § 50, 37), which by addition of a diacritical point gives sedition; cf. § 50, 37 (Ciasca, following Vat. ms.), and Peshitta (both places). and murder, which was in the city, was cast into the
[26] prison.
Mark xv. 8.And all the people cried out and began to ask him to do as the custom was [27] that he should do with them.
Mark xv. 9a; Matt. xxvii. 17b.And Pilate answered and said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called the Messiah, the [28] King of the Jews?
Matt. xxvii. 18.For Pilate knew that envy had moved them to deliver him up. [29]
Matt. xxvii. 20.And the chief priests and the elders asked the multitudes to deliver Barabbas, and [30] to destroy Jesus.
Matt. xxvii. 21.The judge answered and said unto them, Whom of the two will [31] ye that I release unto you? They said, Barabbas.
Matt. xxvii. 22a.Pilate said unto them, And [32] Jesus which is called the Messiah, what shall I do with him?
Mark xv. 13.They all cried out [33] and said, Crucify him.
Luke xxiii. 20.And Pilate spake to them again, for he desired to release [34] Jesus;
Luke xxiii. 21.but they cried out and said, Crucify him, crucify him, and release unto us [35] Barabbas.
Luke xxiii. 22.And Pilate said unto them a third time, What evil hath this man done? I have not found in him any cause
Our translator has retained the Syriac word, which in this context means fault (see § 50, 11, note). to necessitate death: I will chastise him and [36] let him go.
Luke xxiii. 23.But they increased in importunity
The word used in Vat ms. means a repeated charge or attack. That in Borg. ms. is probably used in the post-classical sense of importuning him. Either word might be written by a copyist for the other. The same double reading probably occurs again at § 53, 55. with a loud voice, and asked him to crucify him. And their voice, and the voice of the chief priests, prevailed. [37]
Mark xv. 15a; Luke xxiii. 25a.Then Pilate released unto them that one who was cast into prison for sedition and murder, Barabbas, whom they asked for:
Matt. xxvii. 26b.and he scourged Jesus with whips.
cf. Syriac versions.

[38]
Matt. xxvii. 27.Then the footsoldiers of the judge took Jesus, and went into the prætorium, and [39] [Arabic, p. 191] gathered unto him all of the footsoldiers.
Matt. xxvii. 28.And they stripped him, and put on [40] him a scarlet cloak.
John xix. 2.And they clothed him in garments of purple, and plaited [41] a crown of thorns, and placed it on his head, and a reed in his right hand;
Matt. xxvii. 29b.and while they mocked at him and laughed, they fell down on their knees before him, and bowed [42] down to
This may be a mere clerical error (very natural in Arabic) for scoffed at, the reading of the Syriac versions. This being so, it is worthy of remark that the reading is apparently common to the two mss. The Syriac words are, however, also somewhat similar. The Jerusalem Lectionary has a word agreeing with the text above. him, and said, Hail,
Lit. Peace. King of the Jews!
Matt. xxvii. 30.And they spat in his face, and took the reed from his hand, and struck him on his head,
John xix. 3b.and smote his cheeks. [43]
John xix. 4.And Pilate went forth without again, and said unto the Jews, I bring him forth to [44] you, that ye may know that I do not find, in examining
This reading may be a corruption of a very literal rendering of the Peshitta. him, even one crime.
cf. § 50, 11.
John xix. 5.And Jesus went forth without, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garments. [45]
John xix. 6.Pilate said unto them, Behold, the man! And when the chief priests and the soldiers
cf. § 11, 11, note. saw him, they cried out and said, Crucify him, crucify him. Pilate said unto them, Take him yourselves, and crucify him: for I find not a cause
See § 50, 35, note. against [46] him.
John xix. 7.The Jews said unto him, We have a law, and according to our law he deserves [47] death, because he made himself the Son of God.
John xix. 8.And when Pilate heard this word, [48] his fear increased;
John xix. 9.and he entered again into the porch, and said to Jesus, Whence [49] art thou?
John xix. 10.But Jesus answered him not a word. Pilate said unto him, Speakest
Borg. ms., Why speakest; a reading that might be a corruption of the Peshitta. thou not unto me? knowest thou not that I have authority to release thee, and have [50] authority to crucify thee?
John xix. 11.Jesus said unto him, Thou hast not any
Lit. even one (Pesh.). authority over me, if thou wert not given it from above: therefore the sin of him that delivered [51] me up unto thee is greater than thy sin.
John xix. 12.And for this word Pilate wished to release him: but the Jews cried out, If thou let him go, thou art not a friend of Cæsar: for every one that maketh himself a king is against Cæsar.

div3.title: Section LI.
div3.p:
[1] [Arabic, p. 192]
John xix. 13.And when Pilate heard this saying, he took Jesus out, and sat on the tribune in the place which was called the pavement of stones, but in the Hebrew [2] called Gabbatha.
John xix. 14.And that day was the Friday of the passover: and it had reached [3] about the sixth hour.
Lit. six hours.
John xix. 15.And he said to the Jews, Behold, your King! And they cried out, Take him, take him, crucify him, crucify him. Pilate said unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests said unto him, We have no king except [4] Cæsar.
Matt. xxvii. 24.And Pilate, when he saw it, and
Or, that. he was gaining nothing, but the tumult
was increasing, took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, and said, I [5] am innocent of the blood of this innocent man: ye shall know.
cf. Peshitta. Or, Ye know (cf. Sinaitic).
Matt. xxvii. 25.And all the people [6] answered and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.
John xix. 16a.Then Pilate commanded to grant them their request; and delivered up Jesus to be crucified, according to their wish.

[7]
Matt. xxvii. 3.Then Judas the betrayer, when he saw Jesus wronged, went and returned the [8] thirty pieces of money to the chief priests and the elders,
Matt. xxvii. 4.and said, I have sinned in my betraying innocent blood. And they said unto him, And we, what must we do? [9] know thou.
Matt. xxvii. 5.And he threw down the money in the temple, and departed; and he [10] went away
Borg. ms. omits and he went away. and hanged
Lit. strangled. himself.
Matt. xxvii. 6.And the chief priests took the money, and said, We have not authority to cast it into the place of the offering,
cf. § 32, 15, note. for it is the price [11] of blood.
Matt. xxvii. 7.And they took counsel, and bought with it the plain of the potter, for [12] the burial of strangers.
Matt. xxvii. 8.Therefore that plain was called, The field of blood, unto [13] [Arabic, p. 193] this day.
Matt. xxvii. 9.Therein
Or, at that (time). was fulfilled the saying in the prophet which said, I took thirty pieces of money, the price of the precious one, which was fixed [14] by the children of Israel;
Matt. xxvii. 10.and I paid them for the plain of the potter, as the Lord commanded me.

[15]
John xix. 16b; Mark xv. 20b.And the Jews took Jesus, and went away to crucify him.
John xix. 17a; Matt. xxvii. 31b.And when he bare his [16] cross and went out, they stripped him of those purple and scarlet garments which he [17] had on, and put on him his own garments.
Matt. xxvii. 32a; Mark xv. 21b.And while they were going with him, they found a man, a Cyrenian, coming from the country, named Simon, the father of Alexander and Rufus:
Matt. xxvii. 32b.and they compelled this man to bear the cross of Jesus. [18]
Luke xxiii. 26b.And they took the cross and laid it upon him, that he might bear it, and come after Jesus; and Jesus went, and his cross behind him.

[19]
Luke xxiii. 27.And there followed him much people, and women which were lamenting and [20] raving.
Lit. being burned. The text is probably corrupt.
Luke xxiii. 28.But Jesus turned unto them and said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not [21] for me: weep for yourselves, and for your children.
Luke xxiii. 29.Days are coming, when they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that bare not, and the breasts [22] that gave not suck.
Luke xxiii. 30.Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and [23] to the hills, Cover us.
Luke xxiii. 31.For if they do so in the green tree,
Lit. wood (cf. Syr. and Greek). what shall be in the dry?

[24]
Luke xxiii. 32.And they brought with Jesus two others of the malefactors,
Or, others, malefactors. to be put to death.

[25]
Luke xxiii. 33a; John xix. 17c.And when they came unto a certain place called The skull, and called in the Hebrew Golgotha, they crucified him there:
Luke xxiii. 33b.they crucified with him these two [26] malefactors, one on his right, and the other on his left.
Mark xv. 28.And the scripture was [27] [Arabic, p. 194] fulfilled, which saith, He was numbered with the transgressors.
Mark xv. 23a.And they gave him to drink wine and myrrh, and vinegar which had been mixed with the myrrh;
Matt. xxvii. 34b; Mark xv. 23b.and he tasted, and would not drink; and he received it not.

[28]
John xix. 23.And the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments, and cast lots for them in four parts, to every party of the soldiers a part; and his tunic was [29] without sewing, from the top woven throughout.
John xix. 24.And they said one to another, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: and the scripture was fulfilled, which saith,
They divided my garments among them,
And cast the lot for my vesture.

[30, 31]
Matt. xxvii. 36.This the soldiers did. And they sat and guarded him there.
John xix. 19.And Pilate wrote on a tablet the cause of his death, and put it on the wood of the cross above his head.
Matt. xxvii. 37. And there was written upon it thus: This is Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the [32] Jews.
John xix. 20.And this tablet
A different word from that in the preceding verse; in each case, the word used in the Peshitta (Cur. and Sin. lacking). read many of the Jews: for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city: and it was written in Hebrew and Greek and Latin. [33]
John xix. 21.And the chief priests said unto Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but, He it is [34] that
The Syriac words, retained in Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary (f. 366a), seem to have been transposed. Vat. ms. omits he, probably meaning but that he said. said, I am the King of the Jews.
John xix. 22.Pilate said unto them, What hath been [35] written hath been written.
In a carelessly written Arabic ms. there is almost no difference between hath been written and I have written, as it is in Ibn-at-Tayyib (loc. cit., f. 366a).
Luke xxiii. 35a; Matt. xxvii. 39.And the people were standing beholding; and they
[36] that passed by were reviling
cf. § 7, 17, note. Borg. ms. has jesting at. him, and shaking
The Arabic text has deriding (cf. § 51, 37). Either with is accidentally omitted, or, more probably, we should correct the spelling to shaking (cf. Syriac versions). their heads, and saying,
Matt. xxvii. 40a; Mark xv. 29.Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days,
Matt. xxvii. 40c.save thyself if thou art the Son [37] of God, and come down from the cross.
Matt. xxvii. 41.And in like manner the chief priests and the [Arabic, p. 195] scribes and the elders and the Pharisees derided him, and laughed one with [38, 39] another, and said,
Matt. xxvii. 42a.The saviour of others cannot save himself.
Luke xxiii. 35c; Matt. xxvii. 42c.If he is the Messiah, the chosen of God, and the King of Israel,
Verse 37 or Mt. let him come down now from the [40] cross, that we may see, and believe in him.
Matt. xxvii. 43.He that relieth on God—let him deliver him [41] now, if he is pleased with him: for he said, I am the Son of God.
Luke xxiii. 36.And the soldiers [42] also scoffed at him in that they came near unto him,
Luke xxiii. 37.and brought him vinegar, and [43] said unto him, If thou art the King of the Jews, save thyself.
Matt. xxvii. 44.And likewise the two robbers
Borg. ms. has boys (an easy clerical error). also that were crucified with him reproached him.

[44]
Luke xxiii. 39.And one of those two malefactors who were crucified with him reviled him, and [45] said, If thou art the Messiah, save thyself, and save us also.
Luke xxiii. 40.But his comrade rebuked him, and said, Dost thou not even fear God, being thyself also in this [46] condemnation?
Luke xxiii. 41.And we with justice, and as we deserved, and according to our deed,
Our deed might be read we have done, and perhaps our translator’s style would justify our writing as for to. have we been rewarded: but this man hath not done anything unlawful. [47]
Luke xxiii. 42.And he said unto Jesus, Remember me, my Lord, when thou comest in thy kingdom. [48]
Luke xxiii. 43.Jesus said unto him, Verily
Borg. ms. has Verily, verily. I say unto thee, To-day shalt thou be with me in Paradise.

[49]
John xix. 25.And there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister,
A single word in Arabic. [50] Mary
Vat. ms. has and Mary. that was related to Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
John xix. 26.And Jesus saw his mother, and that disciple whom he loved standing by; and he said to his mother, [51] Woman, behold, thy son!
John xix. 27.And he said to that disciple, Behold, thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto himself.

[52] [Arabic, p. 196]
Matt. xxvii. 45a; Luke xxiii. 44b.And from the sixth hour
Lit six hours and nine hours respectively. darkness was on all the land unto the ninth [53] hour,
Lit six hours and nine hours respectively. and the sun became dark.
Luke xxiii. 45a; Mark xv. 34.And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and said, Yail, Yaili,
In Vat. ms. the second word is like the first. The syllable Ya doubtless is the Arabic interjection O! why hast thou forsaken me? which
The Borg. ms. omits from which to me. is, My [54] God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
Matt. xxvii. 47.And some of those that stood there, when they heard, said,
Borg. ms. omits when they, and has and said. This man called Elijah.

div3.title: Section LII.
div3.p:
[1]
John xix. 28.And after that, Jesus knew that all things were finished; and that the scripture [2] might be accomplished, he said, I thirst.
John xix. 29a; Matt. xxvii. 48.And there was set a vessel full of vinegar: and in that hour one of them hasted, and took a sponge, and filled it with that [3] vinegar,
Mark xv. 36b.and fastened it on a reed, and brought it near
cf. § 12, 13, note. his mouth to give him a [4] drink.
John xix. 30a.And when Jesus had taken that vinegar, he said, Everything is finished. [5]
Matt. xxvii. 49; Luke xxiii. 34.But the rest said, Let be, that we may
Or, Let us. see whether Elijah cometh to save him. [6, 7]
Luke xxiii. 46a.And Jesus said, My Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and said, My Father, into thy hands I commend
Lit. lay down. my spirit.
John xix. 30b.He said that, and bowed his head, and gave up his spirit.

[8]
Matt. xxvii. 51.And immediately the face of
cf. Syriac versions and Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary. Vat. ms. omits the face of. the door of the temple was rent into two parts from [9] top to bottom;
Matt. xxvii. 52.and the earth was shaken; and the stones were split to pieces; and the [Arabic, p. 197] tombs were opened; and the bodies of many saints which slept, arose and [10] came forth;
Matt. xxvii. 53.and after his resurrection they entered into the holy city and [11] appeared unto many.
Matt. xxvii. 54.And the officer of the footsoldiers, and they that were with him who were guarding Jesus,
This sentence is a good example of word-for-word translation of the Peshitta. when they saw the earthquake, and the things which came [12] to pass, feared greatly, and praised God, and said,
Luke xxiii. 47b; Matt. xxvii. 54b.This man was righteous; and, [13] Truly he was the Son of God.
Luke xxiii. 48.And all the multitudes that were come together to the sight, when they saw what came to pass, returned and smote upon their breasts.

[14]
John xix. 31.And the Jews, because of the Friday, said, Let these bodies not remain on their crosses,
The word is probably plural. because it is the morning of the sabbath (for that sabbath was a great day); and they asked of Pilate that they might break the legs of those that were [15] crucified, and take them down.
John xix. 32.And the soldiers came, and brake the legs of the [16] first, and that other which was crucified with him:
John xix. 33.but when they came to Jesus, [17] they saw that he had died before, so they brake not his legs:
John xix. 34.but one of the soldiers pierced
Lit. ripped. him in his side with a spear, and immediately there came forth blood and [18] water.
John xix. 35.And he that hath seen hath borne witness, and his witness is true: and he [19] knoweth that he hath said the truth, that ye also may believe.
John xix. 36.This he did, that [20] the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith, A bone shall not be broken in him;
John xix. 37.and the scripture also which saith, Let them look upon him whom they pierced.
Lit. ripped.

[21]
Luke xxiii. 49a; Mark xv. 41b.And there were in the distance all the acquaintance of Jesus standing, and the women that came with him from Galilee, those that followed him and ministered. [22]
Matt. xxvii. 56a; Mark xv. 40b.One of them was Mary Magdalene; and Mary the mother of James the little and [23] [Arabic, p. 198] Joses,
Matt. xxvii. 56c; Mark xv. 40c, 41c.and the mother of the sons of Zebedee, and Salome, and many others which came up with him unto Jerusalem;
Luke xxiii. 49b.and they saw that.

[24]
Mark xv. 42.And when the evening of the Friday was come, because of the entering of the [25] sabbath,
Luke xxiii. 50.there came a rich man,
Matt. xxvii. 57. a noble
Borg. ms. omits. of Ramah,
Luke xxiii. 51b. a city of Judah,
Syriac versions. named Joseph, and he was a good man and upright;
John xix. 38b.and he was a
Lit. the. disciple of Jesus, but [26] was concealing himself for fear of the Jews.
Luke xxiii. 51a.And he did not agree with the accusers [27] in their desire and their deeds:
Luke xxiii. 51c.and he was looking for the kingdom of God.
Mark xv. 43b.And this man went boldly, and entered in unto Pilate, and asked of him the body of [28] Jesus.
Mark xv. 44.And Pilate wondered how he had died already: and he called the officer of [29] the footsoldiers, and asked him concerning his death before the time.
Mark xv. 45a.And when [30] he knew, he commanded him to deliver up his body unto Joseph.
Matt. xxvii. 58b; Mark xv. 46a.And Joseph bought for him a winding cloth of pure linen, and took down the body of Jesus, [31] and wound it in it; and they came and took it.
John xix. 38d; John xix. 39.And there came unto him Nicodemus also, who of old came unto Jesus by night; and he brought with him perfume
The preparation used in embalming. [32] of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.
John xix. 40.And they took the body of Jesus, and wound it in the linen and the perfume, as was the custom of the Jews to bury.

[33]
John xix. 41.And there was in the place where Jesus was crucified a garden; and in that garden [34] a new tomb cut out in a rock,
Mark xv. 46. Lit. a stone. wherein was never man yet laid.
John xix. 42.And they left [35] Jesus there because the sabbath had come in, and because the tomb was near.
Matt. xxvii. 60b.And they pushed
On the plural, which is to be found also in Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary, see § 38, 43, note (end). The word chosen might be simply a clerical error for an original Arabic rolled. a great stone, and thrust
Lit. cast (cf. Sinaitic). it against the door of the sepulchre, and [36] went away.
Mark xv. 47a.And Mary Magdalene and Mary that was related to Joses came to [37] [Arabic, p. 199] the sepulchre after them,
Dual. The clause (from came) is found verbatim in Sin. and Cur. at Luke xxiii. 55. Here, after the word Luke of the reference, at the end of leaf 117 of Vat. ms., is a note by a later hand: “Here a leaf is wanting.” This second and last lacuna extends from § 52, 37, to § 53, 4.
Luke xxiii. 55b.and sat opposite the sepulchre,
Matt. xxvii. 61b. and saw the [38] body, how they took it in and laid it there.
Luke xxiii. 56a; Mark xvi. 1b.And they returned, and bought ointment
cf. Sinaitic. and perfume,
The two Arabic words are practically synonymous (cf. Luke xxiii. 56, Pesh.). and prepared
Luke xxiii. 56. it, that they might come and anoint him. [39]
Luke xxiii. 56c.And on the day which was the sabbath day they desisted according to the command.

[40, 41]
Matt. xxvii. 62.And the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered unto Pilate, and said unto him,
Matt. xxvii. 63.Our lord, we remember that that misleader said, while he was alive, After three days [42] I rise.
Matt. xxvii. 64.And now send beforehand and guard the tomb
The ms. omits the tomb. until the third day,
Lit. three days. lest his disciples come and steal him by night, and they will say unto the people that he [43] is risen from the dead: and the last error shall be worse than the first.
Matt. xxvii. 65.He said unto them, And have ye not guards?
The word might be taken as a collective noun, singular. But cf. Peshitta and § 52, 51. go, and take precautions as ye know how. [44]
Matt. xxvii. 66.And they went, and set guards at the tomb, and sealed that stone, with the guards.

[45]
Matt. xxviii. 1a; Luke xxiv. 1b.And in the evening of the sabbath, which is the morning of the first day, and in [46] the dawning
cf. Peshitta. The Arabic word is variously explained. while the darkness yet remained, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary and other women to see the tomb.
Matt. xxviii. 1b; Luke xxiv. 1d.They brought with them the [47] perfume which they had prepared, and said among themselves,
Mark xvi. 3.Who is it that will
[48] remove for us the stone from the door of the tomb? for it was very great.
Mark xvi. 4b; Matt. xxviii. 2a.And when they said thus, there occurred a great earthquake; and an angel came down [49] from heaven, and came and removed the stone from the door.
Luke xxiv. 2; Matt. xxviii. 2b.And they came and found the stone removed from the sepulchre, and the angel sitting upon the [50] stone.
Matt. xxviii. 3.And his appearance was as the lightning, and his raiment white as the [51] snow:
Matt. xxviii. 4.and for fear of him the guards were troubled, and became as dead men. [52]
Luke xxiv. 3.And when he went away, the women entered into the sepulchre; and they found [53] [Arabic, p. 200] not the body of Jesus.
Mark xvi. 5b.And they saw there a young man sitting on the [54] right, arrayed in a white garment; and they were amazed.
The diacritical points of the first letter must be corrected.
Matt. xxviii. 5.And the angel answered and said unto the women, Fear ye not: for I know that ye seek Jesus the [55] Nazarene, who hath been crucified. He is not here; but he is risen, as he said.
Matt. xxviii. 6.Come and see the place where our Lord lay.

div3.title: Section LIII.

p.span:
Section LIII.
The Borg. ms. indicates the beginning of the sections, not by titles, but by “vittas ampliusculas auroque oblinitas” (Ciasca, Introduction). Ciasca indicates in the Corrigenda, opposite p. 210 of the Arabic text, where this section should begin.

div3.p:
[1]
Luke xxiv. 4.And while they marvelled at that, behold, two men standing above them, their [2] raiment shining:
Luke xxiv. 5.and they were seized with fright, and bowed down their face to [3] the earth: and they said unto them, Why seek ye the living one with the dead?
Luke xxiv. 6.He is not here; he is risen: remember what he was speaking unto you while he was in [4] Galilee, and saying,
Luke xxiv. 7.The Son of man is to be delivered up into the hands of sinners, [5] and to be crucified, and on the third day to rise.
Matt. xxviii. 7a.But go in haste, and say to his disciples and to Cephas, He is risen from among the dead; and lo, he goeth before [6] you into Galilee;
Mark xvi. 7b; Matt. xxviii. 7c.and there ye shall see him, where
Possibly the translator’s style would warrant the translation as. he said unto you: lo, I have [7] told you.
Luke xxiv. 8; Matt. xxviii. 8a.And they remembered his sayings; and they departed in haste from the [8] tomb with joy and great fear, and hastened and went;
Mark xvi. 8b.and perplexity and fear [9] encompassed them; and they told no man anything, for they were afraid.
John xx. 2.And Mary hastened, and came to Simon Cephas, and to that other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said unto them, They have taken our Lord from the sepulchre, and I [10] know not where they have laid him.
John xx. 3.And Simon went out, and that other disciple, [11] and came to the sepulchre.
John xx. 4.And they hastened both together: and that disciple [12] outran
Lit. hastened and preceded. Simon, and came first to the sepulchre;
John xx. 5.and he looked down, and saw the [13] linen laid; but he went not in.
John xx. 6.And Simon came after him, and entered into the [14] [Arabic, p. 201] sepulchre, and saw the linen laid;
John xx. 7.and the scarf with which his head was bound was not with the linen, but wrapped and laid aside in a certain place. [15]
John xx. 8.Then entered that disciple which came first to the sepulchre, and saw, and believed. [16]
John xx. 9.And they knew not yet from the scriptures that the Messiah was to rise from among [17] the dead.
John xx. 10.And those two disciples went to their place.

[18]
John xx. 11.But Mary remained
Probably an Arabic copyist’s emendation (addition of alif) for stood. at the tomb weeping: and while she wept, she looked [19] down into the tomb;
John xx. 12.and she saw two angels sitting in white raiment, one of them toward his pillow, and the other toward his feet, where the body of Jesus had been [20] laid.
John xx. 13.And they said unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She said unto them, [21] They have taken my Lord, and I know not where they have left him.
John xx. 14.She said that, and turned behind her, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was [22] Jesus.
John xx. 15.Jesus said unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? And she supposed
cf., § 10, 16. him to be the gardener, and said, My lord, if thou hast taken him, [23] tell me where thou hast laid him, that I may go and take him.
John xx. 16.Jesus said unto her, Mary. She turned, and said unto him in Hebrew, Rabboni; which is, being [24] interpreted, Teacher.
John xx. 17.Jesus said unto her, Touch me not;
cf. § 12, 13. for I have not ascended yet unto my Father: go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.

[25]
Mark xvi. 9.And on the First-day on which he rose, he appeared first unto Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.

[26]
Matt. xxviii. 11b.And some of those guards
The Vat. ms. has a form that is distinctively plural. The Borg. ms. uses, with a plural adjective, the form found in § 52, 43. In the next verse the relation of the mss. is reversed. came to the city, and informed the chief priests of [27] [Arabic, p. 202] all that had happened.
Matt. xxviii. 12.And they assembled with the elders, and took [28] counsel;
Matt. xxviii. 13.and they gave money, not a little, to the guards, and said unto them, Say ye, His disciples came and stole him by night, while we were sleeping.

[29]
Matt. xxviii. 14.And if the judge hear that, we will make a plea with him, and free you of blame. [30]
Matt. xxviii. 15.And they, when they took the money, did according to what they taught them. And this word spread among the Jews unto this day.

[31]
John xx. 18.And then came Mary Magdalene, and announced to the disciples that she had seen our Lord, and that he had said that unto her.

[32]
Matt. xxviii. 8b.And while the first
The word first is less correctly spelled in Borg. ms. women
The Vat. ms. omits women and to inform his disciples. were going in the way to inform
Informis dual and masc. in the ms., while the other verbs and pronouns are plural and feminine. his disciples,
The Vat. ms. omits women and to inform his disciples. [33] Jesus met them, and said unto them, Peace unto you.
Matt. xxviii. 9.And they came and took [34] hold of his feet, and worshipped him.
Matt. xxviii. 10.Then said Jesus unto them, Fear not: but go and say to my brethren that they depart into Galilee, and there they shall see [35] me.
Luke xxiv. 9.And those women returned, and told all that to the eleven, and to the rest of the disciples;
Mark xvi. 10b.and to those that had been with him, for they were saddened and [36] weeping.
Luke xxiv. 10.And those were Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and the rest who were with them: and they were those that told the apostles. [37]
Mark xvi. 11.And they, when they heard them say that he was alive and had appeared unto them, [38] did not believe them:
Luke xxiv. 11a.and these sayings were before their eyes as the sayings of madness. [39] [Arabic, p. 203]
Mark xvi. 12a; Luke xxiv. 13b.And after that, he appeared to two of them, on that day, and while they were going to the village which was named Emmaus, and whose distance [40] from Jerusalem was sixty furlongs.
Lit. mils.
Luke xxiv. 14.And they were talking the one of them with the [41] other of all the things which had happened.
Luke xxiv. 15.And during the time of their talking and [42] inquiring with one another, Jesus came and reached them, and walked with them.
Luke xxiv. 16.But [43] their eyes were veiled that they should not know him.
Luke xxiv. 17.And he said unto them, What are these sayings which ye address the one of you to the other, as ye walk and are [44] sad?
Luke xxiv. 18.One of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered and said unto him, Art thou perchance alone a stranger to Jerusalem, since thou knowest not what was in [45] it in these days? He said unto them, What was?
Luke xxiv. 19.They said unto him, Concerning Jesus, he who was from Nazareth, a man who was a prophet, and powerful in [46] speech and deeds before God and before all the people:
Luke xxiv. 20.and the chief priests and [47] the elders delivered him up to the sentence of
Borg. ms., to judgement and. death, and crucified him.
Luke xxiv. 21.But we supposed that he was the one who was to deliver Israel. And since all
Borg. ms. omits all. these [48] things happened there have passed three days.
Luke xxiv. 22.But certain women of us also [49] informed us that they had come to the sepulchre;
Luke xxiv. 23.and when they found not his body, they came and told us that they had seen there the angels, and they
Masc. Plural. said [50] concerning him that he was alive.
Luke xxiv. 24.And some of us also went to the sepulchre, and [51] found the matter as the women had said: only they saw him not.
Luke xxiv. 25.Then said Jesus [52] unto them, Ye lacking in discernment, and heavy in heart to believe!
Luke xxiv. 26.Was it not in all the sayings of the prophets that the Messiah was to suffer these things, and to [53] [Arabic, p. 204] enter into his Glory?
Luke xxiv. 27.And he began from Moses and from all the prophets, [54] and interpreted to them concerning himself from all the scriptures.
Luke xxiv. 28.And they drew near unto the village, whither they were going: and he was leading them to [55] imagine that he was as if going to a distant region.
Luke xxiv. 29.And they pressed
cf. § 50, 36, note. him, and said unto him, Abide with us: for the day hath declined now to the darkness. And he went [56] in to abide with them.
Luke xxiv. 30.And when he sat with them, he took bread, and blessed, [57] and brake, and gave to them.
Luke xxiv. 31.And straightway their eyes were opened, and they [58] knew him; and he was taken away from them.
Vat. ms. omits this clause.
Luke xxiv. 32.And they said the one to the other, Was not our heart heavy within us, while he was speaking to us in the way, and interpreting to us the scriptures?

[59]
Luke xxiv. 33.And they rose in that hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven [60] gathered, and those that were with them, saying,
Luke xxiv. 34.Truly our Lord is risen, and hath [61] appeared to Simon.
Luke xxiv. 35.And they related what happened in the way, and how they knew him when he brake the bread.
Mark xvi. 13.Neither believed they that also.

div3.title: Section LIV.
div3.p:
[1]
Luke xxiv. 36a; John xx. 19.And while they talked together,
The Arabic word after together looks as if it might be due to a misreading of the Syriac, but it is probably a usage cited by Dozy, Supplément, etc., i., 247. the evening of that day arrived which was the First-day; and the doors were shut where the disciples were, because of the fear of the [2] Jews;
Luke xxiv. 36c.and Jesus came and stood among them, and said unto them, Peace be with you: I am he; fear not.
Luke xxiv. 37.But they were agitated, and became afraid, and supposed that they [3] saw a spirit.
Luke xxiv. 38.Jesus said unto them, Why are ye agitated? and why do thoughts rise [4] [Arabic, p. 205] in
Lit. on (cf. Pesh.). your hearts?
Luke xxiv. 39.See my hands and my feet, that I am he: feel me, and know that a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me having that. [5]
Luke xxiv. 40.And when he had said this, he shewed them his hands and his feet and his side.
Borg. ms. has sides. [6]
Luke xxiv. 41.And they were until this time unbelieving, from their joy and their wonder. He [7] said unto them, Have ye anything here to eat?
Luke xxiv. 42.And they gave him a portion of broiled fish and of honey.
Borg. ms. omits and of honey.
Luke xxiv. 43.And he took it, and ate before them.

[8]
Luke xxiv. 44.And he said unto them, These are the sayings which I spake unto you, while I was with you, that
Vat. ms.,for. everything must be fulfilled, which is written in the law of [9] Moses, and the prophets, and the psalms, concerning me.
Luke xxiv. 45.Then opened he their [10] heart, that they might understand the scriptures; and he said unto them,
Luke xxiv. 46.Thus it is written, and thus it is necessary
Borg. ms. omits it is necessary. that the Messiah suffer, and rise from among the [11] dead on the third day;
Luke xxiv. 47.and that repentance unto the forgiveness of sins be preached [12] in his name among all the peoples; and the beginning shall be from Jerusalem.
Luke xxiv. 48.And [13] ye shall be witnesses of that. And I send unto you the promise of my Father.
Luke xxiv. 49a; John xx. 20b.And [14] when the disciples heard that, they were glad.
John xx. 21.And Jesus said unto them again, [15] Peace be with you: as my Father hath sent me, I also send you.
John xx. 22.And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and said unto them, Receive ye the Holy Spirit: [16]
John xx. 23.and if ye forgive sins to any man, they shall be forgiven him; and if ye retain them against any man, they shall be retained.

[17]
John xx. 24.But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Thama, was not there with the disciples [18] when Jesus came.
John xx. 25.The disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen our Lord. But he said unto them, If I do not see in his hands the places of the nails, and put on them my fingers, and pass my hand over his side, I will not believe.

[19]
John xx. 26.And after eight days, on the next First-day, the disciples were assembled again within, and Thomas with them. And Jesus came, the doors being shut, and stood [20] [Arabic, p. 206] in the midst, and said unto them, Peace be with you.
John xx. 27.And he said to Thomas, Bring hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and bring hither [21] thy hand, and spread it on my side: and be not unbelieving, but believing.
John xx. 28.Thomas [22] answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.
John xx. 29.Jesus said unto him, Now since thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen me, and have believed.

[23]
John xx. 30.And many other signs did Jesus before his disciples, and they are they which [24] are not written in this book:
John xx. 31.but these that
cf. Peshitta. are written also are that ye may believe in Jesus the Messiah, the Son of God; and that when ye have believed, ye may have in his name eternal life.

[25]
John xxi. 1.And after that, Jesus shewed himself again to his disciples at the sea of Tiberias; [26] and he shewed himself unto them thus.
John xxi. 2.And there were together Simon Cephas, and Thomas which was called Twin,
Apparently the Vat. ms. means to translate the word. The Borg. ms. retains Tama, as both mss. did in § 37, 61. and Nathanael who was of Cana of Galilee, [27] and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of the disciples.
John xxi. 3.Simon Cephas said unto them, I go to catch fish. They said unto him, And we also come with thee. And they went forth, and went up into the boat; and in that night they caught nothing. [28]
John xxi. 4.And when the morning arrived, Jesus stood on the shore of the sea: but the disciples [29] knew not that it was Jesus.
John xxi. 5.And Jesus said unto them, Children, have ye anything [30] to eat? They said unto him, No.
John xxi. 6.He said unto them, Cast your net from the right side of the boat, and ye shall find.
So Peshitta. Vat. ms. has a form that might possibly be a corruption of take. And they threw, and they were not able [31] to draw the net for the abundance of the fish that were come
Or, were taken. into it.
John xxi. 7.And that
disciple whom Jesus loved said to Cephas, This is our Lord. And Simon, when he heard that it was our Lord, took his tunic, and girded it on his waist (for he was [32] naked), and cast himself into the sea to come to Jesus.
John xxi. 8.But some others of the disciples came in the boat
Vat. ms. adds unto Jesus. (and they were not far from the land, but about two [33] [Arabic, p. 207] hundred cubits), and drew that net of fish.
John xxi. 9.And when they went up on the [34] land, they saw live coals laid, and fish laid thereon, and bread.
John xxi. 10.And Jesus [35] said unto them, Bring of this fish which ye have now caught.
John xxi. 11.Simon Cephas therefore went up, and dragged the net to the land, full of great fish, a hundred and fifty-three [36] fishes: and with all this weight that net was not rent.
John xxi. 12.And Jesus said unto them, Come and sit down. And no man of the disciples dared to ask him who he was, for they knew that it was our Lord. But he did not appear to them in his own [37, 38] form.
John xxi. 13.And Jesus came, and took bread and fish, and gave unto them.
John xxi. 14.This is the third time that Jesus appeared to his disciples, when he had risen from among the dead.

[39]
John xxi. 15.And when they had breakfasted, Jesus said to Simon Cephas, Simon, son of Jonah, lovest thou me more than these? He said unto him, Yea, my Lord; thou [40] knowest that I love thee.
John xxi. 16.Jesus said unto him, Feed for me my lambs. He said unto him again a second time, Simon, son of Jonah, lovest thou me? He said unto him, Yea, my Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He said unto him, Feed for [41] me my sheep.
Lit. rams.
John xxi. 17.He said unto him again the third time, Simon, son of Jonah, lovest thou me? And it grieved Cephas that he said unto him three times, Lovest thou me? He said unto him, My Lord, thou knowest everything; thou knowest that I [42] love thee.
John xxi. 18.Jesus said unto him, Feed for me my sheep.
Lit. ewes. For the three words cf. Peshitta and Sinaitic. Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast a child, thou didst gird thy waist for thyself, and go whither [Arabic, p. 208] thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch out thy hands, and another shall gird thy waist, and take thee whither thou wouldest not. [43]
John xxi. 19.He said that to him to explain by what death he was to glorify God. And when he [44] had said that, he said unto him, Come after me.
John xxi. 20.And Simon Cephas turned, and saw that disciple whom Jesus loved following him; he which at the supper leaned
cf. § 45, 3, note. on [45] Jesus’ breast, and said, My Lord, who is it that betrayeth thee?
John xxi. 21.When therefore Cephas saw him, he said to Jesus, My Lord, and this man, what shall be in his [46] case?
Lit. of him.
John xxi. 22.Jesus said unto him, If I will that this man remain until I come, what is [47] that to thee? follow thou me.
